title: One failed background poll throws the artist out to the sign-in screen mid-gig and permanently stops the live refresh
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: `api()` converts ANY network failure — and any non-JSON response, so a Netlify 502 or a function cold-start timeout too — into `{ok:false, error:'Connection hiccup — try again'}` (studio.html:725). `load()` treats every non-ok answer as an auth failure and calls `gate(d.error)` (studio.html:732). `gate()` does `clearInterval(timer)` (studio.html:754) and then overwrites `#app` with the sign-in form. The Live tab polls `/api/stage` every 4 seconds (studio.html:2297), so the Studio is exposed to this roughly 1,800 times over a two-hour gig. There is no `online`/`offline` listener and no retry anywhere in the file (grep: 0 hits), so nothing brings it back.
failure_scenario: Perry puts his phone on the amp between songs. It sleeps; the bar's wifi drops him or the phone hands off to cellular. One 4-second poll fails. He picks the phone up to start the next song and the Studio is gone — the screen reads 'Artist Studio / Sign in to run your show.' with an empty email box and an empty Studio-code box. His token is still in localStorage, so a page reload would fix it instantly, but nothing on screen says so; what it says is 'sign in'. This is INVARIANT 15d happening again by a different route: on stage, unable to open his own dashboard. The same shape sits in venue-studio.html:353, less severe because a venue has no 4-second poll.
evidence: Reproduced with the file's own code: I extracted studio.html lines 706-790 verbatim with sed into real_funcs.js and ran them via `new Function` with a fetch that succeeds once then throws `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`. Output — poll #1: `app.innerHTML` = the Studio. poll #2: `app.innerHTML` = `<div || Proved with verbatim copies of api/load/gate/start and a stubbed fetch (scratchpad t/gate.mjs). Case A (fetch rejects, i.e. offline): "GATE SHOWN (poll killed). banner=Sign in to run your show. err='Connection hiccup — try again'" — D was still populated and CODE was still 'mycode', so nothing was a || Traced by line, not inferred: 2297 (setInterval 4000 -> load({quiet:true})) -> 715-726 (catch returns ok:false with a non-'unauthorized' error string) -> 728-733 (`if(!d.ok){ ... gate(d.error); return; }`) -> 754 (`clearInterval(timer)` then innerHTML replacement). There is no retry, backoff
fix_sketch: Only `unauthorized` (and a genuine 401/403) may gate. Give `api()` a distinguishable transport failure — e.g. return `{ok:false, offline:true}` from the catch — and in `load()` branch on it: keep `D` and the rendered screen, show a small 'reconnecting…' chip in the header, and let the existing 4s interval keep trying. Add an `online` listener that calls `load({quiet:true})`. Keep the interval alive across failures; only `gate()` should ever clear it.
alt_titles: One failed background poll throws the artist out to the sign-in screen and permanently stops the live poll
One dropped poll in a bar throws the artist out of the Studio mid-song, and the Studio never recovers on its own

title: `newShowId()` has one-minute granularity, so two 'New show' taps in the same minute give the live show the id of an already-archived show and the whole night's detail is silently discarded
what_happens: `newShowId()` formats `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM` — no seconds, no randomness. Two `newShow` actions inside the same wall-clock minute produce an identical id. The first tap archives the old show and stamps id X on the new one; the second tap archives that brand-new (empty) show under id X, then stamps id X on the show again. The live show now carries the id of a document already in history, so when the night really ends, the guard at _history.mjs:113 fires and the entire evening's `played`/`stats` is thrown away — while the index row is rebuilt with the correct numbers.
failure_scenario: Perry opens Settings before the 9pm set and taps '↺ New show (reset everything)' (studio.html:1542), confirms. The Settings tab does not visibly change (the show state lives on the Live tab), so twenty seconds later he taps it again to be sure. He then plays a three-hour gig — 22 songs, 180 votes, $34 in vote sales. He ends the show. The Money tab row reads '22 songs · 180 votes'. Opening it shows 'What you played — 0' and 'No songs were started from the Studio during this show.' The night is gone. Same collision from two devices (phone + iPad) with no double-tap at all, since the client `WRITING` lock (studio.html:741) is per-tab only.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle3.mjs: `newShowId(2026-09-01T20:37:05Z)` and `newShowId(...T20:37:58Z)` both return `2026-09-01-2037`. Then two `newShow` calls produced `showId after tap1: 2026-09-01-0438  after tap2: 2026-09-01-0438  SAME? true`; after playing four songs and ending: `index row songsPlayed:4, t || Ran the real handlers. `await A('newShow')` -> showId `2026-09-01-0439`; played one song; `await A('newShow')` again -> showId `2026-09-01-0439`, `SAME KEY? true`. Played Bravo:2, Charlie:2, Delta:3 in the second show, ended it. Result: `HISTORY DOC: Alpha:2 | stats.songsPlayed: 1 | topSong Alpha` v || Found by measurement, not reading: a scratch run that called admin newShow twice in quick succession produced 'archived show A gross = undefined' and 'live show B gross = 18' (both sessions counted under one id) — I had expected two distinct shows. Investigating the anomaly led to _lib.mjs:8
fix_sketch: Append entropy: `` `${stamp}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,6)}` `` in `newShowId` (it is already generated outside the CAS at admin.mjs:847, so a retry still reuses one value). Cheap belt-and-braces: in the `newShow` case refuse if `freshId === show.showId`. Fixing finding #1's guard also removes the data loss here, but the colliding id would still merge two shows in history.
alt_titles: newShowId() is minute-granular, so two "New show" taps inside the same UTC minute reuse one history key and (with finding 1) freeze the whole night at the aborted show
showId has minute resolution, so metadata.show is not a unique key for a show — two 'New show' taps inside the same minute merge two sets' money and silently discard the second set's history

title: archiveShow freezes a show's history on first call — an accidental End loses every song played after it, and the list row then contradicts the detail page
what_happens: `status:'ended'` archives the show. The HIST document's CAS callback is `if (d && d.showId) { d.money = money; d.archivedAt = endedAt; return true; }` — on any later archive of the same showId it refreshes ONLY the money and leaves `played`, `requested`, `stats` and `endedAt` at their first-call values. But the INDEX write two blocks below (line 127) unconditionally rewrites the row from the freshly computed `doc`. So the two diverge: the row on the Money tab is recomputed, the show it opens is frozen. Because `status:'live'` does not mint a new showId, the same key is re-archived at the real end of the night. `reconcileShow` only refreshes money, so there is no way back through the UI.
failure_scenario: Perry is four songs into a Friday at The Ugly Duckling. At 9:31pm he means to hit "Reset votes" and hits "End the show", taps through the confirm out of habit. He sees "That's a wrap" appear on his own preview phone, taps "Start the show" ten seconds later, and plays fifteen more songs until 1am. He ends the night properly. Money tab shows one row: "19 songs · 47 votes". He taps it and sees four songs — Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta — and a heading that says "Songs played 4". The other fifteen, and the votes they won, are gone for good; show.log was correct the whole time and was never written anywhere else.
evidence: Ran the real admin/vote/show handlers against test/blobs-fake.mjs. Sequence: 2 songs played, status ended (archive #1), status live, 3 more songs played, status ended (archive #2). Result: `HISTORY doc played: Alpha,Bravo | songsPlayed: 2 | totalVotes: 6` while `index row: {"songsPlayed":5,"totalVot || scratchpad/lifecycle.mjs printed `>>> SONGS LOST FROM HISTORY: 3` (index songsPlayed=5, detail songsPlayed=2). Independently re-verified in scratchpad/lifecycle5.mjs by reading `hist_perry-idyll_<showId>` and `histidx_perry-idyll` directly out of the blob store via `__dump()`, bypassing /api/history
fix_sketch: Give archiveShow a `seal` option. Called from `status:'ended'` it is unsealed and Object.assigns the fresh doc over the old one every time (the show is still in progress). Only newShow — the path that mints a new showId — calls it with seal:true and takes today's early-return branch. Alternatively, stop archiving on End entirely and archive only when the next showId is minted.
alt_titles: Re-archiving keeps the STALE detail doc but refreshes the index row, so a show ended twice loses every song played in between — and the two views contradict each other

title: redeemSession claims the payment before it grants it — if the fan-shard write fails, all three delivery paths are permanently disabled and the money shows as delivered
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: redeemSession writes the claim marker into meta.paid[sid] FIRST (line 23-29), then grants the votes with mutateFan (line 36-45). The grant is awaited with no try/catch and casDoc throws Error('busy') after 40 attempts (_lib.mjs:300). If that throw happens, the session is already marked paid — with granted:9 recorded — but fan.extra was never incremented. Every subsequent call, from any of the three delivery paths, hits the `if (pre.paid[sid]) return {ok:true, already:true}` early-out at line 14 and returns success without granting. INVARIANT 5c's three independent paths all funnel through the one function, which is correct, and that is exactly why one bad ordering disables all three at once.
failure_scenario: 10:40pm, forty phones on the venue wifi are hammering the fan shards. A fan buys the $11 / 18-vote pack. Stripe charges the card. The webhook fires, claims cs_x in meta.paid, then spends ~7.5s losing CAS races on shard f7 and throws 'busy' (or the Netlify function simply hits its 10s wall). The buyer's phone comes back to /vote.html?paid=cs_x, calls /api/confirm, and gets {ok:true, already:true, granted:18}. vote.html:588 clears the pending marker and, because d.already is true and loud is false on the retry path, says nothing at all. The fan has 3 free credits and an $11 charge. Perry opens the Money tab: the row shows a green ✓ and 'unredeemed: 0', so the 'Deliver them now' button never appears. There is no way to recover it from inside the app.
evidence: Ran the real redeemSession against an in-memory Blobs fake whose set() returns {modified:false} for the fan shard key only. Output: redeemSession threw 'busy'; meta.paid['cs_2'] = {kind:'votes',amount:7,granted:9,fan:'fan-abc123'}; fan.extra unchanged at 9. Then, with the store fully healthy again,  || Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-perryidyll-Docs-iOhm--Zenbowls--Mac--Product-Design-Renderings/d728d0ad-d3fd-4657-a10b-d3a9753797d8/scratchpad/probe/p1_pay.mjs, real _pay.mjs against the fake store with fan-shard writes forced to {modified:false}. Output: `grant attempt threw: busy (after 7.7s)
fix_sketch: Make the claim provisional, not final. Write meta.paid[sid] = {...,delivered:false} first (so a concurrent path still can't double-grant), do the mutateFan grant, then flip delivered:true in a second mutateMeta. Change the line 14 early-out to only short-circuit when pre.paid[sid].delivered === true — otherwise fall through and retry the grant, which is safe because the fan write is idempotent-by-target (verify already checks extra >= target). Change revenue.mjs:58 to `redeemed: !!(meta.paid[s.id] && meta.paid[s.id].delivered)` so a stuck payment reappears in `unredeemed` and the artist's existing Deliver button fixes it. Wrap the mutateFan in try/catch so confirm.mjs returns a 5xx the client already retries on.
alt_titles: A payment whose grant half fails is claimed forever: all three delivery paths then report success and grant nothing

title: Deleting a song strands a fan's credits with no recovery path — the un-vote toggle IS gated by existence, which the comment two lines above says it must not be
lenses: Mid-show setlist changes — what the serv
what_happens: INVARIANT 15 and the comment at vote.mjs:17-21 both promise that un-voting is never gated by whether a song is still on offer, "whatever the artist has changed since". The `votable()` gate was correctly moved inside the CAS to the cast branch (line 39). But the EXISTENCE check was left outside it: line 22-23 does `const s0 = show.songs.find(x => x.id === song); if (!s0) return bad('That one isn’t on tonight’s list', 404);` — so the request never reaches the toggle at line 37. `removeSong` (admin.mjs:997, the ✕ button in the Studio's Setlist tab, sitting immediately next to Hide) deletes the song from `show.songs` but does not touch any fan shard. The fan's `v` array still contains the id, `costOf()` still charges for it because a missing id simply isn't in `played` so it costs 1, and `creditsUsed()` still counts it. The credit is spent, the song is gone from `/api/show` so there is no button, and the API now refuses the only operation that could give it back. Hiding (`toggleSong`) does not have this problem — the API still accepts the un-vote there, it is only the UI that lacks a button (that is the documented residual). Deletion is strictly worse: it is unrecoverable by any client.
failure_scenario: Perry is 40 minutes into a bar set. Default `freeCredits` is 3. A fan taps three songs — Wonderwall, Bravo, Charlie — and is now at 0/3. Perry, tidying his list on stage between songs, means to tap **Hide** on Wonderwall and hits the **✕** beside it (`removeSong`). Measured result, from the raw fan shard: `{"v":["wonderwall","bravo","charlie"],"extra":0,...}` is unchanged, `creditsUsed = 3 / total 3`, `/api/show` credits `{remaining:0,total:3,used:3}`, and `POST /api/vote {song:'wonderwall'}` returns `404 "That one isn’t on tonight’s list"`. The fan has one third of their night's votes locked inside a song that no longer exists and cannot release it. Their next tap on anything returns `402 no-credits`, and vote.html:245 responds to exactly that error by toasting "Out of votes — grab more below" and calling `openBuy()` — the app destroys a credit and then opens the Stripe sheet. The only thing that frees it is Perry starting another song (`clearAllFanVotes`), so if he deletes a song during the last number of the night the fan is locked out until the lights come up.
evidence: Executed against the real handlers with the project's blob fake. Two independent checks: (a) through the HTTP layer — `/api/show` returned `{"unlimited":false,"remaining":0,"total":3,"used":3,...}` after `removeSong`, and `vote('perry-fan','wonderwall')` returned `{"status":404,"error":"That one isn || /tmp/msaudit/strand.mjs, real handlers: fan votes charlie (`used 1 / remaining 2`, `charlie visible = true`); artist runs `listSongs` dropping charlie; next `/api/show` gives `charlie in d.songs? false`, `charlie in d.played? false`, `d.songs = [alpha(mine=false), bravo(mine=false)]`, `used 1 / rema
fix_sketch: Two lines in vote.mjs, mirroring the fix already applied to the setlist gate. Replace lines 22-24 with `const s0 = show.songs.find((x) => x.id === song);` / `const offered = !!s0 && votable(show)(s0);` and delete the `if (!s0) return bad(...)` early return. The cast branch at line 39 already refuses `!offered`, so nothing new becomes votable; `costOf(song, show)` takes an id and does not need `s0`. Add the regression case next to FINDING 12 in test/e2e.mjs: vote, `removeSong`, then assert the un-vote returns `{ok:true,voted:false}` and `remaining` goes back up.
alt_titles: A fan's credit is stranded when the artist narrows the set — the un-vote the server supports is not reachable from the page

title: Adding a song mid-gig while a setlist is active says "Added to your setlist" and the room can never vote for it
lenses: Mid-show setlist changes — what the serv
what_happens: `addSong` pushes into `show.songs` (the library) only. `libChanged` then fires `syncActive` → `refreshActive` → `applyList`, which re-projects `show.listSongs` from the setlist DOCUMENT — which does not contain the new id. So with a named set active the new song lands with `inSet:false`, `votable:false`; `show.mjs` filters it out of `pool` so it never reaches the room, and `vote.mjs` answers `404 "That one isn’t on tonight’s list"`. The handler sets `note` only for the plan's featured cap (line 967), so `note` is `null` in the ordinary case. On the client, `saveSongSheet` ends unconditionally with `toast(id?'Saved':'Added to your setlist')` at studio.html:1891 — which also fires *after* the `if(d.note) toast(d.note)` at line 1880, so even the cap warning is overwritten. This is the exact shape of the `askAccept` bug that produced INVARIANT 0be, in a sibling handler, and it is the one handler in this family with neither of the two fixes: `askAccept` joins the song to tonight's set (or refuses), `learnDone` warns explicitly ("In your songs — add it to tonight's set to play it", studio.html:625), `addSong` does neither and its toast actively asserts the opposite.
failure_scenario: Perry is playing the Ugly Duckling with his "Late set" active (12 of his 40 songs). Someone at the bar shouts for Tennessee Whiskey; he knows it, so between numbers he taps + Add a song, types it, taps Save. The sheet closes and the Studio says **"Added to your setlist"**. He tells the table it's on there, go vote for it. It is not in `/api/show`; nobody in the room can find it; anyone who somehow POSTs for it gets "That one isn’t on tonight’s list". The only signal anywhere is a small grey "Not in this set" line on that song's row further down the Setlist tab, which he has no reason to scroll to. Measured: with "Set A" active, `addSong {title:'Golf'}` returned `{ok:true, note:null, songId:'golf'}`, the stage payload showed `golf(inSet=false,votable=false)`, `/api/show` listed only `alpha bravo charlie delta`, and `vote('f5','golf')` returned `{"status":404,"error":"That one isn’t on tonight’s list"}`. At a thousand artists this is the single most common mid-gig action there is.
evidence: Scenario 4b executed end-to-end: setup with a 4-song library, `listNew`/`listSongs(['alpha','bravo','charlie'])`/`listUse`, then `A('addSong',{title:'Golf'})` → response `ok:true, note:null`; `stagePayload` showed `golf(v0,inSet=false,votable=false)`; `/api/show` songs = `alpha:1 bravo:1 charlie:1 d || Probe p3.mjs: with a 2-song set active, `addSong('Encore Tune')` returned `note = null`; the stage row came back `inSet false votable false active true`; the public payload's queue stayed `['Alpha','Bravo']`; and `vote('fanA','encore-tune')` returned 'That one isn't on tonight's list'. `learnDone` b
fix_sketch: Server first, because the Studio is not the only future client. In admin.mjs after the mutation, where `newSongId` is known and `show.listId` is set, add a note: if a set is active and `newSongId` is not in `show.listSongs`, `note = join(note, `Added to your songs — it isn’t in “${show.listName}”, so the room can’t vote for it yet.`)`. Then in studio.html change line 1891 to prefer the server's note over the fixed string, the way `learnDone` already does. If Perry would rather it just work (and mid-gig he almost certainly would), the 0be-consistent alternative is to have `addSong` join the active setlist when one is active — but keep the warning path, because an artist building next week's set from the Setlist tab does not want tonight's set edited under him.
alt_titles: Adding a song mid-gig with a setlist active toasts "Added to your setlist" but the room can never vote for it

title: /api/revenue reads the newest 100 Stripe sessions account-wide and treats untagged ones as belonging to whoever is asking
lenses: Scale & multi-tenancy — does this hold a
what_happens: `stripe.checkout.sessions.list({ limit: 100 })` is called with no `created` window and no pagination, against the single shared `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` that every artist's audience pays into (INVARIANT 0r). `isOurs()` then returns true when `!md.artist` — an untagged session is claimed by whichever artist happens to be looking. The GET response includes each buyer's `customer_details.email`, and the POST sweep calls `redeemSession(aid, s)` on those sessions, writing them into the asking artist's `meta.paid` and granting the votes under their namespace.
failure_scenario: Two failures. (a) Cross-tenant: Sam signs up, opens his Money tab, and sees Perry's pre-multi-tenancy charges — amounts, tip notes and buyer email addresses — listed as his own. He taps "Recover them" (the button INVARIANT 5c requires him to have) and those payments are marked redeemed in Sam's ledger; Perry's own sweep then reports nothing to recover and his real un-delivered payment stays undelivered. (b) At scale: on a Friday with 50 artists gigging, the newest 100 sessions across the whole account cover about ten minutes. Perry ends his set at 1am, opens Money, and the reconcile sweep — the THIRD delivery path that exists precisely because a buyer's browser doesn't always come back — can no longer see his 11pm purchase at all. The fan who paid $3 gets nothing and nobody can find the charge.
evidence: Traced from source; no Stripe call needed to establish it. revenue.mjs:19 is `const r = await stripe.checkout.sessions.list({ limit: 100 });` with `sessions = r.data || []` and no `has_more` loop — contrast `_history.mjs:27-49`, which does page (`for (let page = 0; page < 10; page++)`) and does boun || Both runs are reproducible in scratchpad m/money.mjs and m/legacy.mjs against the real revenue.mjs handler with a shared-account Stripe stand-in. Verbatim from the second run: `GET artist457 sees: [{"id":"cs_legacy_tip","email":"another.buyer@gmail.com","note":"you were amazing tonight","amount":40}
fix_sketch: Mirror `moneyForShow()`: bound by `created` to the artist's own show window and page with `has_more`/`starting_after`. Drop the `!md.artist` clause entirely — legacy untagged sessions should be reported only to `isPlatformOwner(aid)` and labelled `unattributed`, exactly as `_history.mjs:37` already does. Strip `customer_details.email` from the payload unless the session's `md.artist` matches. This is a Connect blocker too: INVARIANT 0r already says don't onboard a second paying artist, and this is a concrete reason why.
alt_titles: /api/revenue reads only the newest 100 Stripe sessions platform-wide — the third payment-delivery path dies at artist #2, and it hands strangers' buyer emails to every artist

title: clearAllFanVotes/carryFans and the show write are both unverified, so an acked-but-lost show write destroys a round while nothing advances
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: INVARIANT 4 states as measured fact that a conditional write can report success without sticking, which is why every fan write goes through casDoc's read-back `verify`. mutateShow (_lib.mjs:350-359) passes no verify at all, and admin.mjs ignores mutateShow's return value entirely (:851 `await mutateShow(...)` — nothing is assigned or inspected). The decision to wipe is taken inside the callback (`resetVotes = true`) and then executed unconditionally afterwards, on a document state nobody confirmed. Compounding it, clearAllFanVotes and carryFans wrap each of the 12 shard writes in `.catch(() => {})` (:392, :415), so a partial wipe — some fans reset, others still holding last round's votes and spent credits — is invisible to everyone. wipeFans (:419-425) is worse still: a bare non-CAS `store().set(key, '{}')` that would clobber a concurrent paid grant, though it is currently dead code and called from nowhere.
failure_scenario: Perry taps "Start top voted" at 21:30. The show document's conditional write is acknowledged but does not stick. /api/admin returns 200 ok:true; clearAllFanVotes runs regardless and erases the entire tally. The room's screens still say the previous song is playing, nothing has moved, and the 11 votes eight phones had placed are gone — with no show.log entry either, so the round is not even recoverable from history. Every phone in the room simultaneously drops to zero votes for no visible reason, on stage, mid-set. The partial-wipe variant is quieter and nastier: eight of twelve shards clear, so a third of the room starts the next round already out of credits while their old votes still count in the tally.
evidence: Probe .../scratchpad/probe/p6_ghost.mjs, real admin.mjs, fake store returning `{modified:true}` for `show_*` without storing (the exact behaviour INVARIANT 4 documents). Output: `votes in the room before Start: 11, nowPlaying = null` → `Studio was told {"status":200,"ok":true}` → `what the store act || Ran the real redeemSession three times for one session with the fake store set to report modified:true for meta_perry-idyll without persisting on the first call only. Output: webhook -> granted 9; return page -> granted 9 (no 'already'); reconcile -> already:true. Final fan.extra = 18 for a 9-vote p
fix_sketch: Two changes, both small. (1) Give mutateShow the same read-back verify the fan writes get — for play/playTop the predicate is `sh.nowPlaying === id && sh.log.length === expectedLen`; casDoc already supports it. (2) Make the destructive step conditional on the mutation result: capture `const r = await mutateShow(...)` and only run clearAllFanVotes/carryFans when `r.ok` and the verify passed. Separately, drop the per-shard `.catch(() => {})` in clearAllFanVotes/carryFans in favour of collecting failures and returning them, so admin.mjs can add a note ("votes didn't fully reset — tap Reset votes") instead of leaving the room in a split state. Delete wipeFans or give it CAS.
alt_titles: mutateMeta is the one money write with no read-back verify — a Blobs write that reports success without sticking double-grants a purchase

title: Any one artist tapping "Sign out all devices" signs out EVERY artist on the platform
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: `revokeAll` increments `a.rev` on the ONE global `artists` registry document. `verifyToken()` rejects any token whose embedded `rev` doesn't equal that single global value. There is no per-artist revision, so the revocation is platform-wide. The identical bug exists in the venue realm (`venueauth.mjs:126` bumps the shared `venues.rev`).
failure_scenario: Sam in Berlin loses his phone on Tuesday afternoon and taps "Sign out all devices" in his Studio settings — exactly what the button is for. At that moment Perry is on stage in Koh Phangan holding a guitar; his Studio's next 4-second poll returns 401 and the whole app drops to the sign-in gate. He now has to type an email, wait for a code from Resend, and read it on the phone he is performing with, mid-set. At 1000 artists this fires whenever anyone anywhere taps that button, so it is not a rare event — it is a nightly one, and it hits whichever artists happen to be on stage.
evidence: Executable probe against the real handlers (scratchpad/probe3.mjs, run with the repo's own blob fake): created two artists, signed both in, confirmed both get 200 from /api/stage. Sam POSTs {action:'revokeAll'} with his own Bearer token -> 200. Both then get 401, and `verifyToken(perryToken)` return || /tmp/rev.mjs, real auth.mjs handler against the blob fake: created three artists, signed tokens for all three at rev 1, had B call revokeAll. Output: `before: C valid true D valid true` / `B revokeAll -> 200 true` / `AFTER : B valid false | C (a different artist, mid-gig) valid false | D valid false
fix_sketch: Move the revision off the shared registry and onto the artist record: sign `${email}|${exp}|${byId[aid].rev}` and check `reg.byId[link.artistId].rev` in verifyToken. `revokeAll` then bumps only `reg.byId[me.aid].rev`. Same change in `_venues.mjs`. Keep the global rev as a separate platform-wide kill switch if one is wanted, checked in addition.
alt_titles: One artist tapping "Sign out every device" signs out every artist on the platform

title: A request title with no ASCII letters or digits (Thai, Japanese, Cyrillic, emoji) accepts into a song with id "" — invisible to the room, and a second one silently merges into it
lenses: Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: slug() strips everything outside [a-z0-9] and then trims leading/trailing dashes, so slug('ทะเลใจ'), slug('日本語の歌'), slug('сердце') and slug('🎉🎂') all return the empty string. askAccept (admin.mjs:580) uses that as the song id with no emptiness check, pushes {id:'', title:'ทะเลใจ', active:true} into show.songs, and sets songId = ''. Line 610 then gates the setlist join on `if (songId && show.listId)` — '' is falsy, so with a setlist active the song never joins tonight's set and never re-projects into show.listSongs. attachSong still stamps the row 'added'. The handler returns ok:true with note:null, so the Studio toasts its default "Added — the room can vote for it now" (studio.html:1660) and the fan's page shows "On the list — go vote for it" (vote.html:399). This is exactly the failure INVARIANT 0be was written to close, reached through a different door. With NO setlist active it is worse in a second way: the song IS in /api/show (id ""), which breaks INVARIANT 0bd — vote.html renders the row, and tapping it POSTs song:'' which vote.mjs rejects at line 11 with 400 'missing fan or song'. And because '' is now a taken id, the NEXT such request hits the `sh.songs.some(x => x.id === sid)` branch, is handed the FIRST fan's song back, and is marked 'added' with songId '' without adding anything at all.
failure_scenario: Koh Phangan, 10pm. Requests are on at 3 votes with the "Late set" setlist active. A Thai regular types ทะเลใจ (Carabao) and pays 3 credits. Perry sees "1 request waiting / ทะเลใจ", taps "+ Add", and gets the green toast "Added — the room can vote for it now". Her phone flips to "On the list — go vote for it". The song is not in /api/show at all — not in her queue, not in her search, not in Perry's votable pool — so nobody can vote for it and playTop will never name it. Ten minutes later her friend requests เพลงอื่น, pays another 3 credits, Perry taps "+ Add" again and gets the same toast; that request resolves to the FIRST song's empty id and nothing is added for him either. Two fans, 6 credits, two "On the list" confirmations, one invisible song. Perry has no way to tell from the Studio that anything went wrong.
evidence: Reproduced end to end through the real handlers (scratchpad/probe1.mjs and probe2.mjs, run with --import ./test/register.mjs). With a setlist active: askAccept -> {ok:true, songId:"", note:null}; setlist members unchanged ["alpha","bravo"]; stage payload shows {id:"",title:"🎉🎂🎉🎊",inSet:false,votable || /tmp/msaudit/ids.mjs, real handlers: adding ['ก็เพราะเธอ','上を向いて歩こう','Привет','Normal Song','愛してる'] produced ids ["", "-8mu", "-nvs", "normal-song", "-80i"]. `/api/show` listed id="" title=ก็เพราะเธอ; voting for it returned 400 `missing fan or song` while the very next song voted fine. Second, indep
fix_sketch: Two changes. (1) In askAccept, derive a fallback id when slug() comes back empty — e.g. `let sid = slug(row.title) || ('req-' + row.id)` — so every accepted request gets a real, unique, votable id. Consider the same guard in addSong (admin.mjs:958) for consistency. (2) Stop using truthiness as the "did we get an id" test: change `if (songId && show.listId)` to `if (songId !== null && show.listId)`, and have askAccept refuse rather than succeed if it somehow still ends with no id — a refusal leaves the fan's credits attached to something the artist can honour or decline, which is the rule 0be already states. A regression test belongs in test/e2e.mjs alongside the existing FINDING 1+4 block: ask for a Thai title, accept, assert the song appears in /api/show and that a vote for it succeeds.
alt_titles: A song title with no ASCII letters or digits gets the id "" and can never be voted for, while sitting in the room's payload

title: Every Stripe purchase returns the fan to Perry's voting page, whichever artist they paid
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: `success_url` and `cancel_url` are hard-coded to `${origin}/vote.html`, with no slug segment and no `?a=`. vote.html:205 derives SLUG from the path — a segment containing a dot is treated as a real file, so `/vote.html` yields SLUG='' — and `publicArtist()` falls back to DEFAULT_ARTIST ('perry-idyll') when no `?a=` is present. The Checkout Session's `metadata.artist` is correct, so confirm.mjs grants the votes to the right artist; only the page the buyer is dropped onto is wrong.
failure_scenario: Sarah's fan taps "More votes", picks the $7 / 9-vote pack and pays. Stripe redirects to https://myset.vip/vote.html?paid=cs_... — Perry Idyll's page. Confetti fires and the toast reads "9 extra votes added — vote away!" while the credit pill above it reads 3/3 and the setlist is a stranger's 66 covers. `history.replaceState` has already stripped the query, and the browser's back button goes to Stripe, so there is no route back to Sarah's page except retyping the URL. The fan concludes the payment went to the wrong band. Cancelling checkout does the same thing with "Payment cancelled". Invisible today because Perry is the only artist; fatal for artist #2.
evidence: Ran the real pay.mjs and confirm.mjs with a stubbed `stripe` module (/tmp/msaudit/hk/pay.mjs). Captured create args: success_url `https://myset.vip/vote.html?paid={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}`, metadata.artist `sarahvaughantribute`. Then: `/api/confirm?session_id=cs_test_1&fan=fanQ` (no `a=`, exactly what  || Ran the real redeemSession + real show.mjs handler against the blob fake (/tmp/paid.mjs). Output: `confirm granted: {"ok":true,"kind":"votes","granted":9,"fan":"fzz9"}` then `page then shows artist: Perry Idyll | venue: The Ugly Duckling | songs: [ 'Perry A' ]` / `their credits on that page: {"remai
fix_sketch: Build the return URL from the artist: `const slug = (await artistById(aid)).slug; success_url = `${origin}/${slug}/vote?paid={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}``, falling back to `/vote.html` only when there is no slug. `/:slug/vote` already routes to vote.html (netlify.toml) and vote.html already reads the slug from the path, so nothing else changes. Add a regression assertion that the success_url contains the paying artist's slug.
alt_titles: Stripe's success_url has no slug, so every non-founding artist's paying fan is returned to Perry's voting page

title: revenue.mjs lists the newest 100 Checkout Sessions of the WHOLE Stripe account with no pagination and no date filter — an artist's entire Money tab can read $0.00 while their money sits in Stripe
what_happens: `stripe.checkout.sessions.list({ limit: 100 })` returns the 100 most recent sessions across the entire Stripe account, newest first. revenue.mjs never reads r.has_more and never passes starting_after or a `created` window. The per-artist filter (isOurs, line 28-33) is applied AFTER that truncation, so an artist's payments are only visible if they happen to fall inside the account-wide newest 100. Everything downstream inherits it: `totals.all` (rendered as 'All payments, all time' at studio.html:1290), `unredeemed` (line 67), and the POST reconcile sweep (line 36-43), which is INVARIANT 5c's third and last delivery path. The sibling function _history.mjs:26-50 does this correctly, with a comment saying 'sessions.list() does NOT paginate on its own and a busy month would silently truncate' — so the project already knows the rule and revenue.mjs is the one place that breaks it.
failure_scenario: At 1000 artists this is certain, but it bites at three. Sam plays Thursday and sells four $7 vote packs. Over the weekend 120 sessions are created platform-wide by other artists on the same shared key. Sam opens his Money tab on Monday: 'All payments, all time  $0.00', 'No payments yet.', and unredeemed 0. If one of his four was the stuck kind from finding 1, the Deliver button is not offered because the payment is not in the list at all. Meanwhile his History tab shows gross $28 for that night, because that screen uses moneyForShow, which pages properly — two screens in the same app disagreeing about whether he was paid. This also reaches Perry alone: at ~100 lifetime sessions his 'all time' total silently becomes 'last 100 sessions' and starts shrinking.
evidence: Ran the real revenue.mjs handler with a stubbed `stripe` module implementing genuine list() semantics (newest-first, honours limit/starting_after/created, reports has_more). Ledger: 4 paid sessions tagged artist perry-idyll worth $28, then 120 later sessions tagged other artists. GET returned status || Read of revenue.mjs:19-22 versus _history.mjs:28-49 in the same repo — the paginating version exists and carries the comment 'sessions.list() does NOT paginate on its own and a busy month would silently truncate'. The filter `s.payment_status === 'paid'` is applied at line 34, after the list call, w
fix_sketch: Give revenue.mjs the same loop moneyForShow already has: page on has_more/starting_after, bound with `created: { gte }` (e.g. last 180 days, or since the artist's signup), and cap the pages. Better still for the 1000-artist case: make meta.paid the primary ledger for the list (it is already per-artist and already read on line 45) and use Stripe only to find sessions meta.paid has never seen — that turns an O(whole platform) scan into an O(this artist) one. Under Connect (finding 3) this becomes a per-connected-account list and the problem disappears, so fixing it in the same change as Connect is reasonable — but the 'all time' label at studio.html:1290 should stop claiming all-time until then.
alt_titles: The reconcile sweep — the third and last delivery path for a payment — reads one unpaginated page of 100 Checkout Sessions, abandoned ones included

title: ANSWER 4 — CRITICAL: a deploy preview today shares the PRODUCTION blob store AND carries the LIVE Stripe key. Perry has already made 44 such deploys.
what_happens: Two independent problems, both confirmed against the live account. (a) DATA: `getStore('myset')` (_lib.mjs:4) is a SITE-scoped store. Netlify's own docs state site-scoped stores are shared across all deploys and that 'Deploy Previews can access production data'. Every deploy preview, every branch deploy and every `netlify deploy` draft reads and WRITES the same `show_perry-idyll`, `f0..f11_perry-idyll`, `artists` documents as myset.vip. (b) MONEY: I read the site's live env config. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY has scopes [builds, functions, runtime] and per-context values for production, deploy-preview, branch-deploy, dev-server — and the masked values for all four end in the SAME four characters, `HAsL`. It is one key. ADMIN_CODE, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and RESEND_API_KEY are the same shape. So a preview URL is a fully armed production console: it can take real card payments, it can be unlocked with the real Studio passcode, and it can send real email. The prior session's instinct was right — that draft deploy was safe only because it happened to be exercised read-only.
failure_scenario: Perry gives a test user a PR preview URL to try the new setlist feature. They open the Studio with the passcode he shares, tap 'Start the show', and add three songs. myset.vip's live show document is now mid-gig with three test songs in it. Separately, a tester taps 'Buy 10 votes' to check the flow — Stripe Checkout opens against the LIVE key, their real card is charged $5, `pay.mjs` writes metadata `{show: <production showId>}`, and the return page's /api/confirm credits the votes into the PRODUCTION fan shard. Perry now has a real charge on a real card in his real Stripe balance for a test, and the reconcile sweep will happily honour it. If the tester instead abandons at the Stripe page, the webhook (configured to point at production) fires against production anyway.
evidence: Netlify Blobs docs: site-scoped `getStore` is 'shared across all deploys… Deploy Previews can access production data'; only `getDeployStore` is deploy-scoped. Live env read via the Netlify API for site 8f5c9f01…: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY values -> dev:'' , branch-deploy:********HAsL, deploy-preview:*******
fix_sketch: CONCRETE SAFE SETUP, in order of what to do first. STEP 1 (5 minutes, do this before any other preview work): `netlify env:set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY <sk_test_…> --context deploy-preview` and again for `branch-deploy` and `dev`. Same for STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (a test-mode signing secret) and ADMIN_CODE (a different passcode). This alone makes a leaked preview URL unable to touch money. Per-context values are confirmed working on Perry's Personal plan — his vars already carry them. STEP 2 (data isolation, ONE line): introduce a plain user-defined env var, `BLOB_STORE`, and change _lib.mjs:4 to `export const store = () => getStore(process.env.BLOB_STORE || 'myset');`. Set it to `myset` for production and `myset-preview` for deploy-preview/branch-deploy/dev. User-defined env vars ARE available at function runtime; do NOT try to use `process.env.CONTEXT` — Netlify's docs are explicit that CONTEXT, DEPLOY_ID, BRANCH and NETLIFY are build-time only and NOT available to functions. Note the failure mode: if BLOB_STORE is ever unset on a preview it falls back to production. That is why step 1 comes first — the Stripe test key is the belt to this brace. STEP 3 (VERIFY, do not trust): add a temporary `/api/whoami` returning `{ deployContext: ctx.deploy.context, store: process.env.BLOB_STORE, stripe: (process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY||'').slice(0,7) }` — the second handler argument `ctx` is the documented v2 Context object with `deploy.context`, `deploy.id`, `site.id`, and it IS available at runtime even though the env var is not. Run `netlify deploy` (draft, 0 credits), curl it, confirm it says deploy-preview / myset-preview / sk_test_, then delete the endpoint. STEP 4 (seed): the preview store starts empty, and `defaultShow()` deliberately returns a blank artist — so create a throwaway test artist through the normal signup flow on the preview. Never copy production data in. STEP 5 (the PR flow Perry asked about): the GitHub integration is already installed and previews are not skipped, so PR previews work the moment there is a PR — open one against main and Netlify posts a `deploy-preview-N--mysetvip.netlify.app` URL. They are FREE (deploy previews and branch deploys cost 0 credits), so this is strictly cheaper than the current double-production-deploy habit. ALTERNATIVE if maximum safety is wanted over minimum effort: create a SECOND Netlify site pointed at the same repo on a `staging` branch. A different site is a different siteID, which is a platform-guaranteed separate blob namespace with no code change and no env var that can be forgotten. It costs 15 credits per staging production deploy, but it cannot possibly touch live data. Given that this app handles real money at live gigs, I would take the second site.

title: The head-count venues buy on is inflatable by plain GETs, and `nets` — INVARIANT 0ae's stated defence against exactly this — is stored but rendered nowhere
lenses: Fan identity & anti-abuse — how a person
what_happens: markPresence (_lib.mjs:540-550) stamps a fan record once per (device, show) whenever /api/show is called with in=1 and a fan id, while status==='live'. Both the fan id and the in=1 flag come from the URL, so a GET loop with a fresh id each time mints one presence-stamped record per request. roomCounts then reports `phones` as the head-count. INVARIANT 0ae says the network hash 'is kept alongside it as the defence against one phone rotating its id' — but I traced every consumer: `ipH` is written at _lib.mjs:546 and read only by roomCounts to compute `nets`; `nets` is returned by stage.mjs:46 and stored in the archive doc (_history.mjs:105), and then it is dropped from the history index row (_history.mjs:125 carries `room` and not `nets`), it is absent from _vstats.mjs (which uses `s.room ?? s.peakVoters`), and grepping all of public/ for 'nets' returns zero hits. studio.html:1066 renders `voters / room` only. So the defence is collected and never shown to a human and never used in any comparison. Nothing anywhere asks 'why are there 500 phones on 1 network'.
failure_scenario: Two versions, and the second is the one that matters at 1000 artists. (a) A griefer runs `for i in $(seq 500); do curl -s "https://myset.vip/api/show?in=1&fan=g$i&a=perry-idyll" >/dev/null; done` during the gig. Perry's Studio says '3 / 500 — Voting · in room' and he spends the set wondering why 497 people are ignoring him; the archived night, which is his record of what that venue was worth, says 500 people. (b) The artist does it to himself. INVARIANT 0aj says the room numbers 'are the single biggest reason a bar signs up' and _vstats.mjs shows a venue `s.room` per night per act. An artist who wants the Friday residency runs 300 GETs at his own gig, and the venue's dashboard — the one thing MySet sells to bars — says he drew 300. There is no cost, no skill, and no signal anywhere that would contradict it, because the one number that would (`nets`) is never displayed. That is a platform-integrity failure, not an artist-level annoyance.
evidence: scratchpad/abuse.mjs: 500 GETs to the real show.mjs handler with in=1 and ids 'ghost0'..'ghost499', zero votes cast. stagePayload then reported `room = 500`; ending the show and reading /api/history returned archived `stats.room = 500` — and note the returned index row contains no `nets` key at all,
fix_sketch: (1) Show `nets` next to `room` everywhere `room` is shown — Studio tile, history detail, and the venue's night row — so '500 phones / 1 network' is visible to the person being lied to. That is a one-line-per-surface change and it makes 0ae's claimed defence real. (2) Raise the bar for what counts as present: stamp on the SECOND poll from an id, or only once the id has been alive for ~30 seconds, so a single fire-and-forget GET is not a person. (3) Cap presence stamps per roomHash per show (again generously — 0ae is right that one network can legitimately be forty people, so pick a number like 150 and clamp rather than reject). (4) Separately: because markPresence writes, /api/show is currently an unauthenticated unbounded WRITE endpoint, which is worth fixing on its own account — see the storage finding.

title: Two in-flight "Start top voted" taps burn two songs and destroy the round — and the Studio's own error message invites the second tap
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: playTop reads the tally OUTSIDE the CAS (admin.mjs:795-799) and there is no idempotency key or server-side lock on the action. Two concurrent requests both capture the same `counts`, both run the mutateShow, and CAS serialises them rather than rejecting the second: the first sets nowPlaying=alpha, the second re-reads, sees alpha as nowPlaying, filters it out of the pool and starts bravo. Both call logPlay with the same stale counts, so show.log records two winners both claiming roundVotes:14, and clearAllFanVotes runs twice. The client's WRITING lock (studio.html:741) is per-browser only, and api() at :722-723 catches a failed fetch and returns `{ok:false, error:'Connection hiccup — try again'}` while releasing the lock in `finally` — but the request is already executing on Netlify. The UI literally tells the artist to do the thing that causes this.
failure_scenario: 22:10, bar wifi. Alpha has 9 votes, Bravo 4, Charlie 1. Perry taps "Start top voted". The fetch stalls and the browser drops it; the Studio toasts "Connection hiccup — try again". He taps again. Both requests are alive server-side. He starts playing Alpha. The room's screens show Alpha jump straight into "already played" AND Bravo as now playing — a song nobody is hearing. Alpha's 9 votes are gone, and any fan who wants it back must now pay the 5-credit replay cost. The archived history for the night records Alpha and Bravo as each winning out of the same 14 votes, double-counting the round. Same result if his phone and his laptop both have the Studio open.
evidence: Probe .../scratchpad/probe/p11_playtop.mjs — real admin.mjs, `await Promise.all([A('playTop'), A('playTop')])`. Output: `two in-flight playTop -> statuses 200 200` / `nowPlaying: bravo` / `played[]: ['alpha']` / `show.log: ['alpha won with 9 of 14', 'bravo won with 4 of 14']` / `votes left in the ro
fix_sketch: Give every song-starting write an idempotency token: the client sends the showId plus the id of the song it currently believes is playing (`expectNow`), and playTop/play abort with 409 inside the CAS callback if `show.nowPlaying !== expectNow`. That makes a duplicate request a no-op rather than a second song, and costs nothing on the happy path. Belt and braces: reject a play/playTop whose `show.nowPlayingAt` is less than ~2 s old. Also change studio.html's api() catch text — after a POST that may have landed, "try again" is the wrong advice; it should reload state first.

title: Changing free credits, unlimited, or replay cost mid-show retroactively re-prices votes already cast and permanently destroys purchased credits at the next New show
lenses: Vote & credit accounting — every path th
what_happens: `me.v` stores only song ids — never the price the fan was charged. `creditsUsed()` recomputes each vote's cost from the LIVE show record every time it is read, so any artist tap that changes `freeCredits`, `unlimited` or `replayCost` silently re-prices votes that were cast under the old settings. Because `unspentPaid()` = `min(extra, freeCredits + extra - creditsUsed)`, an increase in `creditsUsed` eats straight into the fan's PAID balance. `carryFans()` (admin.mjs:1052, on New show) writes exactly that number back, so whatever `unspentPaid` says at that instant is what the fan keeps — the rest is gone with no record anywhere.
failure_scenario: 10:40pm. A fan has bought the $7 nine-vote pack and used one of them on a "play it again" for a song Perry did at 9 (replay cost 5). Their phone reads 7/12. Perry, working the queue on stage, decides replays are too cheap and taps 20 in the Replay-cost row of Settings. That fan's phone instantly reads 0/12 and every Vote button on the page greys out (vote.html:383 disables on `c.remaining < cost`) — they paid $7 four minutes ago. Perry then taps New show for the second set: `unspentPaid` is 0, `carryFans` deletes the record, and all nine purchased votes are gone. The "what should happen to your leftover votes?" sheet never appears either, because vote.html:372 only opens it when `c.paidLeft > 0`. Same shape, two other triggers: dropping free credits from 20 to 3 after a fan cast 5 votes destroys 2 of their 9 paid votes; and turning OFF ∞ Unlimited (which the `freeCredits` handler does implicitly, admin.mjs:923) charges the fan retroactively for votes that were explicitly free when cast — 18 bought, 16 carried.
evidence: T3b (scratchpad/c3.mjs, real handlers): fanB granted 9, replay-votes a played song at cost 5 → `{"remaining":7,"used":5,"paidLeft":9}`. After `admin replayCost n=20` → `{"remaining":0,"used":20,"paidLeft":0}`, `unspentPaid` = 0. T4: fanC granted 9, 5 votes cast with freeCredits=20 (`paidLeft` 9); af
fix_sketch: Stamp the price at spend time and never recompute it. `me.ts[song]` already exists per vote; add `me.c[song] = cost` written in the same branch of vote.mjs:43-45, and make `creditsUsed` sum `me.c[id] ?? costOf(id, show)` so historical votes keep their price and only new votes see the new one. Do the same for the free allowance by stamping `me.freeAt = show.freeCredits` on the round's first spend, or (better, and it fixes finding 1 too) move to the explicit `paidUsed` ledger so a settings change can never reach into the paid balance at all. Whichever way, `unspentPaid` must be non-increasing except when a vote is actually withdrawn.

title: Nothing ever ends a live show but the artist, and a show carried into the next night prices the new room out of the setlist at replayCost
what_happens: `status` is a plain assignment (admin.mjs:916) with no time component, and grep confirms nothing anywhere else ever writes `'ended'` — there is no expiry, no cron, no `endsAt` check against the calendar. If the artist never taps End, `show.played`, `show.log`, `showId` and `startedAt` all carry into the next gig. `costOf` (_lib.mjs:487) then charges `replayCost` (default 5) for every song on last night's `played[]`, against `freeCredits` (default 3). Because status is still 'live', the Studio's Live tab shows only '■ End the show' — there is no 'Start the show' button to make the artist notice the state, and 'New show' is buried on the Settings tab behind a dialog.
failure_scenario: Perry plays the Ugly Duckling on Friday, 25 songs from a 60-song library. He packs the guitar and drives home without tapping End. Saturday, different bar, forty new phones scan the QR. Each fan gets 3 free credits — and 25 of the 60 songs are marked 'played', so voting for any of them costs 5. Nobody can afford one. The room can only vote inside the 35 songs Perry did not play on Friday, and the voting page shows a 'Played' section listing songs this room never heard. Nothing on either phone explains why. MEASURED with a smaller set: after a 6-song Friday, a Saturday fan with the default 3 credits could vote for exactly 2 of 8 songs, and `vote Zulu -> no-credits`.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle7.mjs: after Friday's 6 starts, `played = ['zulu','yankee','xray','whiskey','victor']`, `status live`. A fresh Saturday fan's /api/show payload: `songs still to play (cost 1): ['Sierra/1','Tango/1']`, `already "played" (cost 5): ['Victor/5','Whiskey/5','Xray/5','Yankee/5','Zulu/5
fix_sketch: Two independent guards, both cheap. (1) In `getShow`/`stagePayload`, treat a show as stale when `Date.now() - (show.nowPlayingAt || show.startedAt) > ~8h` and surface it — the Studio's Live tab shows a 'This show has been running since Friday 9pm — start a new one?' strip, and the artist page stops rendering the Live pill. (2) On `status:'live'`, if the stored `startedAt` is on a different calendar day in the artist's own tz, treat the tap as a `newShow` (fresh id, clear `played`/`log`, `carryFans`) rather than a resume. The auto-list logic at admin.mjs:833-845 already reads the calendar on this exact action, so the gig data is in hand.

title: The homepage's first fetch does O(cities x artists) SEQUENTIAL blob reads and will time out into "No gigs listed yet"
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: index.html's boot() begins with `/api/events?places=1`. That handler loops every country, then every city, calling `countUpcoming(ids)` which does `for (const aid of ids.slice(0,40)) await readEvents(aid)` — sequential, one blob read at a time, with no cap on the number of cities. The city feed below it is the same shape: `for (const id of ids)` with an awaited readEvents AND an awaited artistById, and artistById re-reads the whole global registry once per row. venueStats has the identical pattern (sequential, up to MAX_ARTISTS=80). If ?places=1 exceeds the function timeout, index.html's `catch(e){}` leaves PLACES null and renders the empty state: "No gigs listed yet — MySet is brand new."
failure_scenario: MySet reaches a thousand artists spread over 20 cities. Someone opens myset.vip to find live music near them. The picker request fans out to ~800 sequential blob reads; at a realistic 40 ms per strong read that is 32 seconds against a 10-second function timeout. The fetch fails, and the front door of a platform with a thousand working artists tells every visitor there are no gigs anywhere and offers them a signup button. The city feed for a busy city does 81 reads including 40 full pulls of the 209 KB registry — 8.4 MB per page view.
evidence: /tmp/ev.mjs with the read-counting blob fake, 20 cities x 40 artists each, real events.mjs handler: `/api/events?places=1 -> 801 blob GETs, ALL SEQUENTIAL`; `/api/events?country=..&city=.. -> 81 GETs; 'artists' global doc read 40 x`. /tmp/venue.mjs: `venueStats over 40 acts in one city -> 42 blob GE
fix_sketch: Two changes, neither structural. (1) Parallelise: `await Promise.all(ids.map(readEvents))` in countUpcoming, the city-feed loop and venueStats — that alone turns 800 serial round trips into ~20 batched ones. (2) Stop calling artistById per row: read the registry ONCE per request and index it locally (this compounds with the hot-path fix above). Then, for the picker specifically, keep the per-city gig COUNT denormalised inside the cityindex document, written by reindexCities, so ?places=1 becomes a single blob read regardless of how many artists exist.

title: meta_<aid> grows without bound and sits on the Studio's 4-second poll — 1 MB pulled per poll and per button tap
lenses: Scale & multi-tenancy — does this hold a
what_happens: redeemSession appends to `meta.tips` (line 26) and adds a `meta.paid[sessionId]` marker (line 27) for every payment ever taken, and nothing anywhere prunes either — grep for a cap on tips finds only the two display-side slices (stage.mjs:62 `.slice(-15)` and _history.mjs:54 `.slice(0,12)`). admin.mjs never touches meta at all, so "New show" does not reset it. That whole document is read on every stagePayload — which is both the Studio's 4-second poll and every single /api/admin write — to compute a sum, a count and the last 15 rows.
failure_scenario: Perry after two years: 5 gigs a week, ~20 tips a night, so ~5,200 tips and ~5,200 payment markers. I built exactly that record and measured meta_perry-idyll at 975 KB. His Studio, sitting on the Live tab, then pulls 1.03 MB every 4 seconds — 2,700 polls across a 3-hour gig, 2.8 GB of blob egress for one artist's phone in one night — and every tap of Start top voted costs 1.08 MB before it does anything. On a bar's wifi at 10 pm that is the difference between the button responding and the busy overlay (studio.html's 140 ms threshold) flashing on every tap. Then note that redeemSession's mutateMeta is a CAS on that 975 KB doc: read + write + read, for a $3 purchase, during the gig.
evidence: Measured with the counting store against the real handlers, on an account with 200 songs, 40 log entries and 5,200 tips/markers: `meta_perry-idyll 975.1 KB`; `GET /api/stage reads=19 bytesRead=1027 KB`; `POST /api/admin window reads=20 writes=1 bytesRead=1078 KB`. Confirmed independently by code sea
fix_sketch: Keep meta small and hot-path-shaped: store a running `tipTotal` and `tipCount`, keep only the last ~50 tip rows in meta, and roll the rest into the show's own history doc at archiveShow time (which already snapshots the night). For `paid`, either move each marker to its own key (`paid_<aid>_<sessionId>`, which is what redeemSession's replay check actually needs — a single point lookup, not the whole map) or age markers out after 90 days, well past Stripe's session lifetime. Either change makes stagePayload's meta read constant-size forever.

title: ANSWER 1 — `netlify dev` is broken for writes, current CLI has NOT fixed it, and an 18-line dev-only shim makes it work
what_happens: `netlify dev` always starts a local BlobsServer and points functions at localhost — it can never touch production, which is good. But that server's GET handler returns the body and a metadata header and NO etag. `readDoc` (_lib.mjs:270-276) therefore returns `etag: null`, so `casDoc` (_lib.mjs:290) falls back to `onlyIfNew: true`, which the same server correctly refuses on any key that already exists. casDoc then retries 40 times with backoff and throws `busy`. This is NOT fixed in the current CLI: netlify-cli 26.2.0 ships @netlify/blobs 10.7.9 and the repo has 10.7.13 — both have the identical no-etag-on-read `get()`. The practical consequence: locally you get exactly ONE successful write per blob key, then a 7.7-second hang and a crash. WHAT PERRY CAN DO LOCALLY TODAY: `npm test` (4 stages, 64 assertions, real handlers, real Requests, in-memory etag-capable store, no server, seconds) exercises every write path at full fidelity — that IS the local write loop. `netlify dev` is fine for serving public/, for CSS/HTML/JS iteration, and for read paths (/api/show against an empty store returns defaultShow correctly). WHAT HE CANNOT DO: click through the Studio locally. Tap Add song twice and the second tap hangs 7.7s then errors.
failure_scenario: Perry runs `netlify dev`, opens localhost:8888/studio, types a song title, taps Add. It works. He taps Add on the second song. The Studio's busy overlay (raised after 140ms by `act()`) sits there for seven and a half seconds and then the request fails. He concludes the Studio is broken, or that his change broke it, and spends an hour chasing a bug that does not exist in production. I reproduced this exactly: `addSong Alpha: ok=true (35ms)`, then `addSong Bravo` → `Error: busy at casDoc (_lib.mjs:300) at async default (admin.mjs:851)`.
evidence: Read netlify-cli/dist/lib/blobs/blobs.js — `getBlobsContextWithEdgeAccess()` always wires edgeURL+uncachedEdgeURL to a local BlobsServer with primaryRegion 'dev'. Read @netlify/blobs/dist/server.js: put() lines 221-252 honour if-match/if-none-match and return an etag; get() lines 107-152 return `new
fix_sketch: Replace `readDoc` in _lib.mjs with a version that fills the etag from `list({prefix})` ONLY when the store is the local dev server. Gate it on the one thing that identifies that server: `const DEV_BLOBS = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(process.env.NETLIFY_BLOBS_CONTEXT,'base64')).primaryRegion === 'dev'` (wrapped in try/catch, defaulting false). Then inside readDoc, if `r.data && !r.etag && DEV_BLOBS`, look the key up via `store().list({ prefix: key })` and take `.etag`. Two independent safeties mean it cannot violate INVARIANT 1 ('never list() for live data'): the region gate, and the `!r.etag` guard — production reads always carry an etag, so the list() branch is unreachable there. MySet's keys are flat (`show_perry-idyll`, `f0_perry-idyll`) so INVARIANT 2's nested-prefix trap does not apply; I confirmed it works against the real keys. RECOMMENDED DEV LOOP: (1) `npm test` for anything touching server logic — it is the fast, high-fidelity loop and it already exists; (2) `netlify dev` + the shim for clicking through the UI; (3) `netlify deploy` draft (0 credits, real Blobs) for a final smoke test — but see finding 7 before you trust a draft with money or data.

title: A fan can never un-vote a song the artist deleted — vote.mjs's existence check sits one line above the comment explaining why the guard must not be there (INVARIANT 15)
lenses: Vote & credit accounting — every path th
what_happens: vote.mjs:17-21 carries a careful comment saying the on-offer test is deliberately deferred into the cast branch, because un-voting has to keep working after the artist narrows the set — INVARIANT 15's exact promise. But line 22-23 then rejects the whole request with 404 if the song is not in `show.songs` at all, BEFORE `mutateFan` is ever reached. `removeSong` (admin.mjs:997, the one-tap Delete in the song editor, studio.html:1923) and `clearSetlist` (admin.mjs:1019) both drop songs out of `show.songs` without touching any fan's `me.v`. The credit stays counted by `creditsUsed` (which happily prices an id that no longer exists) and the fan has no way to get it back. `show.mjs` doesn't render the song either, so the vote is invisible: the fan sees credits missing with no vote anywhere on the page to explain them.
failure_scenario: Three fans have voted for "Wagon Wheel". Perry, tidying his library between sets, taps Delete on it because he's sick of playing it. Each of those fans is now holding a permanently spent credit: their pill reads 2/3, no song on their page is marked Voted, and tapping anything to try to free the credit does nothing. If free credits are low (0 or 1, which is exactly the setting that drives pack sales) and the credit came from a $3 purchase, it is gone for good: `unspentPaid` keeps counting the deleted song, so tapping New show carries less than the fan bought. Verified: a fan who paid for 3 votes with freeCredits=0 and had one voted song deleted can never recover that credit, gets 404 "That one isn't on tonight's list" on every attempt, and the credit is only released if and when Perry happens to start another song.
evidence: T1 (scratchpad/credits.mjs, real handlers): fanA votes alpha → `{voted:true,remaining:2}`. `admin removeSong song=alpha`. Public payload: `credits {"remaining":2,"used":1}` but `mine flags: (none)` — the vote is invisible. `vote fanA alpha` → `{"status":404,"error":"That one isn’t on tonight’s list"
fix_sketch: Move the existence check inside the mutation, after the toggle-off branch, exactly as the setlist check already is. In vote.mjs: drop the early `if (!s0) return bad(...)`; compute `const offered = !!s0 && votable(show)(s0);` and let the `at >= 0` branch at line 37 run unconditionally so an un-vote always succeeds; only the cast branch (line 39) needs `if (!s0 || !offered) { err = [...]; return false; }`. Add the e2e case next to the existing "narrowing the set must not strand a fan's credit" test: delete the song outright and assert the holder can still toggle it off.

title: A dead artist slug renders a permanently shimmering voting page with no error, and polls every 3 seconds forever
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: vote.html paints a skeleton at line 220 and only ever replaces it inside `if(d.ok)` (line 232). Every other outcome — a thrown fetch, a 404, a 500 — lands in `}catch(e){}` (line 233) or falls off the end of `load()` with nothing rendered and nothing logged. `/api/show?a=<unknown>` returns HTTP 404 `{ok:false,error:'unknown artist'}`, so `ST` stays `null` forever. `signature()` then returns `null` on every tick, and `tick()`'s backoff is `if(sig!==null && sig===LASTSIG) QUIET++; else QUIET=0` (line 642) — a null signature always takes the reset branch, so the phone is pinned at the fastest 3-second interval indefinitely, defeating INVARIANT 9d. Meanwhile `setSlug` deletes the old slug outright (`delete a.bySlug[old]`, auth.mjs:134) with no alias or redirect, and `/:slug/vote` still serves vote.html with HTTP 200, so the dead link *looks* alive.
failure_scenario: Perry has QR stickers on twelve tables pointing at myset.vip/perry-idyll/vote. Two months in he changes his address in Settings to /perryidyll. Netlify still serves vote.html for /perry-idyll/vote with a 200, the page paints its skeleton, `/api/show?a=perry-idyll` 404s, and every fan in the bar sits looking at four grey shimmering rectangles with no message, no artist name and no way to guess what is wrong — while each phone hits the API every 3 seconds. Perry has no signal at all that this is happening; from his Studio the show looks fine and the room simply doesn't vote. At 1000 artists, slug changes are routine and each one silently kills every printed QR that artist ever handed out.
evidence: Ran show.mjs directly against the fake store: `?a=not-a-real-artist -> 404 {"ok":false,"error":"unknown artist"}`. Traced vote.html's `load()` — the only `render()` call is inside `if(d.ok)` at line 232, and the catch at 233 is empty, so no path replaces the skeleton. Confirmed the backoff pin by re
fix_sketch: Two independent fixes, both cheap. Client: give `load()` a failure branch that renders a real card — 'We can't find this artist. Ask them for a fresh link.' for a 404, 'Can't reach MySet — retrying' for a thrown fetch — and let a null `ST` back the poll off like anything else. Server: on `setSlug`, keep the old slug in an `a.aliases` map pointing at the artist id and have `publicArtist()` fall back to it, so printed QR codes never die.

title: revenue.mjs treats any Stripe session without an `artist` tag as belonging to whoever is asking — artist B sees Perry's payments and buyer emails, and can redeem them into their own ledger
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: `isOurs(s)` ends with `return !md.artist || md.artist === aid;`. The `artist` metadata field was only added when multi-tenancy landed, so every session created before that — including the ones from Perry's first real gig on 2026-08-30 — has no `md.artist` and therefore passes `isOurs` for EVERY artist. GET renders them in that artist's Money tab (amount, kind, note, and `customer_details.email`). POST — the "Deliver them now" button — loops `redeemSession(aid, s)` over the same list, which writes `meta.paid[sid]` into artist B's meta, pushes Perry's tips into artist B's tip list, and grants `extra` votes to Perry's fan ids inside artist B's fan shards.
failure_scenario: Bravo Band signs in for the first time and taps Money to see if anything came through. The tab lists Perry's untagged legacy payments — "$3.00 · 3 extra votes · someone@gmail.com", "$10.00 · Tip · 'loved the Landslide cover'" — plus a red box: "2 payments were never delivered. Someone paid and the app didn't hand over what they bought. This gives it to them — safe to tap twice." They tap it, because that is what a decent person does. Perry's old sessions are now marked redeemed in Bravo's meta, Perry's tippers appear in Bravo's tip totals, and a fan id that has never been at a Bravo gig now holds free paid votes on Bravo's next show.
evidence: Replicated the exact predicate from revenue.mjs:28-33 against a legacy-shaped session `{id:'cs_legacy', payment_status:'paid', amount_total:300, metadata:{kind:'votes',votes:'3',fan:'fold'}}` with aid='bravoband': returns true. Cross-checked pay.mjs — it sets `artist: aid` in metadata on both the vo
fix_sketch: Drop the `!md.artist ||` clause and require `md.artist === aid`, then special-case the founding artist explicitly: `md.artist === aid || (aid === DEFAULT_ARTIST && !md.artist)`. One line, and it is the difference between "untagged means legacy Perry" and "untagged means everyone's". While in there: `sessions.list({limit:100})` is a global, unpaginated list — see the note in the scale finding.

title: A second artist's self-set Studio code is stored but never checked — email OTP is their only door, and the Studio tells them otherwise
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: `requireArtist` has two paths. The Bearer path is per-artist. The code path checks `process.env.ADMIN_CODE` and then `getShow(DEFAULT_ARTIST).codeHash` — hard-wired to the founding artist — and returns `{aid: DEFAULT_ARTIST}` either way. But `setCode` (admin.mjs:1002) writes `show.codeHash` into the CALLING artist's show via mutateShow(aid, ...). So artist B's code is stored under show_<B> where nothing ever reads it. The Studio's Settings offers the field to every artist and, on save, toasts "Saved — that's your code from now on" and writes it to localStorage as if it were a working credential; the sign-in gate keeps showing "Unlock with code" as an equal option.
failure_scenario: Bravo Band sets a Studio code in Settings on Tuesday, sees the confirmation, and stops worrying about email. Three weeks later their session token expires (TOKEN_TTL is 30 days) — or Safari evicts the Studio's localStorage, or another artist taps revokeAll (see above). They arrive at the gig, open the Studio, type their code into "Unlock with code", and get "That didn't work — try again." Their only route in is a six-digit email code, which needs RESEND_API_KEY to be working and their inbox to be reachable on bar wifi. If either fails they cannot start a single song — the exact failure INVARIANT 15d was written to prevent, reproduced for everyone who is not Perry.
evidence: /tmp/two.mjs: artist B (Bearer-authenticated) called setCode with 'bravo2026'; `setCode ok: true`, `stored on B's show? codeHash present: true`, `checked against Perry's show only. Perry codeHash: false`. Then a request with `?code=bravo2026` returned `401 unauthorized`. Confirmed by reading _lib.mj
fix_sketch: The code cannot identify an artist on its own (it is a bare string with no namespace), so either (a) make it an email+code pair — the gate already collects the email — and check `getShow(resolvedAid).codeHash`, or (b) until that exists, hide the code field and the "Unlock with code" button for any artist whose aid !== DEFAULT_ARTIST, so nobody is told they have a fallback they don't have. (b) is a ten-minute change and must land before artist #2.

title: Every audience poll reads the one global `artists` document twice — and the second read is pure waste, because nothing ever writes show.artist
lenses: Scale & multi-tenancy — does this hold a
what_happens: publicArtist(req) resolves ?a=<slug> via artistBySlug -> readArtists(), which reads the ENTIRE registry. Then getShow() at _lib.mjs:343 finds show.artist empty and calls artistById(aid) -> readArtists() again. I checked all 21 `case` labels in admin.mjs: there is no action that ever writes show.artist, so for every artist except the founding one (whose doc predates multi-tenancy) that fallback fires on every single request, forever. The registry is one key, so the entire platform's audience read traffic converges on it.
failure_scenario: 1,000 artists. The registry is 310 KB (measured, with realistic slug/name/plan/referral fields). A room of 20 phones on a 3-hour Friday generates 50,400 /api/show polls; each one pulls and JSON.parses 620 KB of a document that is 99.9% other people's names — 31 GB of registry traffic per gig, and 0.70 ms of parse CPU x 2 per request. Multiply by 5,000 concurrent-ish gigs a week and one blob key is serving the whole company's hot path. The first symptom is not an error: it is /api/show getting slower for everyone at once on a Friday night, which reads to Perry as "the app is laggy in bars now".
evidence: Op-counted the real show.mjs handler with a counting blob store. One poll = 16 reads, and the key trace is verbatim: `R artists / R show_perry-idyll / R f0..f11 / R artists / R f3_perry-idyll`. The second `R artists` lands after the shard fan-out, which is exactly where getShow's name fallback runs.
fix_sketch: Three layers, in order of payoff. (1) Kill the second read outright: write show.artist at signup (createArtist already knows the name) and on rename, and keep the registry fallback only as a repair path. (2) Replace the hot-path lookup with a tiny per-slug pointer doc, `slug_<slug>` -> aid, written by createArtist/rename; the fat `artists` doc then only serves admin and sign-in. (3) Memoise readArtists() in module scope for 15-30 s keyed on nothing (it is global) — containers are reused across polls, and the registry's own `rev` field is already the invalidation signal.

title: Starting a second night without "New show" reuses the showId — last week's played list, votes and now-playing carry into the new room, and the archive silently merges two gigs
lenses: Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: `status:'live'` (case 'status', admin.mjs:915-916) sets only the status. `showId`, `played[]`, `nowPlaying`, `show.log` and every fan record are cleared only by `newShow` (admin.mjs:1020-1026). The Studio's Live tab shows a big green "Start the show" whenever status!=='live' (studio.html:1076); "New show (reset everything)" is buried on another tab behind a frightening confirm (studio.html:1542). Because showId is unchanged, `archiveShow` refuses to overwrite the existing detail doc (_history.mjs:112-116, "only refresh the money") while the index row IS overwritten (_history.mjs:127-128) — so the two disagree.
failure_scenario: Tuesday week 1 at The Ugly Duckling: Perry plays Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, ends the show. Next Tuesday at Lazy Dog Bar he taps the big green "Start the show". The first fan through the door sees "● PLAYING NOW — Charlie" with dancing equalizer bars before he has touched the guitar; an "Already played · 5 votes to hear again" list of two songs nobody in this room has heard; only 3 of his 6 songs votable at cost 1; and any returning phone opens on 2/3 credits with a vote already spent on last week's song. When he ends night two, History lists ONE show: "Lazy Dog Bar — 5 songs", and tapping it opens a detail page that says "The Ugly Duckling — Alpha, Bravo, Charlie". Night two is never recorded. The head-count is also wrong: markPresence skips any phone whose `seenShow` already equals this showId, so returning regulars are never counted for night two while still being counted in `roomCounts` — the number a venue signs up for.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/tuesday.mjs, real handlers. After week 1 end → week 2 `status:'live'`: venue 'Lazy Dog Bar', nowPlaying {id:'charlie'}, played ['bravo@5','alpha@5'], fanX still holding ['delta'] at 2/3, only delta/echo/fox at cost 1. After ending week 2: history index row = {venue:'Lazy Dog Bar', songs
fix_sketch: Two parts. (a) Make `status:'live'` mint a fresh showId (and clear played/nowPlaying/log, and run carryFans) whenever the previous show is already 'ended' or startedAt is older than, say, 8 hours — a new night is a new show, and the artist should not have to know that. (b) In `archiveShow`, if the doc already exists but `show.startedAt` differs from `d.startedAt`, write a new archive under a fresh id rather than only refreshing money — and never let the index row and the detail doc describe different venues.

title: Free vote credits are minted per client-chosen fan id, so ballot stuffing is free, unlimited and untraceable
what_happens: `vote.mjs` takes the voter identity straight out of the request body (`cleanFanId(body.fan)`), creates the record on first sight, and grants `show.freeCredits` (default 3) to it. Nothing ties a fan id to a device, an IP, a session or a payment. INVARIANT 9g ("the audience never signs in") is deliberate and right, but there is no compensating control of any kind — no per-IP cap on NEW fan ids, no rate limit, no proof of work.
failure_scenario: A punter who wants to hear Wonderwall opens the browser console at the bar and pastes a five-line loop: 100 iterations of `fetch('/api/vote?a=perryidyll',{method:'POST',body:JSON.stringify({fan:'x'+i,song:'wonderwall'})})`. In under ten seconds Wonderwall has 100 votes; the real room has maybe 40 people who have cast maybe 60 votes between them. Perry taps "Start top voted" and plays Wonderwall. He now plays whatever that one person wants, all night, and the honest room's votes never win again. The same trick removes any reason to buy a $3 vote pack, which is the revenue model — and at 1000 artists the trick is public knowledge the week after the first person notices.
evidence: scratchpad/probe1.mjs, real vote.mjs handler: 50 fresh fan ids each cast one vote for the same song. Output: `RESULT 1: votes cast from 50 fresh anonymous fan ids = 50 | server tally = 50`. Every one was accepted; each of those ids still had 2 free credits left. No 429, no 402, no throttle.
fix_sketch: Keep anonymity, but stop making identity free. Bind the free grant to the hashed IP that already exists: store `ipH` on the fan record at creation (markPresence already computes it) and refuse to mint a NEW free-credit record when that `ipH` already backs more than N records this show — N around 8 covers a family sharing a hotspot without covering a script. Paid votes and unlimited fans bypass the cap. Surface the refusal as "too many devices on this network" rather than an error, per INVARIANT 16.

title: Bought vote packs never deplete — `extra` is a permanent per-round allowance, so one $3 purchase buys unlimited voting for the whole night and every night after
