lenses: Vote & credit accounting — every path th
what_happens: A fan's allowance is computed fresh on every read as `total = show.freeCredits + me.extra`, and spending is measured only by `creditsUsed(me, show)` = the cost of the song ids currently sitting in `me.v` plus `me.spent`. `clearAllFanVotes()` empties `me.v` and zeroes `me.spent` every time a song starts, but it never touches `me.extra`. Nothing anywhere decrements `me.extra` except `gift.mjs`. So the moment the next song starts, `creditsUsed` is 0 again and the fan's balance is back to the full `freeCredits + extra` — the purchased votes are restored in full, every round, forever. `unspentPaid()` then reports the entire `extra` as still unspent, so `carryFans()` carries the whole pack into the next show, and the one after that. Nothing in the store records how many paid credits a fan has actually consumed.
failure_scenario: Perry sets free credits to 1 (a realistic setting for a busy bar — you want people to buy). A fan buys the $3 small pack, advertised in the sheet as "$3 / 3 votes" and confirmed by the toast "3 extra votes added". Round 1 they cast 4 votes and the header pill reads 0/4. Perry starts the next song. The pill snaps back to 4/4 and they cast 4 more. Over a 25-song gig that one $3 purchase casts 100 votes. They never buy a second pack, because they never run out — and neither does anyone else in the room. Then the pack follows them: `unspentPaid` still returns 3, `carryFans` writes `extra: 3`, and at Perry's gig three months later that phone still starts every round with 4 votes.
evidence: T11 (scratchpad/c4.mjs, real handlers): fanX granted 3 extra, freeCredits=1. Five rounds, each ending with `admin play`. Every round: `cast 4 votes | credits {"remaining":0,"total":4,"used":4,"extra":3,"paidLeft":0}`. Total votes cast on a 3-vote purchase: 20. Final record `{"v":[],"extra":3,...}` a
fix_sketch: Give paid credits a ledger instead of deriving them. Add `me.paidUsed` (never reset by `clearAllFanVotes`): in vote.mjs and `createRequest`, after the free allowance is exhausted, increment `me.paidUsed` by the paid portion of the cost and decrement it on an un-vote/refund. `unspentPaid` becomes `max(0, extra - paidUsed)`, `total` becomes `freeCredits + extra - paidUsed`. `clearAllFanVotes` keeps zeroing `v`/`spent` (free credits should refresh) but must leave `paidUsed` alone; `carryFans` writes `extra: extra - paidUsed, paidUsed: 0`. Add a regression test asserting that a fan granted 3 extra with freeCredits=1 can cast at most 3 + (1 per round) across N rounds.

title: Accepting one paid song request while the setlist has fallen back collapses the room's voting page from the whole library to that single song
what_happens: When a chosen setlist resolves to nothing, `playable()` deliberately falls back to the whole library and reports `fellBack:true` (INVARIANT 0aq). `askAccept` then pushes the accepted song id into that same empty list (admin.mjs:612-616) and calls `applyList`. `show.listSongs` becomes a one-element array, so `narrowed.length` at _lib.mjs:455 is now 1 — non-zero — and the fallback switches OFF. Every other song in the library instantly stops being votable, and `listFellBack` flips to false so the Studio's warnstrip disappears at the same moment. The fix for INVARIANT 0be (make an accepted request votable) becomes the mechanism that makes it the ONLY votable thing.
failure_scenario: Perry taps '+ New setlist', names it 'Late set', and the Studio's own flow (studio.html:479-482) creates it and toasts 'Now put some songs in it' — then he taps 'Use tonight' before filling it, or fills it and later hides its songs. The safety net does its job: the warnstrip shows and the room sees all 10 (in production, all 66) of his songs. Three fans are holding votes. At 10:40pm a fan pays 3 credits to request 'Freebird'. Perry taps Accept. The Studio says 'Added to "Late set" too, so the room can vote for it.' — and every phone in the bar, on its next 6-second poll, refreshes to a voting page containing exactly one song: Freebird. The three existing votes still exist server-side but their songs have vanished from the payload, so nobody can see or un-vote them. The warnstrip that would have explained it is gone.
evidence: Probe p5.mjs, real handlers + in-memory blobs. Before accept: `listFellBack = true, room sees 10 songs`. After accept: `listFellBack = false`, `room now sees: [ 'Freebird' ]`. Second, independent check by hand against _lib.mjs:447-457: with `listId` set and `listSongs = ['freebird']`, `live` = 11 ac
fix_sketch: `askAccept` must not silently convert a fallback state into a one-song set. Read `playable(show).fellBack` before the mutation; if it is true, either (a) refuse the join and leave the list empty so the fallback keeps holding — the song is votable anyway, because the room is seeing the whole library — or (b) seed the list with the currently-playable set plus the accepted song. Option (a) is one line and matches 0aq's intent. Whichever is chosen, `applyList` should assert that the room's playable count never shrinks as a side effect of accepting a request.

title: After a write whose response is lost, the Studio tells the artist to "try again" — and retrying playTop starts the wrong song and has already destroyed the tally
lenses: public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: act() cannot tell "the write never happened" from "the write happened and the answer was lost". Both surface as `toast('Connection hiccup — try again')` (744-745), D is left untouched (so the screen still shows the pre-write state), and the WRITING lock is released. playTop is not idempotent: it starts a song, pushes the previous one into played[], and then clearAllFanVotes() zeroes every fan's `v` and `spent` across all 12 shards. A second playTop therefore ranks a pool in which every song has 0 votes, so rankSongs falls through to first-voted (all absent) and then to title order.
failure_scenario: Wonderwall has 3 votes, Zombie 2, Angie and Creep 0. Perry taps "Start top voted". The server starts Wonderwall and clears the room's votes; the response is lost on the bar's wifi. His screen still says nothing is playing and toasts "Connection hiccup — try again". He does exactly that. The server now moves Wonderwall into played[] and picks from a tally that is already all zeros — so it starts ANGIE, alphabetically first, with 0 votes. Every phone in the room updates to "Now playing: Angie" while he is four bars into Wonderwall; Zombie's two voters lost their votes for nothing; and show.log records a play of Angie that never happened, which is unrecoverable per INVARIANT 17b.
evidence: scratchpad t/retap.mjs, against the real admin.mjs handler. Output: `before: Wonderwall:3 Zombie:2 Angie:0 Creep:0` → `tap 1 -> server started: Wonderwall` → `tally after the start: Angie:0 Creep:0 Wonderwall:0 Zombie:0` → `tap 2 -> server started: Angie`, `played[]: ['wonderwall']`.
fix_sketch: Two halves. (1) Client: on a transport-level failure of a state-changing action (as opposed to a server-returned error), do not say "try again" — say "Couldn't tell if that went through — checking…", then force a load() and re-render before re-enabling the button. (2) Server: give play/playTop an idempotency key. The client generates a uuid per tap and sends it; admin.mjs records the last key in the show doc inside the same CAS and returns the existing stagePayload unchanged if the key repeats. That makes the retry safe rather than merely discouraged.

title: Nothing in the code stops a second artist's audience from paying — their room's Buy and Tip buttons work today and the money lands in Perry's Stripe balance with no payable ledger
what_happens: INVARIANT 0r says 'Do not onboard a second paying artist before Connect', but it is a note in a document, not a check in the code. show.mjs:97 sets `paymentsEnabled: !!process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` — a global flag, identical for every artist. pay.mjs resolves the artist with publicArtist(?a=slug) and then creates a Checkout Session against the one platform key with no ownership test. isPlatformOwner exists (_plan.mjs:65) but is used only to gate promo-code minting (admin.mjs:70), never money. PLANS.free.cut = 0.10 is displayed in the Studio (studio.html:1441) as '10% cut on money taken' — a commitment shown to an artist about a cut that is not taken from a payment that is not theirs.
failure_scenario: Perry hands the app to his first test user, Sam. Sam signs up, gets myset.vip/sam-jones, prints the QR, plays Friday. Sam's audience sees identical 'More votes — From $3' and 'Tip Sam' buttons, because show.mjs told their phones paymentsEnabled:true. Eleven people buy packs and two tip. $94 lands in Perry's Stripe balance. Nothing in MySet records that Perry owes Sam $84.60 — meta_sam-jones.paid is a grant ledger (what the fans received), not a payable ledger, and Sam's Money tab may show $0 anyway (finding 2). Sam asks where his money is on Saturday morning. This is the failure the whole test-user handoff walks into, and it needs no bug to trigger — it is the default behaviour.
evidence: Ran createArtist({email:'sam@example.com', name:'Sam Jones', slug:'sam-jones'}) then the real show.mjs and pay.mjs handlers. /api/show?a=sam-jones returned paymentsEnabled = true with the full pack list. POST /api/pay?a=sam-jones reached stripe.checkout.sessions.create — my stub throws there, so the
fix_sketch: Ship a one-line interlock TODAY, before the test users, and independently of Connect: in pay.mjs after resolving aid, `if (!isPlatformOwner(aid)) return bad('payments-not-configured', 503)`, and in show.mjs:97 make it `paymentsEnabled: !!key && isPlatformOwner(aid)`. vote.html:518/534 already render the graceful 'Card payments aren't on tonight' copy for that state, so the room degrades correctly with no UI work. Replace both tests with `artist.connect.chargesEnabled` when Connect lands.

title: A 10-second countdown cannot be delivered honestly: the poll backs off to 12s and stops entirely on a backgrounded phone
what_happens: Three independent blockers. (1) There is no scheduled round end to count down to — a round ends only when the artist taps play/playTop (admin.mjs:882/896); nothing in the show document holds a future time. (2) vote.html:635 `const wait = QUIET<5 ? 3000 : QUIET<12 ? 6000 : 12000` — a quiet room, which is precisely the state just before the artist picks, sits at the 12-second interval, so a 10-second countdown pushed via /api/show arrives 0-12s late and can expire entirely between two polls. (3) vote.html:640 `if(document.hidden){ schedule(); return; }` — a screen-off or backgrounded phone does not fetch at all, so most of the room never sees the countdown.
failure_scenario: Perry taps 'closing votes' at 10:52pm. Fan A's phone polled 400ms ago and is in the 12s tier: her screen shows nothing until 10:52:12, by which time the window has closed — her Vote buttons simply go dead with no explanation. Fan B, phone in his pocket since the last song, sees nothing at all; he pulls it out at 10:53 and his votes have vanished and reset with no account of why. Fan C, actively tapping, is in the 3s tier and sees '7 seconds left' when the artist and the poster both promised ten. Three people at the same table, three different truths. Worse variant: Perry gets talking to someone and starts the song 40 seconds after the countdown hit zero — the room sits locked out for 40 seconds with a dead voting page mid-gig, which reads as the app having crashed.
evidence: Read the polling block at public/vote.html:626-655 in full. `signature()` (vote.html:627-632) includes windowOpen, so QUIET only resets AFTER the change is observed — the backoff cannot pre-empt itself. `tick()` returns before `load()` when document.hidden. Confirmed no scheduled-end field exists: g
fix_sketch: Do not build it. If a lock is wanted, make the ARTIST's tap the event rather than a predicted deadline (next finding) — 'late' on a persistent state is harmless; 'late' on a 10-second countdown is fatal. Fixing the poll to make a countdown work would mean reintroducing a fast fixed interval, which violates INVARIANT 9d and re-opens the Netlify cost hole from 2026-08-31.

title: Paid credits are never consumed — `extra` refreshes in full at every song start, so a $3 purchase buys +10 votes per round for the whole night
what_happens: `creditsUsed(fan, show)` sums only the CURRENT round's votes plus `fan.spent`. `clearAllFanVotes()` runs on every `play`/`playTop` and resets `v`, `ts` and `spent` to empty — but never touches `fan.extra`. `_pay.mjs:42` only ever increments `extra`; nothing decrements it. So the vote guard at `vote.mjs:41-43` recomputes `total = show.freeCredits + me.extra` against a used-count of zero at the start of every round. Paid credits are not a consumable balance, they are a permanent per-round capacity boost that lasts until the show ends. `unspentPaid()` at `_lib.mjs:398` then only carries forward what was unspent in the FINAL round, so the end-of-night maths quietly disagrees with the in-show maths.
failure_scenario: A fan at Perry's gig buys the 10-vote pack for $3 at 9pm. Round 1: the server accepts 13 vote-casts from him. Perry starts a song. Round 2: the server accepts 13 again. Round 3: 13 again. Over a 20-song set he casts roughly 200 votes against every other person's 60, having paid once. Meanwhile the customer-facing wording in MYSET.md:139 ("if the show ends with votes they paid for, they choose: keep for next time, or let the artist keep it as a tip") describes a balance that depletes, so the end-of-night sheet offers him a 'leftover' of 1 after he has effectively spent 200 — the two models disagree in front of a paying customer. At 1000 artists this is the single most exploitable thing in the app: the cheapest way to own a room is to pay $3, and every artist's queue is dominated by whoever bought first.
evidence: Measured twice, two different methods, in-process against test/blobs-fake.mjs. (1) Via /api/show: fan with extra:10 → round1 `{remaining:13,total:13,used:0}` → spent down to `remaining:1` → after one `play` → `{remaining:13,used:0}` → after another `play` → `{remaining:13}`. (2) Ignoring the API's o
fix_sketch: Decide which model is intended and make one of them true everywhere. Simplest: make `extra` a real balance — decrement it inside the same `mutateFan` mutation in vote.mjs when a cast exceeds `show.freeCredits`, and refund it on the un-vote branch. Then `clearAllFanVotes` needs no change and `unspentPaid` becomes just `fan.extra`. Alternative (if per-round-forever was deliberate): say so in INVARIANTS.md, fix the end-of-night 'leftover' wording, and price the packs accordingly — but note that then a single $3 purchase permanently outvotes the room. Add a regression test asserting the accepted-cast count across three consecutive rounds.

title: No rate limit and `access-control-allow-origin: *` on /api/vote — one script anywhere on the internet sets the room's queue and inflates the venue head-count
what_happens: `/api/vote` requires only `{fan, song}` in the body and `?a=<slug>` in the query. `cleanFanId` (`_lib.mjs:638`) strips characters but validates nothing, so any string is a new fan with a fresh `show.freeCredits`. There is no rate limit anywhere in `netlify/functions/` (grepped), no origin or referer check, and `json()` sets `access-control-allow-origin: '*'` so any web page can drive it cross-origin. The artist slug is a public guessable URL. Every fabricated fan id also becomes a permanent record in one of the 12 shards that `readFans` re-reads on EVERY `/api/show` poll from every phone in the room, and it counts toward `roomCounts().phones`, which is the head-count shown to the artist and — per INVARIANT 0aj — sold to the venue as the main reason a bar signs up.
failure_scenario: Perry is on stage at 10pm. Someone who is not in the bar (a rival act, a bored teenager, a competitor at 1000-artist scale) runs a 20-line loop against myset.vip/perryidyll. Measured against a real room of 40: 2000 scripted votes put 'Bravo' at the top of the queue at 2000 votes against the room's 40, so every phone in the bar now shows a song nobody there chose; the fan shards grow from 4,602 to 153,492 bytes, which all 40 phones then re-read on every poll for the rest of the night (INVARIANT 9d's cost problem, multiplied); and the Studio's head-count reads 2040 instead of 40, which is the number that later lands in `_history.mjs`'s archive and in the venue's stats page. Perry's only recourse on stage is to stop using the queue.
evidence: Measured in-process: 40 real fans then 2000 scripted ones. Output: `40 real fans : shard bytes 4602 | alpha 40 votes` then `+2000 remote bots : shard bytes 153492 | bravo 2000 votes`, `room queue: Bravo:2000 Alpha:40 Charlie:0`, `Studio: room = 2040`. Grep for rate/throttle across netlify/functions/
fix_sketch: Netlify supports code-based per-IP rate limiting in the function's exported `config` on ALL plans (2 rules on Free/Personal): `export const config = { path: '/api/vote', rateLimit: { windowLimit: 900, windowSize: 60, aggregateBy: ['ip','domain'] } }`. Sized from measurement: a 100-person room's worst legitimate burst (everyone re-voting the instant a song ends) is ~400/min from the venue IP, so 900 leaves 2x headroom and still caps a script. Verify on a DRAFT deploy that `config.path` resolves correctly through the existing `/api/*` redirect. Do NOT rate-limit /api/show — 40 phones polling at 6s is 400 req/min from one venue IP. Optionally also drop `access-control-allow-origin: '*'` from `json()` for the write endpoints (vote/request), keeping it for img/qr.

title: /api/gift is an unauthenticated, unbounded write into any artist's fan shards — and those shards are read whole on every poll and every Studio tap
what_happens: `gift.mjs` calls `mutateFan(aid, fan, me => { me.decided = show.showId; return true; })` with no auth, no cost, no rate limit and — unlike `markPresence` — no `status === 'live'` gate. Every distinct `fan` string (cleanFanId allows 40 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]) creates a new record in one of the 12 shards. `/api/show` calls `readFans()` which reads ALL 12 shards in full on every single poll from every phone in the room, and `stagePayload()` does the same on every /api/admin write. `/api/show?in=1&fan=` gives a second, head-count-inflating version of the same primitive while a show is live.
failure_scenario: A rival act (or a bored punter) runs `for i in $(seq 1 200000); do curl -s -XPOST https://myset.vip/api/gift?a=perryidyll -d "{\"fan\":\"g$i\",\"choice\":\"keep\"}"; done` on Thursday afternoon while Perry isn't even gigging. Friday 9pm the room scans the QR: every phone's 3-second poll now transfers ~20MB of fan shards out of Blobs, and every tap Perry makes in the Studio does the same. The page times out or crawls, the queue stops moving, and the only recovery — "New show", which is what `carryFans()` prunes on — resets `played[]` and `show.log` and wipes the set in progress. Using the `?in=1` variant instead also makes the Studio report a room of 200,000 phones and writes that number into the archived show history.
evidence: Two independent probes. (1) scratchpad/probe8.mjs: with NO show ever started (status 'pre'), 500 anonymous POSTs to /api/gift produced 500 fan records — output `gift with no show running -> 200 {ok:true,...}` and `fan records created by 500 anonymous POST /api/gift: 500`. (2) scratchpad/probe1.mjs:
fix_sketch: Three parts. (a) `gift.mjs` must abort (`return false` from the mutate callback) when the fan record does not already exist and has nothing to decide — a gift decision is only meaningful for a fan who bought something. (b) `mutateFan` should take a `createIfMissing` flag so only `vote`/`redeemSession` may mint a record. (c) Cap the number of records per shard and reject beyond it, and add a per-IP token bucket in front of the write endpoints (`clientIp()` already exists and is already hashed for the head-count).

title: Deleting a song from the library strands any vote held on it, blanks Now Playing mid-song, and leaves a ghost id in `played[]` that re-prices a re-added song at replay cost
what_happens: `case 'removeSong'` filters the song out of `show.songs` and does nothing else. `show.nowPlaying` is not cleared and `show.played` is not pruned; `normShow` prunes `listSongs` against the library (_lib.mjs:322) but never `played` or `nowPlaying`. Three consequences: (1) `vote.mjs:22-23` rejects with 404 BEFORE the un-vote branch, so a fan holding a vote on a deleted song can never toggle it off — the exact shape of the bug INVARIANT 15 was written about ('Un-voting is never gated by whether the song is still on offer'), reached through `removeSong` instead of through narrowing the set; (2) if the deleted song was `nowPlaying`, `show.mjs:55` finds nothing and the room's Now Playing hero goes blank while he is still singing it; (3) the ghost id stays in `played[]` forever, and because `addSong` de-dupes its `slug()` id only against `show.songs`, re-adding the same title yields the same id — which is already in `played[]`, so it arrives priced at 5 replay credits and filed under 'Already played' instead of in the queue.
failure_scenario: 10:20pm. Perry is playing 'Wonderwall'. In the Setlist tab the red ✕ (Remove) sits immediately beside 'Hide' on the same row (studio.html:1153-1155); he means to hide it and taps ✕. Instantly: every phone in the room loses the Now Playing card (it renders null) while he is mid-chorus; two fans who had spent a credit on 'Wonderwall' see their balance still reading 1 used with no row anywhere on the page to tap, and the API answers 'That one isn't on tonight's list' if they do; and when he re-adds 'Wonderwall' after the song ends it lands in the 'Already played — 5 votes to hear again' section rather than the queue. If a fan had bought a $3 pack of 10 votes and spent 5 of them, and Perry taps 'New show' before starting another song, `carryFans`/`unspentPaid` (_lib.mjs:398-417) carries only 6 — four paid credits are destroyed on songs that no longer exist.
evidence: Probe p2.mjs: after `removeSong alpha`, fanA still shows `used 2 remaining 1`, the queue contains no Alpha row, and `vote('fanA','alpha')` returns `404 That one isn't on tonight's list`. Same probe, part C: after removing the playing song, `stage.show.nowPlaying = bravo` but `library = ['charlie']`
fix_sketch: Three small changes at admin.mjs:997: clear `show.nowPlaying` (and `nowPlayingAt`) if it is the removed id, and drop the id from `show.played`. Add the `played` prune to `normShow` alongside the existing `listSongs` prune so historical documents heal on read. Separately, `vote.mjs:22-23` should let the un-vote branch run for an id the fan actually holds even when the song no longer exists — move the `!s0` rejection inside the cast branch, next to the existing `if (!offered)` check at vote.mjs:39, which is where the setlist guard was already moved for exactly this reason.

title: No fetch has a timeout, so a stalled request wedges the whole Studio behind a full-screen overlay that cannot be dismissed
lenses: public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: There is no AbortController, no AbortSignal.timeout, no setTimeout race anywhere in studio.html (grep for AbortController|signal:|timeout returns nothing). api() awaits fetch unbounded. busy() raises #busy after 140ms; #busy is `position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:80`, `display:grid` when on, with no pointer-events:none and no click handler — it is a hard, undismissable modal. act() holds WRITING for the whole call. So if the socket black-holes rather than resetting (mobile handing off wifi→cellular, a captive-portal re-auth, a bar router that drops state), the overlay stays up and every control in the app is dead until the OS gives up on the connection.
failure_scenario: Song ends. Perry taps "Start top voted". The venue's router has just dropped his association and the TCP connection black-holes instead of resetting. 140ms later the screen goes to a dimmed blur with three bouncing bars. Nothing he taps does anything — not the tab bar, not Voting: Paused, not End the show. iOS will not fail that request for tens of seconds. He has no cancel, no back, and no indication that reloading would help; the only exit is to close and reopen the app from the home screen, which then lands on the sign-in gate (finding 1). That is the entire gap between two songs, in front of the room.
evidence: Static verification: `grep -n "AbortController|AbortSignal|signal:|timeout" public/studio.html` returns nothing; the CSS at 375-378 has no pointer-events override and `<div id="busy" aria-hidden="true">` (line 401) has no onclick; act()'s finally at 750 only runs when the awaited fetch settles.
fix_sketch: Wrap every api() call in `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` (Netlify's own function ceiling is 10s, so anything past that is already lost) and treat the abort as the transport failure in finding 2. Give #busy a "Taking longer than usual — tap to cancel" affordance after ~3s that aborts the controller and releases WRITING. Never let a lock's release depend on a network event that may never arrive.

title: The audience page names the wrong winner whenever a paid "play it again" out-polls the pool — it recomputes the queue from a list that excludes played songs
what_happens: show.mjs deliberately splits one ranking into two arrays: `songs` (show.mjs:37 filters out everything in `show.played`) and `played` (show.mjs:49-53). vote.html then builds "Up next" from ONE of them — `const voted=d.songs.filter(s=>s.votes>0); const queue=voted.slice(0,3);` (vote.html:285-286) — and labels `queue[0]` "Winning — plays next" (vote.html:323). playTop (admin.mjs:898-904) ranks across BOTH: votable songs, minus nowPlaying, keeping any played song that is holding votes. So a replay that is winning is invisible to the queue the room is looking at. This is the exact drift INVARIANT 12b and 0bc were written to prevent, still alive on the surface with the most eyes on it. MYSET.md:131 states the opposite: "Same ranking rule the Studio uses, so the two can never disagree."
failure_scenario: 9:40pm. Perry played Wonderwall an hour ago. Four people at the front each spend 5 credits (replayCost) to hear it again — 20 credits, most of it bought with real money. Three other people vote for Bravo. The whole room's voting page shows "Up next: 1. Bravo (3) — Winning, plays next", with Wonderwall sitting further down in "Already played" showing 4. Perry's Studio button reads "Start top voted — Wonderwall (4)". He taps it and Wonderwall starts. The three Bravo voters just watched the app tell them they had won and then not play their song; the four who paid for Wonderwall were never told they were winning at all.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/upnext.mjs, real handlers end to end: seeded Wonderwall/Alpha/Bravo, played Wonderwall then Alpha, cast four replay votes on Wonderwall (all four returned ok:true and were charged cost 5) and three on Bravo. Output — server `songs` (unplayed pool) = ['Bravo:3'], server `played` = ['Wond
fix_sketch: Either (a) have the client merge before ranking — `const all=[...d.songs,...(d.played||[])].filter(s=>s.votes>0).sort(serverOrder)` won't work because the two arrays arrive pre-sorted separately, so it needs firstAt, which is already on the payload (`s.firstAt`) — rank by `votes desc, firstAt asc, title` exactly as rankSongs does; or (b) better, and in keeping with 12b: have show.mjs compute and ship an explicit `upNext` array off rankSongs applied to the same pool playTop uses, and let vote.html render it without a predicate of its own. Option (b) also lets the replay row carry its rank so the four people who paid can see they are winning. Note (a) reintroduces a fourth copy of rankSongs on the client, which is what caused this.

title: ANSWER 2e — the `artists` registry is a single global blob on the hot read path, and it is the real multi-tenancy brick wall
what_happens: Every storage key in MySet is namespaced per artist except one: `'artists'` (_auth.mjs:48), which holds byId, bySlug and byEmail for every artist on the platform in a single JSON document. `publicArtist(req)` (_lib.mjs:632-637) calls `artistBySlug(slug)` -> `readArtists()` on EVERY request that carries `?a=slug` — which is every poll from every phone at every gig by every artist except Perry (bare myset.vip short-circuits to DEFAULT_ARTIST without the read). It is also read on every session verify, every plan check, every referral. And it is a single CAS-written document, so signup, rename, plan change and referral reward all serialise on one key across the whole platform. `rev` bumping signs out every artist worldwide at once. It is read before the parallel show+shards read, so it is a serialised extra hop on the hot path, and the document grows with every artist you sell to.
failure_scenario: 1,000 artists. Every one of ~268 million /api/show polls a month first does a strong (cache-bypassing) read of a document now holding 1,000 artist records plus two index maps — on the order of 300 KB. Every poll pays that latency serially before it can start the real work. Meanwhile two artists sign up in the same second: both CAS the same document, one retries. That is survivable. But an artist renaming their slug mid-gig, or the referral reward path firing during a busy Saturday, contends with every signup on the platform — and if that document ever fails to converge, casDoc throws 'busy' and NOBODY can look up ANY artist by slug, i.e. every voting page on the platform 404s at once with 'unknown artist'. There is no per-artist blast radius on this one key.
evidence: _auth.mjs:47-52 `readDoc('artists', null)` — no artist id in the key, unlike every other key in KEY.* which is `<thing>_<aid>`. _auth.mjs:68-71 artistBySlug reads the whole registry for one lookup. _lib.mjs:632-637 publicArtist calls it for any `?a=` request; show.mjs:8 awaits it BEFORE the `Promise
fix_sketch: Two changes, both cheap now and expensive later. (1) Break the slug lookup out of the registry into its own tiny per-slug key — `slug_<slug>` holding just `{ artistId }`. That is a 200-byte read instead of a 300 KB one, it never grows, and a busy registry can no longer take down every voting page. Write it alongside the registry in the same mutateArtists callback so they cannot diverge, and fall back to the registry on a miss during migration. (2) Cache the resolution in-process: the artist for a given slug essentially never changes, so a module-level Map with a 60s TTL removes the read from the steady-state hot path entirely (Lambda containers are reused across invocations, so this is real). Add an INVARIANT: 'no global document may be on the per-poll read path.' Longer term this is exactly the thing a Durable Object or a Postgres index solves for free.

title: /api/venueauth checkDomain hands out the public ✓ Verified badge on an email-domain match alone — no site fetch, no vouches
what_happens: venueauth.mjs:132-149 (`action:'checkDomain'`) does `if (site && domainMatches(me.email, site))` and, on a true, writes `v.verified = true; v.verifiedVia = 'domain'` straight into the venues registry. `site` is whatever URL the venue itself typed into its own profile. The page is never fetched, `checkWebsite()` is never called, and the vouch count is never consulted. This is precisely what INVARIANT 0ak forbids ('Domain match alone is not proof of a venue... verification needs BOTH') and what _verify.mjs's own header says is impossible ('ALL THREE of these are required for the automatic tick'). The correct implementation, tryVerifyByWebsite/recheck, lives one file away and is wired to venueadmin.mjs:139 — checkDomain is the stale twin that survived and is still live.
failure_scenario: I want to own the MySet page for a bar I have nothing to do with. I buy any domain, set up an email on it, sign up at myset.vip/venues as 'The Ugly Duckling, Koh Phangan', paste my own domain into the website field, and POST {action:'checkDomain'} to /api/venueauth with my venue token. The registry flips to verified and myset.vip/v/ugly-duckling renders the green ✓ Verified chip — the one signal artists and drinkers use to decide the listing is real. No artist has vouched, and no page anywhere names the venue.
evidence: Executed end-to-end against the real handlers: createVenue({email:'me@totally-not-the-bar.example', name:'The Ugly Duckling'}), set profile.links.website to 'https://totally-not-the-bar.example' (a domain that does not resolve), signed a venue token, POSTed {action:'checkDomain'} -> 200 {"ok":true,"
fix_sketch: Delete the `checkDomain` branch and let venueadmin's `recheck` (which calls tryVerifyByWebsite and therefore requires website + emailOnDomain + siteNamesVenue + 5 vouches) be the only path to `verified`. Then sweep the registry for any row with `verifiedVia === 'domain'` and re-run recheck on it, because badges already granted this way are still showing.

title: "Start the show" the next night resumes YESTERDAY's show — same showId, same played[], last night's songs cost 5 credits, and last night's history row disappears
what_happens: `case 'status'` sets `show.status` and nothing else. showId, startedAt, played[], log[], nowPlaying and every fan record survive. The Live tab renders the identical "Start the show" button whenever `s.status!=='live'`, so the button that resumes a finished show is visually indistinguishable from the one that starts a new one, and "New show" is buried on the Settings tab. Consequences chain: costOf() charges show.replayCost for everything in played[]; show.mjs puts last night's closing song in `nowPlaying`; markPresence skips every returning device because `me.seenShow === show.showId`; and history.mjs:50 filters the current showId out of the shows list while the show is live, so last night's completed row vanishes from the Money tab.
failure_scenario: Saturday 8:40pm, second night of the residency. Perry opens the Studio, sees "Start the show", taps it. The room scans the QR and the audience page says "Playing now: Wagon Wheel" — the song he finished with last night. Every one of the eleven songs he played on Friday sits under "Already played · 5 votes to hear again", so a fan with 3 free credits cannot ask for any of them. His own Money tab is now empty — Friday's row is gone, replaced by a live card claiming 11 songs already played tonight. At 1am he ends the show and Saturday never gets a history entry at all, because archiveShow hits Friday's frozen document (finding 1).
evidence: Ran the real handlers: night one played Alpha then Bravo, status ended, archived (songsPlayed 2, room 4). Then `status:'live'` -> `showId now: show-1788237461184 | same as night1? true | startedAt still night1? true | played carried over: ['alpha']`. A brand-new fan's /api/show payload on night two:
fix_sketch: In `case 'status'`, when transitioning to 'live', compare `show.endedAt`/`show.startedAt` against now. More than ~6 hours (or a different local date) means this is a new night: mint a fresh showId, archive-and-seal the previous one, clear played/log/nowPlaying and run carryFans — exactly what newShow does. Under the threshold, resume as today. Also show the current show's start time on the Live tab so the artist can see which show he is in.

title: The free plan's featured cap is measured against the whole library, not against what the room can see, so a covers act on the free tier has every paid song request refused at 402 on stage
what_happens: Every cap check counts `sh.songs.filter(x => x.active !== false).length` — library-wide `active` songs — with no awareness of `playable()`. With a setlist active the audience sees only `listSongs ∩ active`, which is typically a fraction of that. INVARIANT 0s0 states the plan 'caps how many are live to the audience at once'; with a setlist active, that is not the quantity being measured. The sharpest consequence is `askAccept`'s deliberate refusal (admin.mjs:584/595, INVARIANT 0be): a request the fan has already been charged for is refused because of songs the room cannot even see tonight. Free's cap is 50; Plus and Pro are Infinity, so this bites only — and always — on the tier the thousand-artist plan depends on.
failure_scenario: A test user signs up on free, imports his 60-song working repertoire (Perry's own library is 66-67 songs, so this is the normal case, not the edge). Songs 51-60 arrive switched off. Tonight he plays a 12-song 'Tonight' set, so the room sees 12. A fan pays 3 credits to request 'Wonderwall'. He taps Accept on stage and gets: 'Your plan features 50 songs at a time. Switch one off first, then accept this — their votes stay put until you do.' There is no song he can switch off that would help — the room is seeing 12. To honour a 3-credit request he has to leave the Live tab, scroll a 60-row list, and switch a song off that nobody could vote for anyway. The Studio's own copy on that screen reads '50 of 50 featured. Your plan shows 50 to the audience at a time', which is false: the audience is being shown 12.
evidence: Probe p7.mjs, real handlers: `plan = "free", featured cap = 50`; 60 songs added → `library 60 active 50`, song 51 returned the note 'Added, but switched off — your plan features 50 at a time.'; a 12-song setlist activated → `room sees 12 songs`; a fan paid 3 credits for a request; `askAccept` return
fix_sketch: Count the cap against what is actually offered. Where a setlist is active, the relevant number is `playable(show).songs.length`; where none is, it is the current library-active count. At minimum, exempt `askAccept` from the cap when a setlist is active and the accepted song joins that set — the room's visible count goes from N to N+1, which is the quantity the plan is meant to limit. Fix the Studio's copy (studio.html:1127) to say what is being counted. Given the $10/mo goal, also reconsider whether 50 is the right free ceiling when a typical working act arrives with 60-100 songs — today the free tier's first experience is a truncation notice.

title: `playTop` is not idempotent, so one lost response on bar wifi makes the Studio start the alphabetically-first song instead of the one the room voted for
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: `act()` holds the WRITING lock only for the duration of the fetch and releases it in `finally` (studio.html:749). When the POST reaches the server but the response is lost, the server has already started the song and run `clearAllFanVotes()` (admin.mjs:1053), while the artist sees `toast('Connection hiccup — try again')` and an unchanged screen. A second tap runs `playTop` again — but now `counts` is all zeros, so `rankSongs` falls through votes-desc and first-voted to the title tiebreak, and the winner from tap 1 has moved into `show.played` where the `!show.played.includes(s.id) || counts[s.id] > 0` filter (admin.mjs:900) excludes it. The request carries no idempotency key and the server has no notion of 'this is the same tap'.
failure_scenario: Room voted: Wonderwall 3, Zombie 1, Angie 0, Brown Eyed Girl 0. Perry taps 'Start top voted'. The server starts Wonderwall and wipes the tally; the response never arrives. He sees 'Connection hiccup — try again' and taps again three seconds later. The server starts **Angie** — zero votes, first alphabetically — and Wonderwall is now in `played[]`, so the song three people just voted for can only come back if somebody pays 5 credits for a replay. Show history gets a phantom round too. Everyone in the bar is looking at their phone watching 'Wonderwall — Winning, plays next' vanish and Angie start.
evidence: End-to-end against the real handlers with test/blobs-fake.mjs (same rig as test/e2e.mjs). Output: `tally before the tap: Wonderwall=3, Zombie=1, Angie=0, Brown Eyed Girl=0` / `tap 1 -> server started: Wonderwall` / `tally now: all=0` / `tap 2 -> server started: Angie  status 200` / `played[]: Wonder
fix_sketch: Have the Studio mint a `tapId` (crypto.randomUUID) per press of Start and send it with `play`/`playTop`. Server-side, keep the last few tapIds in `meta` (or on the show doc); if the incoming tapId was already applied, skip the mutation and just return the current `stagePayload` — the same claim-before-grant shape `_pay.mjs` already uses for Stripe sessions. Also: hold the WRITING lock on a transport failure and change the toast to 'Couldn't reach the server — check before tapping again', so the artist is not invited to retry a write that may already have landed.

title: askDecline reports "votes refunded" to both the artist and the fan even when the refund did not happen — no read-back verify on either fan-record write, and the failure is swallowed
what_happens: INVARIANT 4 says a conditional write on Netlify Blobs can report success without sticking, which is why every fan-record write is supposed to go through casDoc's read-back verify. vote.mjs does this (vote.mjs:50). The request flow does not: refund() at _requests.mjs:125 calls mutateFan with no verify argument, and so does the charge at _requests.mjs:91. casDoc with verify === null returns {ok:true} the moment the store says modified !== false (_lib.mjs:293-294), so a lost write is never retried and never reported. On top of that, resolveRequest wraps the refund in `.catch(() => {})` (_requests.mjs:154), so even a hard 'busy' throw after casDoc's 40 retries is discarded — and admin.mjs:562 then unconditionally returns `refunded: row.cost`. The artist's Studio toasts "Declined, votes refunded"; the fan's page renders "Not tonight — votes refunded" (vote.html:401). The row is now permanently 'declined', so a second askDecline returns 409 and there is no retry path for anyone. The charge side fails in the opposite direction: a lost charge hands out a free request, which is the exact thing INVARIANT 0ac's take-first ordering exists to prevent.
failure_scenario: Busy Saturday, forty phones in the room, a burst of votes landing on the same fan shard. A fan asks for a song Perry doesn't know and pays 3 of her 3 free credits, so her page shows 0 votes left. Perry taps ✕. His Studio freezes behind the busy overlay for about eight seconds (40 casDoc retries with backoff), then says "Declined, votes refunded". Her page says "Not tonight — votes refunded". Her balance is still 0. She cannot vote for anything for the rest of the round, cannot re-ask, and there is no button on either phone that will try the refund again. If she had bought those votes, that is a real $3 gone with two screens telling her it was returned.
evidence: Scratchpad probe6.mjs injects the precise failure INVARIANT 4 names — one store.set() that returns {modified:true} without persisting — through my own module hook (fakewrap.mjs), and runs three paths against it. (A) CONTROL, vote.mjs which HAS verify: vote succeeds and credits.used = 1, i.e. it reco
fix_sketch: Pass a verify callback to both mutateFan calls, mirroring vote.mjs:50. For the refund, capture the expected `spent` and verify it landed; for the charge, verify me.spent increased. Then stop lying about the outcome: let refund() propagate, and have resolveRequest return whether the refund actually stuck so admin.mjs:562 can report `refunded: 0` plus an error the Studio can show ("Declined, but the refund didn't go through — tap ✕ again"). That needs the status transition to stay retryable, so on a failed refund leave the row `pending` rather than committing it to 'declined'. Add the injected-failure harness to test/ — it is the only way this class of bug is ever going to be caught.

title: Every /api/show poll from a non-founding artist's room reads the whole global artists registry twice — 419 KB per poll at 1000 artists, on the hottest path in the app
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: `publicArtist` calls `artistBySlug`, which calls `readArtists()` — a strong-consistency read of the single global `artists` document. Then `getShow` fills in the artist's display name by calling `artistById`, which reads the SAME document again (defaultShow().artist is '' and no admin action ever sets show.artist, so this second read fires on every single request forever). The document holds byId + bySlug + byEmail for every artist on the platform, so its size is O(artists) while it is read on the per-phone, per-poll path. Perry has never felt this because his fans use the bare URL, which short-circuits at _lib.mjs:634 and skips artistBySlug entirely. stagePayload does the same registry read on every Studio write.
failure_scenario: A thousand artists are signed up; a hundred are playing on a Friday night with twenty phones each. Each phone polls /api/show?a=<slug> every 3 seconds. That is ~670 requests/second, each pulling 419 KB of a single global blob key — roughly 280 MB/s of strong reads against ONE key, plus 1340 reads/sec of that key. Blobs read latency on that key climbs, every room's queue stops updating, and the vote page's backoff never engages because the latency is not a change in the payload. It also lands squarely on INVARIANT 9d's cost problem from a direction it doesn't cover: not call count, bandwidth.
evidence: /tmp/hot2.mjs with an instrumented copy of the blob fake counting every getWithMetadata by key. Built a 1000-artist registry in the exact shape createArtist writes: 209 KB serialized. Then: `/api/show?a=artist7 -> 16 blob GETs; 'artists' read 2 x = 419 KB of the global doc per poll` versus `/api/sho
fix_sketch: Three cheap steps. (1) Memoise readArtists() per request (module-level with a short TTL) so no single handler reads it twice — kills half of it immediately. (2) Store the artist's display name on the show record when it changes, so getShow stops needing the registry at all. (3) Split the registry: a small `slugs` document (slug -> {aid, name}) for the public hot path, keeping byEmail/byId in `artists` for auth. The public lookup then reads ~40 bytes per artist instead of ~210.

title: Show history attributes another artist's revenue as your own — no artist filter, and showId collides across tenants
lenses: Scale & multi-tenancy — does this hold a
what_happens: moneyForShow(aid, showId, ...) takes `aid` and never uses it — `md.artist` appears zero times in the whole file (verified with grep -c). Filtering is purely `md.show === showId`. But showId comes from newShowId() (_lib.mjs:82), which is `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM` in UTC with no artist in it, and every artist's audience pays into the same Stripe key (INVARIANT 0r). So any two artists who tap "New show" in the same UTC minute produce byte-identical showIds and each archives the other's takings. Separately, line 37 sums EVERY untagged MySet session on the platform into every artist's `unattributed`. The 10-page/1,000-session cap at line 27 silently truncates a busy night on top of that.
failure_scenario: Friday 4 Sep, 20:00 UTC. Alice taps New show; so does Bobby, 40 seconds later. Both showIds are "2026-09-04-2000". Alice sells one $3 vote pack all night. Bobby sells an $11 pack and takes a $20 tip noted "legend". A third artist, Carla, takes a $50 tip on an untagged legacy session. I ran this through the real moneyForShow against a shared-account Stripe stub: Alice's archived show reports gross $34.00, votes $14.00 / 2, tips $20.00 / 1 with the note "legend" and Bobby's fan id, and unattributed $50.00. Alice opens History on Saturday, sees $34 from a night she made $3, and either believes it or stops trusting the product. INVARIANT 17d exists precisely to stop a fabricated number landing on that screen.
evidence: Ran the real _history.mjs moneyForShow() in-process with @netlify/blobs and stripe both redirected to stand-ins (scratchpad m/money.mjs + m/stripe-fake.mjs, which models one shared Stripe account exactly as sessions.list does). Output verbatim: {"gross":34,"votes":{"amount":14,"count":2},"tips":{"am
fix_sketch: Two independent fixes, both cheap. (1) Add `if (md.artist && md.artist !== aid) continue;` and `if (!md.artist && aid !== DEFAULT_ARTIST) continue;` to the loop in moneyForShow — the parameter is already there. (2) Make showId unforgeable across tenants: `newShowId()` -> `${aid}-${YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM}` or append 4 random chars. Keep reading old ids so existing history still resolves. Also drop `unattributed` for anyone but DEFAULT_ARTIST rather than showing a stranger's total.

title: ANSWER 3 — Perry is paying TWICE for every release: `git push` and `netlify deploy --prod` each bill 15 credits, and they race over what is actually live
what_happens: The site IS already wired to GitHub for CI builds (provider github, installation_id 148158530, repo perryidyll/myset, allowed_branches ['main'], skip_automatic_builds not set). So every `git push` to main triggers a Netlify production build — 15 credits. Perry ALSO runs `netlify deploy --build --prod`, which uploads a second production deploy — another 15 credits. Both fire for the same change. In the 26 hours I sampled there were 37 CI production deploys and 19 CLI production deploys: 56 × 15 = 840 credits, against a 1,000-credit monthly Personal allowance that does not roll over. INVARIANT 9d0 correctly identifies deploys as the expensive thing but does not know the count is being doubled. Worse than the money: whichever finishes last wins. The CLI deploy publishes the local working tree; the CI build publishes the commit. If they differ, production silently ends up as whichever landed second, and the repo no longer describes what is live.
failure_scenario: Perry fixes something at 19:20, runs `netlify deploy --build --prod` from his laptop with one uncommitted tweak still in the working tree, then commits and pushes at 19:23. The CI build finishes at 19:26 and republishes — silently reverting the uncommitted tweak. He refreshes myset.vip, the tweak is gone, and nothing in the deploy log says why. This is the exact interleaving I found at 13:21:30 (CI, commit fa6e1d24) / 13:21:36 (CLI, no commit) and again at 13:23:10 / 13:23:16. Cost side: on 2026-08-31 alone this pattern burned ~840 credits against a 1,000-credit month.
evidence: `netlify api getSite` -> build_settings.provider 'github', repo_url https://github.com/perryidyll/myset, repo_branch main, installation_id 148158530, allowed_branches ['main'], skip_automatic_builds null. `netlify api listSiteDeploys` (100 deploys, 2026-08-30 17:34 → 2026-08-31 19:26) classified by
fix_sketch: Pick ONE path and turn the other off. RECOMMENDED: keep git-triggered CI as the only way to reach production. It is reproducible, it is what the commit says, it gives you PR previews for free, and it costs the same 15 credits. Then stop using `netlify deploy --prod` entirely — `netlify deploy` (draft, 0 credits) stays the iteration tool. If Perry prefers to keep laptop control, do the opposite: turn off auto-publishing at Project configuration > Build & deploy > Continuous deployment (either 'Stop builds' or restrict allowed_branches to a branch nobody pushes), and deploy only via CLI. Either way the immediate saving is 50% of the deploy line, which is the dominant line at his current volume. Also add to INVARIANTS.md that a push and a CLI --prod both publish, and that the loser is silently overwritten.

title: An accidental "End the show" immediately asks every fan holding purchased votes to donate them, and "Let them keep it" destroys the credits while the gig carries on
what_happens: vote.html render() fires `if(ended && c.paidLeft>0 && !c.decided && !SHEETED){ SHEETED=true; setTimeout(()=>openLeftover(c.paidLeft),700) }`. The only trigger is `status === 'ended'`; there is no dwell time and no notion of the show being finished for good. gift.mjs then does `me.extra = Math.max(0, me.extra - votes)` and records the gift — irreversible, with no refund path anywhere in the app. Because the poll signature includes `d.status`, the sheet reaches the room within 12 seconds of the artist's tap; because `status:'live'` changes nothing else, the show then resumes with the fan's balance at zero.
failure_scenario: A fan at the beach bar buys the $7 / 9-vote pack at 9:20pm and spends one credit on Alpha. At 9:31 Perry fat-fingers "End the show". Within twelve seconds her phone shows a sheet: "You've got 9 votes left — that's a wrap. Let Perry keep it / Call it a tip". She is being generous, so she taps it. Perry taps "Start the show" at 9:31:40 and plays for another three hours. She now has 2 free credits, no paid balance, no way to get the 9 back, and the app never tells her the show did not actually end. At a thousand artists this is a recurring refund request against a Stripe account that has no per-artist Connect split (INVARIANT 0r) to refund from.
evidence: Ran gift.mjs and the real admin/show handlers end to end. Buyer seeded with extra=9, spent 1 credit -> payload `paidLeft: 9, decided: false`. `status:'ended'` -> payload still `paidLeft: 9, decided: false` (the exact condition on vote.html:372). POST /api/gift {choice:'gift'} -> `{ok:true, choice:'g
fix_sketch: Gate the sheet on the show being sealed rather than on `status==='ended'` (see finding 1's seal flag), or at minimum require `Date.now() - show.endedAt > ~10 minutes` before offering the choice. Server-side, make gift.mjs refuse while the show is not sealed. The "Do nothing and they stay yours" default is already correct — the bug is only that the question is asked too early.

title: The public city feed is an uncapped sequential per-artist fan-out, and each row re-reads the whole registry
lenses: Scale & multi-tenancy — does this hold a
what_happens: `for (const id of ids)` at events.mjs:67 awaits inside the loop — the fan-out is strictly sequential — and there is no cap on `ids` at all (the picker at line 137 caps at 40; the feed does not). Each iteration does readEvents(id) plus artistById(id) or venueById(id), and both of those read their ENTIRE global registry document from scratch with no memoisation. The response also carries `cache-control: no-store` (from json() in _lib.mjs), so every homepage visitor pays the full cost.
failure_scenario: MySet takes off in Nashville: 300 artists index themselves into country=USA, city=Nashville. Someone opens the city feed. The handler makes 600 strictly sequential strong-consistency blob reads — at a conservative 20 ms each that is 12 seconds, past Netlify's 10-second synchronous function limit, so the request is killed and the homepage shows nothing. It fails for everyone simultaneously and gets worse as the product succeeds; the more artists in a city, the more certain the city's feed is dead. On the way there it is also reading 300 x 310 KB = 93 MB of registry JSON to answer one page view.
evidence: Op-counted the real events.mjs handler against a synthetic platform of 200 registered artists with recurring gigs, half of them piled into one city. `?places=1` = 124 blob reads; the busiest city feed = 235 blob reads, i.e. ~2.35 sequential reads per artist in that city, exactly matching readEvents
fix_sketch: Cap and parallelise: `const batch = ids.slice(0, 200)` then `await Promise.all(batch.map(...))` — the reads are independent. Hoist the registry: call readArtists()/readVenues() ONCE before the loop and look up from the in-memory map instead of calling artistById per row (this alone halves the reads and removes the 93 MB). Then denormalise name+slug into the city index entry so the feed needs no registry read at all, and put a short `cache-control: public, max-age=60` on this one public endpoint — a gig listing does not need to be second-fresh.

title: Thirty throwaway fan ids fill the request queue permanently, and the artist cannot clear it — declining refunds the bot and fresh ids are free
lenses: Fan identity & anti-abuse — how a person
what_happens: createRequest caps the queue at MAX_PENDING = 30 open rows per show (_requests.mjs:17, enforced at :85-86 with a 429) and at one open row per (fan, kind) (:80-84). Both caps are keyed on the client-supplied fan id, which is free to mint. Default request cost is 3 votes (defaultShow: `requests: {on:false, cost:3}`) and a fresh id holds exactly 3 free credits — so every invented id can afford exactly one request, and the queue fills in 30 requests. The artist's only remedy is to decline them one at a time; resolveRequest refunds a declined row (:150-152), and even without the refund the attacker has an unlimited supply of new ids. There is no per-network cap and no 'clear all'.
failure_scenario: Perry switches requests on at 9pm — the feature he switched on precisely because he wants the room to engage. Someone fires 30 POSTs to /api/request in about four seconds. Perry's Studio now shows '30 requests waiting', thirty rows deep, each one a line of whatever text the attacker chose (up to 80 chars, escaped so it can't script, but it is still on his stage screen). A real fan at table six taps 'Request a song', types 'Wonderwall, for my wife's birthday', and her phone says "There are a lot of requests in already — try again in a bit". Perry, holding a guitar, has to tap ✕ thirty times between songs — and each ✕ is a full /api/admin write that reads the show, all twelve fan shards, meta, requests, lists and learn to rebuild stagePayload. By the time he has cleared it the attacker has refilled it. This is exactly the 10pm-in-a-noisy-bar defect the audit brief is about, and it is four seconds of effort.
evidence: scratchpad/abuse.mjs, real request.mjs + _requests.mjs handlers: 30 POSTs from ids 'flood0'..'flood29' all returned ok; bot 30 got `429 There are a lot of requests in already`; a genuine fan id ('genuinefan') then got the same 429. `askList` confirmed 30 rows in the artist's panel. Each bot spent ex
fix_sketch: Three cheap changes, none of which touches 0ab (never charge money) or 0ac (take the votes first): (1) cap open requests per roomHash bucket at ~3, so one network cannot own the queue; (2) reserve headroom — e.g. MAX_PENDING 30 but never let a single bucket hold more than a quarter of it, so a genuine fan always gets in; (3) give the Studio a single 'Decline all pending' action that resolves the batch in one admin write rather than thirty. If server-minted cookie ids land (finding 1), (1) becomes much stronger because a bucket's identities are then countable.

title: Purchased votes are never consumed — a $11 pack grants +18 credits EVERY round for the rest of the night, and `unspentPaid`/`carryFans` assume the opposite
what_happens: `clearAllFanVotes` resets `v`, `ts` and `spent` but deliberately leaves `extra` alone (_lib.mjs:389). Since spend is never debited from `extra` — it is only ever recomputed as `creditsUsed` against the pooled total `freeCredits + extra` (vote.mjs:41) — a fan's `extra` is a permanent per-round bonus, not a stock. `extra` is decremented in exactly one place in the entire codebase: gift.mjs:26, when the fan gives it away. Meanwhile `unspentPaid()` (_lib.mjs:398-403) computes 'votes they bought and haven't spent' and `carryFans` (_lib.mjs:404-417) carries only that portion into the next show — code written on the assumption that paid votes deplete. The two halves of the same system model `extra` differently, which is the strongest evidence this is unintended rather than a deliberate 'bigger allowance for the night' design. Nothing in INVARIANTS.md documents it either way (I checked all 98).
failure_scenario: 10:15pm. One fan buys the $11 max pack: 18 votes. `extra = 18`, so his total is 21 credits per round against everyone else's 3. Perry plays fourteen more songs that night. That fan gets 21 credits fourteen times — 294 credit-rounds for $11 — and can single-handedly force a 5-credit replay every single round while also outvoting any three other people on the main pool. The room's queue stops reflecting the room. Under the product lens this is worse than a UX problem: at 1000 artists the vote pack is the only per-fan revenue line, and it is priced as a consumable while behaving as an unlimited night pass. One purchase per room per night is the ceiling, because after the first one nobody needs a second. It also quietly breaks INVARIANT 0ab's spirit — 'never charge money for a request' — since $11 now buys effectively unlimited 5-credit replay requests all night.
evidence: Two independent checks. (1) grep -rn '\.extra' across netlify/functions and public: the only decrement anywhere is gift.mjs:26. (2) Ran the real handlers (/tmp/msaudit/credits2.mjs): granted extra=9 via mutateFan the way _pay.mjs:42 does; read remaining=12/total=12. Cast a 5-cost replay vote → remai
fix_sketch: Decide the intended model and make both halves agree. If paid votes are meant to be consumable (which unspentPaid and carryFans already assume, and which the pack pricing implies): debit `extra` at the point of spend — in the vote.mjs cast branch, charge free credits first and decrement `me.extra` for the remainder, and mirror that in _requests.mjs:93. If they are meant to be a night pass, say so on the buy sheet and delete unspentPaid/carryFans' pretence that a balance is left over. Either way this needs settling before a second artist sells a pack, and it is adjacent to but separate from the vote-locking question — flagging it here because it is the only place in the app where a fan's votes can genuinely be worth money round-to-round.

title: Turning on "∞ Unlimited" disables every Vote button in the room — the client's affordability rule forgot the unlimited case the ask-card's rule remembers
what_happens: show.mjs:92 sends `remaining: unl ? null : ...`. The affordability rule then exists in three places on the audience page and only two of them guard on `unlimited`. The header pill (vote.html:300) guards: `!c.unlimited && c.remaining<=0`. The ask-card (vote.html:396) guards: `short=k=>!c.unlimited&&c.remaining<k`. The song row (vote.html:383) does NOT: `const dis=!open||(!s.mine&&c.remaining<cost)`. With `remaining === null`, JS coerces null to 0, so `null < 1` is true and every row renders `<button ... disabled>`. Only songs the fan has already voted for stay tappable (to un-vote). The page simultaneously displays "∞" in the credit pill and "Unlimited votes" in the status strip.
failure_scenario: Perry is booked for a private 40th birthday party. The host has paid for the night, so before the room fills up he opens Studio → Settings → Free votes and taps the "∞ Unlimited" chip (studio.html:1361). Everyone scans the QR. Their pill reads ∞, the strip reads "Unlimited votes", and not one Vote button in the list works — every one is greyed out. Nobody in the room can cast a single vote, and there is no error message to explain why. Same failure on the narrower path: the artist's own phone with "Unlimited votes for me" switched on (studio.html:1428) can never cast a test vote, which is the exact thing that toggle exists for.
evidence: Two independent measurements. (1) /tmp/msaudit/unl.mjs ran the REAL admin.mjs and show.mjs handlers via test/register.mjs: after `unlimited {on:true}` the payload is `{"unlimited":true,"remaining":null,...}` and, feeding that through the row() predicate, both songs came back `disabled: true` with `o
fix_sketch: Make row() use the same guard the other two use: `const dis=!open||(!s.mine&&!c.unlimited&&c.remaining<cost)`. Better, since this rule is now in three places on one page: hoist one `const afford=n=>c.unlimited||c.remaining>=n;` at the top of render() and call it from row(), askCard() and the pill. Cheapest belt-and-braces alternative is to have show.mjs send `remaining: Infinity` instead of null for unlimited fans, but that changes the pill and the signature() string, so fixing the predicate is the smaller change.

title: ANSWER 2c — the economics: Netlify at 1,000 artists is ~$1,350–$2,580/mo (13–26% of revenue) and SSE/WebSockets — the correct fix — cost MORE on Netlify, not less. That is the structural reason to move.
what_happens: Modelling 25 phones per gig, 8 gigs/month/artist, busy room, 10 production deploys/month, against measured payload and a bounded duration: 1 artist = 352–537 credits (Personal $9 — note ONE artist already eats a third to a half of the 1,000-credit allowance); 10 artists = 2,165–4,021 credits (Pro $20–$33 — comfortable); 100 artists = 20,301–38,859 credits ($136–$256/mo against $1,000 revenue); 1,000 artists = 201,658–387,241 credits ($1,346–$2,576/mo against $10,000 revenue). WHICH LIMIT BITES FIRST: not a hard ceiling — the credit BILL bites first, and it bites at around 100 artists, where hosting crosses ~15–25% of revenue. The hard limits are comfortable: 1,000 concurrent Lambda executions, 60s sync timeout, 6 MB payload, 5 GB objects, no documented Blobs QPS ceiling. The trap is that the obvious engineering fix makes Netlify WORSE. Replacing polling with SSE (Netlify streaming functions, 60s limit) would cut invocations ~18x, but Netlify bills compute by WALL-CLOCK GB-hours: holding a function open 55s costs 55 GB-s where 18 polls cost ~6 GB-s. On Netlify, the right architecture is 9x more expensive. Cloudflare bills CPU only and does not bill I/O wait, so the same design is nearly free there.
failure_scenario: Perry hits 120 paying artists, feels successful, and gets a $260 Netlify bill on $1,200 of revenue. He does the sensible thing and rewrites the polling as SSE to cut the invocation count — and the bill goes UP, because he has traded 33,000 short invocations per gig for 130 long ones that are billed for every second they sit waiting on nothing. He has no way to know this in advance because the pricing page frames compute as GB-hours without saying it is wall clock.
evidence: Model driven by measured inputs (11,035-byte payload, 0.12–0.37s duration band, simulated poll counts) against docs.netlify.com credit rates and the Pro tier table (3k/$20, 5k/$33, 10k/$63, 15k/$95, 20k/$126, then 1,500-credit packs at $10). Netlify compute is explicitly 'GB-Hour' with a worked exam
fix_sketch: Stay on Netlify through ~100 artists — it is cheap, it works, and the credit line is a rounding error against revenue until then. Use that runway to (a) fix the signature coupling above, which is free money, and (b) keep the storage door open (next finding). Plan the move at the point where hosting crosses ~10% of revenue. Do NOT build SSE on Netlify; if real-time is wanted, it is the thing you migrate FOR, not the thing you retrofit.

title: Every new artist's audience gets live Stripe buy buttons that pay into the platform's single Stripe key — INVARIANT 0r is a note, not a guard
what_happens: defaultShow() (_lib.mjs) gives every brand-new artist the full DEFAULT_PACKS(), and show.mjs:96 returns `paymentsEnabled: !!process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` — a global, not a per-artist fact. pay.mjs creates the Checkout Session with the one `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, tagging metadata.artist with the artist's id, and confirm/webhook/_pay grant the votes under that id. So the votes are delivered correctly to the fan, and the cash lands entirely in the platform owner's Stripe account. revenue.mjs then shows the new artist a Money tab with those totals in it. INVARIANT 0r states the rule ('Do not onboard a second paying artist before Connect') but nothing in code enforces it — no per-artist Stripe account, no flag, no refusal in pay.mjs.
failure_scenario: Perry hands MySet to Sam for a Saturday. Sam signs up at myset.vip/signup, taps the starter setlist, plays. He never touches a pricing screen — the packs are on by default. Twelve people in the room buy the $3 pack. $36 is charged to twelve real cards and settles into Perry's Stripe balance. Sam's own Money tab shows gross $36 and twelve payments. There is no transfer mechanism, no application_fee_amount, and no record that the money is owed to Sam. On Sunday Sam asks where his $36 is, and the honest answer is 'in my bank account, and there is no button that moves it'. Multiply by the intended thousand artists.
evidence: Measured: with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set, createArtist('sam@band.example') then GET /api/show?a=samreeves returns `paymentsEnabled: true` and the full default packs `{small:{votes:3,cents:300},big:{votes:9,cents:700},max:{votes:18,cents:1100}}` — with zero configuration by the new artist. Script at /tmp

Until Connect exists, gate money on identity: in pay.mjs, refuse with 503 'payments-not-configured' unless `aid === DEFAULT_ARTIST` (or unless the artist record carries a `stripeAccount`), and have show.mjs compute `paymentsEnabled` from the same test so the buttons never render for anyone else. That way a test user's gig degrades to free voting — which the app already supports fully (INVARIANT 9) — instead of quietly collecting their audience's money for someone else.

title: A renamed or mistyped slug returns 404 and vote.html sits on the loading skeleton forever — printed table QR codes die silently

Every fan who scans a card gets a page that shimmers grey forever — no message, no setlist, no error. They assume the wifi is bad, try twice, put the phone away. title: There is no server-side identity at all: anyone on the internet can cast unlimited votes for any artist, without being in the room
lenses: Fan identity & anti-abuse — how a person
what_happens: vote.mjs:9 takes the voter's identity straight from the request body — `cleanFanId(body.fan)` — and cleanFanId (_lib.mjs:638) is a character filter, not a check: it accepts any [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,40} string. mutateFan then creates the record on demand (`bag[fanId] ||= {v:[],extra:0,ts:{}}`), so every string the attacker invents is a brand-new fan holding show.freeCredits (default 3) free votes. There is no rate limit anywhere on /api/vote — I grepped every function for one; the only 429 in the codebase is the request-queue cap in _requests.mjs:86. The artist slug is a public URL (?a=perry-idyll), and song ids are `slug(title)` (admin.mjs:959), so "wonderwall" is guessable without even reading /api/show. Nothing requires the caller to have scanned the QR, to be on the venue's network, or to be in the country.
failure_scenario: Perry is on stage at the Ugly Duckling. In the room there are 30 people and the real leader is 'Sweet Caroline' with 8 votes. A 19-year-old at the bar opens Safari, puts it in desktop mode, opens the console on the voting page and pastes a 12-iteration loop of `fetch('/api/vote',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({fan:'z'+i,song:'wonderwall'})})`. Ninety seconds later 'Wonderwall' has 12 votes and every phone in the room agrees it won. Perry taps "Start top voted" and plays it. Nobody — not the room, not Perry, not the history archive — can tell it was one person. Worse at 1000 artists: the attacker does not have to be in the bar. `curl -X POST 'https://myset.vip/api/vote?a=<anyslug>' -d '{"fan":"z1","song":"wonderwall"}'` from anywhere pins one song at the top of any artist's queue all night, and a competitor or a bored teenager can do it to a stranger's gig they will never attend.
evidence: Ran the real vote.mjs handler in-process against test/blobs-fake.mjs (scratchpad/attack.mjs). 200 sequential POSTs with fan ids 'x0'..'x199' on song 'bravo': /api/show then reported `bravo:200 alpha:3 charlie:0`, i.e. 200/200 accepted, zero rejected, in 18ms of handler time. A single invented id was
fix_sketch: Two layers, neither of which breaks 9g (the audience never signs in). (a) Mint the fan id SERVER-side: on the first /api/show, set an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie carrying an HMAC-signed id, and have vote.mjs prefer the cookie over body.fan. That alone turns a one-line curl loop into 'manage a cookie jar per identity' and lets you count identities per network honestly. (b) Rate-limit by network bucket. INVARIANT 0ae is right that an IP is not a PERSON — forty people on the beach bar's wifi are one IP — but it does not follow that an IP is useless as a RATE bucket. Cap new fan-id creations per roomHash(aid, ip) per show at something no honest room reaches (say 80) and votes per bucket per minute at say 120; over the cap, still return 200 and still show the vote to that phone, but do not count it (INVARIANT 16 — nothing may break the gig, so this must fail open toward 'the page still works'). (c) The strongest and cheapest: a per-show proof-of-presence token. The QR already exists and already carries a URL; put a short rotating token in it that the Studio displays, require it on /api/vote, and remote stuffing dies without the room noticing anything.

title: The $3 vote pack is exactly reproducible for free by opening one private tab — the paid product is protected only by ignorance
lenses: Fan identity & anti-abuse — how a person
what_happens: The smallest pack is `small: { votes: 3, cents: 300 }` (_lib.mjs:199-203) — three votes for $3. A fresh fan id is worth `freeCredits: 3` (_lib.mjs:106), and the fan id is nothing but a localStorage string minted in the browser (vote.html:212-215). So the thing being sold and the thing given away for nothing are the same size. Clearing site data, a private tab, a second browser, a second phone, or editing localStorage each yields another 3. And clearAllFanVotes (_lib.mjs:383) resets `v` and `spent` on every song start, so free credits already refresh every round — the ONLY thing $3 buys is 'vote for 3 more songs within this one round', which is precisely what a private tab gives away.
failure_scenario: Two friends at the gig. One taps 'Get more votes', pays $3 through Stripe, gets 3 extra votes. The other holds down the Safari tab button, taps 'Private', reopens myset.vip, and has 3 more votes in about five seconds — no console, no curl, no technical knowledge. The first one watches. At one artist this is a shrug. At 1000 artists on $10/month, audience vote-pack revenue is the pitch for why the free tier converts and why an artist tolerates the platform taking a cut once Connect exists (INVARIANT 0r) — and that revenue line evaporates the first time someone posts the private-tab trick in a comment thread.
evidence: scratchpad/attack.mjs: fan 'x0' cast 3 votes (`ok:true, remaining:0`) then was refused; fan 'x1' immediately cast 3 more. /api/show reported `credits.total = 3` for every distinct id, with no per-device, per-network or per-show ceiling above it. Nothing in _lib.mjs, vote.mjs or show.mjs ties freeCre
fix_sketch: Make the free grant a property of the ROOM, not of the id. Grant the 3 free credits against the network bucket (roomHash) the first time an id appears, and give a new id on an already-seen bucket 0 free credits with wording like 'you've already got your free votes tonight' — that is exactly the 'one phone rotating its id' case INVARIANT 0ae says the net hash exists to catch. It cannot be perfect (mobile data, a second phone), and it should not try to be: the goal is that the free path costs more effort than $3 is worth. Also consider making the packs differ in KIND rather than quantity — e.g. a pack is what lets you afford a replay (cost 5 > free 3), which is already the one thing a free identity provably cannot buy.

title: moneyForShow is the one Stripe consumer of four that does not filter on metadata.artist, and showId is only minute-precision — so two artists starting a show in the same minute inherit each other's revenue forever
what_happens: pay.mjs:37 and :51 stamp every Checkout Session with `artist: aid`. Three of the four consumers respect it: revenue.mjs:32 (`return !md.artist || md.artist === aid`), webhook.mjs:36 and confirm.mjs:23 both route by `metadata.artist`. The fourth — _history.mjs::moneyForShow, the one that writes the permanent number onto the artist's show history — never mentions md.artist. It lists sessions account-wide by time window and matches on `md.show !== showId` only (_history.mjs:36), and dumps any MySet session in the window with no show tag into THIS artist's `unattributed` (:37). Under INVARIANT 0r every artist's audience pays into one Stripe key, so the whole account is in scope. The collision key is weak: newShowId (_lib.mjs:82-86) returns `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM` — no artist id, no randomness, one-minute resolution.
failure_scenario: Two artists on the free tier, both in Thailand. At 21:30:12 UTC Maya taps "New show" for her second set; at 21:30:49 UTC Tom taps it for his. Both shows are now `2026-09-05-2130`. A fan at Maya's gig buys the $11 pack; a fan at Tom's gig tips $20. Both nights end within the same window. Maya's archive calls moneyForShow('maya-x','2026-09-05-2130', …), matches BOTH sessions on md.show, and writes gross $31 with Tom's tip and its note text into her `tips.recent`. Tom's archive writes the same $31. Both artists now see a permanently wrong number on their Money tab and in their history index (`idx.shows[].gross`), and Tom's tipper's private note is displayed in Maya's Studio. Neither can tell anything is wrong. With one artist this is unreachable; at a thousand it happens on the first busy Saturday.
evidence: Collision proven directly: `node -e` on the real export gave newShowId(2026-09-05T21:30:12Z) = '2026-09-05-2130' and newShowId(2026-09-05T21:30:49Z) = '2026-09-05-2130', collide: true. The absent filter is a read of _history.mjs:31-37 — the loop tests `s.payment_status`, `md.kind`, and `md.show`, an
fix_sketch: Two independent fixes, both wanted. (1) In moneyForShow's loop add the same guard revenue.mjs uses, before the show test: `if (md.artist && md.artist !== aid) continue;` and treat a session with no md.artist as unattributed rather than as this artist's. (2) Make showId unforgeable across tenants — `newShowId(now, aid)` returning `${aid}-${YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM}` or appending 4 random chars. Existing history keys are `hist_<aid>_<showId>` so they are already namespaced and old ids keep resolving; only the Stripe match string changes, and (1) alone makes it safe even for shows created before (2) lands.

title: The Studio code has no lockout and a 4-character minimum — and for every artist except the founder it silently does nothing
what_happens: Two problems in the same code path. (1) `requireArtist()` compares `sha(given)` against `ADMIN_CODE` and then against `show.codeHash` with no attempt counter, no lockout, no delay and no rate limit; `setCode` accepts any code of 4+ characters and stores an unsalted SHA-256. (2) The code branch is hard-wired to `getShow(DEFAULT_ARTIST)` and returns `{ aid: DEFAULT_ARTIST }`. `setCode` in admin.mjs writes `codeHash` into the CALLER's own show document, which is never read. So artist #2's Settings screen accepts a code, says it saved, and the code can never unlock anything.
failure_scenario: (1) Perry, on stage, sets his studio code to his year of birth. An attacker in the bar runs 10,000 GETs against `/api/stage?code=NNNN` from their phone. They get in, and now hold full owner rights on `perry-idyll`: they can tap `clearSetlist` and delete all 66 songs mid-gig, flip `windowOpen` off, change pack prices, end the show, and read `/api/revenue` — which returns every buyer's `customer_details.email` (revenue.mjs:57). Each guess also costs Perry one function invocation and one strong blob read. (2) Sam signs up, sets his studio code to 'sammy99' in Settings and gets a success toast. Next Friday his email code doesn't arrive (Resend delay, bad signal in the bar). He types 'sammy99' into "Unlock with code" and gets 401.
