Then: `Sam signs out, unlocks with HIS OWN code 'sammy99' -> [401, null]` and `Perry's code '8842' -> [200, 'perry-idyll']`. Brute force loop over
fix_sketch: Resolve the code against the artist being addressed, not DEFAULT_ARTIST — the Studio already knows the slug, so accept `?a=<slug>` on the code path and look up that artist's `show.codeHash` (keeping ADMIN_CODE as the founder's recovery key). Add a per-IP and per-artist failure counter in Blobs: 5 wrong codes locks the code path for 15 minutes and the response stays identical. Raise the minimum to 8 characters, salt the hash with the artist id, and until the per-artist lookup ships, hide the "Set a studio code" control for anyone who is not `isPlatformOwner`.

title: A failed show archive is silent and the very next line destroys the only copy of the night
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: archiveShow's two casDoc writes each end in `.catch(() => {})` (_history.mjs:117, :132), and admin.mjs wraps the whole call in `try { } catch { /* never block ending a show on the archive */ }` (:807). Two lines later, `newShow` resets show.log to [] inside the mutation (:1023) and carryFans/clearAllFanVotes wipe the shards (:1052-1053). failure_scenario: Perry finishes the 8pm set, taps "New show" before the 10pm set. The write to hist_perry-idyll_2026-09-01-2015 fails (hot key, transient Blobs error, or the casDoc loop exhausted). /api/admin returns 200 ok:true with no note. The show record is reset, the fan shards are carried/wiped, and the entire first set — nine songs, what each won with, the round-by-round record of what the room actually wanted, the head-count — is gone permanently. With `hist_`/`histidx_` writes forced to fail: `newShow response: {"status":200,"ok":true,"note":null}` / `history index rows after: 0` / `hist_ docs in the store: 0` / `fan votes after newShow: 0`. Healthy-store control (p
fix_sketch: Have archiveShow return a boolean (or throw) instead of swallowing, and read the hist doc back before returning true. In admin.mjs, gate the destruction on it: if the archive did not land, still let the artist end the show but do NOT wipe — set status/ended, leave show.log and the shards intact, and return a note ("Ended — but tonight's numbers didn't save; tap End again in a moment"), which is recoverable because archiveShow is already idempotent on showId. That preserves "nothing blocks ending a show" (INVARIANT 16) without trading it for permanent data loss.

title: ANSWER 2b — the polling backoff is defeated by a GLOBAL signature, so cost per fan RISES as the room gets bigger
what_happens: `signature()` (vote.html:627-632) is built from `updatedAt`, `totalVotes`, `nowPlaying.id`, `status`, `windowOpen`, the fan's own remaining credits and myAsks. Five of those seven are ROOM-WIDE. `totalVotes` changes when ANYONE in the bar votes, and `updatedAt` changes on every admin write. So one person voting resets QUIET to 0 on EVERY phone in the room, and the 3s→6s→12s ladder never climbs. The backoff works beautifully in an empty room and stops working precisely when the room fills up — which is the only time it matters. The result is superlinear: at 20 phones the effective interval settles around 6.2s; at 150 phones it collapses to 3.5s, so each phone makes 75% MORE calls than it did at 20. This is per-room, so it does not get worse at 1,000 artists — but it makes every big-venue gig disproportionately expensive, and big venues are exactly the accounts worth having.
failure_scenario: An artist on the $10 plan plays a 150-person venue on a Saturday. Two hours, busy room: my simulation gives 306,021 /api/show calls for that single gig — 13x the ~23,000 the same simulation gives for Perry's 20-person pub, for 7.5x the people. That one gig costs roughly 300–430 credits ($2–$3) against $10/month of revenue, before that artist plays their other seven gigs. The room feels great; the margin does not.
evidence: Simulated vote.html's actual state machine (QUIET counter, 3000/6000/12000 ladder, reset on any signature change) with signature-changing events generated from a global vote stream. 20 phones/busy: 23,343 calls, 1,167 per phone, 6.2s effective. 60 phones/busy: 95,770 calls, 1,596 per phone, 4.5s. 15
fix_sketch: Split the signature into two. Keep a FAST-reacting part that is genuinely about this phone — `credits.remaining`, `myAsks`, `nowPlaying.id`, `status`, `windowOpen` — and demote `totalVotes`/`updatedAt` to a SLOW part that is allowed to lag: e.g. only count as a change if the queue's top-3 song ids changed order, not if a vote count ticked. A fan cares that the running order moved, not that the number went 7→8. That alone should push the busy-room average from ~3.5–6s back toward 9–12s (a 2–3x cost cut) with no perceptible loss, because the thing they are watching — the order — still snaps instantly. Verify it by re-running the simulation against the new signature before deploying. Do NOT reach for a fixed slower interval; INVARIANT 9d is right that liveness matters.

The Studio confirms: "Everyone in the room can vote as much as they like." Forty people scan the QR. Every phone shows "∞" in the header and "Unlimited votes" in the green strip — and every single Vote button is greyed out at opacity .4 and does nothing when tapped. evidence: /tmp/msaudit/unl.mjs drives the real admin + show + vote handlers through test/register.mjs and feeds the real payload into a verbatim copy of `row()`. Room-wide: `credits {"unlimited":true,"remaining":null,...}` → `DISABLED vote buttons=3/3` (vs 0/3 with `freeCredits:3`), while `POST /api/vote -> {
fix_sketch: vote.html:383 → `const dis = !open || (!s.mine && !c.unlimited && c.remaining < cost);`, matching the shape already used at 396. Worth a regression test asserting `row()` produces zero `disabled` attributes for an `unlimited:true` payload. Related nit at 239: the optimistic path does `ST.credits.remaining += adding?-k:k`, so `null - 1 = -1` and `null + 1 = 1` — an unlimited fan who un-votes a song sees `1 < 1` = false and every button springs back to life for one poll cycle, then dies again.

title: Perry's premise is false: a vote on a losing song costs the fan nothing — credits refresh in full every round
what_happens: clearAllFanVotes() sets `bag[id].v = []; bag[id].ts = {}; bag[id].spent = 0` on every fan in all 12 shards, and it runs on every `play` and `playTop`. Because `remaining` is derived on read as `freeCredits + extra - creditsUsed(fan)`, wiping `v` and `spent` restores every fan to a full balance — whether they backed the winner, backed a loser, or held a 5-credit replay vote. There is no code path in which a vote on a song that did not get played costs a fan anything. Un-voting is separately free and unlimited while the window is open (vote.mjs:35, ahead of both the setlist gate and the credit check).
failure_scenario: Not a crash — a false premise that would drive a wrong build. Perry ships a 10-second lock-in countdown to stop fans 'wasting' votes. On the night, a fan holds a vote on 'Wish You Were Here' at 4 votes while 'Wonderwall' sits at 6. The countdown appears; they are now prevented from moving their vote. Perry starts Wonderwall. clearAllFanVotes runs and that fan's credit comes straight back anyway — it was never at risk. The countdown restricted them for nothing, and the one thing it did accomplish was to make the app feel like it was taking something away.
evidence: Ran the real handlers in-process (node --import ./test/register.mjs, /tmp/msaudit/credits.mjs and credits2.mjs). Fan f1 votes Delta → remaining=2, used=1. Artist starts Alpha (a song f1 never voted for) → f1 reads remaining=3, used=0, myVotes=[]. Winner-backer case: f5 votes Delta+Echo → remaining=3
fix_sketch: No code change to the mechanic — it is correct and INVARIANT 14 defends it. The fix is to stop building the countdown, and to tell the audience the truth (see next finding).

title: The audience UI presents refreshing credits as a depleting stock, and sells more at the moment of false scarcity
what_happens: vote.html:300 renders the credit pill as `${c.remaining}<small>/${c.total}</small>` — reading as "1/3", the universal shape of a consumable. vote.html:314 says "1 vote left". vote.html:383 disables the Vote button when `c.remaining < cost`. vote.html:245: on a 402 the page toasts "Out of votes — grab more below" and calls `openBuy()`. Nowhere in the file does any string tell the fan that votes come back when a song starts — I grepped vote.html and studio.html for refresh/reset/next song/each round and the only hits are the artist's own 'Reset votes' control and internal comments. The fan is given every signal that this is a scarce, spendable, purchasable resource, and no signal at all that it replenishes every four minutes for free.
failure_scenario: 10:40pm, twenty people in the bar. A fan votes for one song, sees '2/3', and stops — she is saving two votes for later in case something better comes up, exactly as Perry described. Two songs go by; her credits have silently refreshed twice and she has cast one vote all night. Another fan spends all three, gets 'Out of votes — grab more below' and the buy sheet, and pays $3 for something the app would have handed him free ninety seconds later. Both behaviours are rational responses to what the screen says. At 1000 artists this is not one confused fan — it is a systematic suppression of engagement in every room, and a purchase funnel that converts on a scarcity the server does not actually enforce.
evidence: grep over public/vote.html and public/studio.html for 'refresh|back when|next song|each round|per song|reset' returns no audience-facing copy about replenishment. Read vote.html:295-320 and 240-250 in full to confirm the exact strings. Cross-checked against the measured server behaviour in the previ
fix_sketch: One string, in the strip at public/vote.html:313: after `${c.remaining} vote${...} left`, append "— they come back when the next song starts". Optionally change the 402 toast at vote.html:245 from 'Out of votes — grab more below' to 'That is all three for this song — you get three more when the next one starts', and hold openBuy() for the fan who taps 'More votes' deliberately. Ship this before anything else in this area; it removes the motivation for the countdown entirely.

title: The artist-set Studio code is a silent no-op for every artist except the founding one — reintroducing the exact 2026-08-30 stage lockout
what_happens: admin.mjs:999-1003 `setCode` writes `show.codeHash` onto the CALLING artist's own show document. requireArtist (_lib.mjs:618-628) only ever consults `process.env.ADMIN_CODE` and `getShow(DEFAULT_ARTIST).codeHash` — it never looks at the show of the artist whose code was typed. So for artist #2 onward the code is stored, reported saved, and can never sign anybody in. studio.html:1533-1537 renders 'Your studio code' unconditionally for every artist, with the copy 'it works from any phone' and 'you can never lock yourself out' — the second half of which is meaningless for anyone who never had an ADMIN_CODE. Their only real recovery is an emailed 6-digit code, which needs RESEND_API_KEY set and inbox access.
failure_scenario: Sam signs up, opens Settings, sets his studio code to 'sam2026', gets the toast 'Saved — that's your code from now on'. Six weeks later his session token has expired (TOKEN_TTL is 30 days, _auth.mjs:143) or Perry has bumped artists.rev. Sam is on stage at 10pm, his own phone is at 3%, he borrows the bar owner's phone, opens myset.vip/studio and types sam2026. Measured: HTTP 401 {"ok":false,"error":"unauthorized"}. This is INVARIANT 15d's original incident, verbatim, for artists 2..1000.
evidence: Ran the real handlers against test/blobs-fake.mjs with ADMIN_CODE='perrys-recovery-code'. createArtist('sam@band.example') -> aid 'samreeves'. POST /api/admin {action:'setCode',code:'sam2026'} with Sam's Bearer token -> 200, and getShow('samreeves').codeHash is set. POST /api/admin {action:'window'}
fix_sketch: requireArtist cannot resolve an artist from a bare code without knowing who to look up, so the code has to carry identity: accept `code` only together with the slug already present in the Studio URL/localStorage (e.g. x-admin-artist), resolve the slug to an aid, and compare against THAT show's codeHash — keeping the ADMIN_CODE→DEFAULT_ARTIST branch as the platform recovery key. Until that exists, hide the 'Your studio code' section for any artist whose aid !== DEFAULT_ARTIST, or setCode must return an error rather than a success toast.

title: A poll landing mid-vote reverts the button, and the fan's re-tap cancels their own vote
what_happens: `vote()` applies an optimistic mutation to `ST` and renders (238-240), then POSTs. `load()` (228-234) assigns `ST=d` and re-renders on ANY successful poll response, with no knowledge of the in-flight mutation — `busy` guards re-entry into `vote()` but is never consulted by `load()`. So a poll that was already on the wire when the fan tapped lands with the pre-vote server state and repaints the button back to "Vote", the count back down, and the credit pill back up. Worse, line 248 is `busy.delete(id); load();` — `load()` is not awaited, so the re-entry guard is released while the screen still shows the reverted state. A second tap therefore passes the guard, reads `s.mine === false` from the stale `ST`, and sends a second /api/vote, which vote.mjs:36-37 correctly treats as a toggle-OFF (INVARIANT 15). There is also no sequencing on responses: two `load()`s can resolve out of order and the older payload wins.
failure_scenario: 10:40pm, a bar with ~400ms round trips. A fan taps Vote on "Wonderwall". The button says "Voted", the count goes to 4, the pill drops 3→2. About half a second later the queue snaps back: "Vote", 3 votes, 3 credits. She assumes the tap missed and taps again. Net result on the server: **no vote at all**, and her credit is back — she pressed Vote twice and has nothing. In the Studio, Perry's "Start top voted" names a different song than the one she was trying to push.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/race.mjs runs the verbatim `vote()`/`load()` from vote.html against the real show/vote handlers behind a 400ms-each-way fake network. Scenario 1 (poll on the wire, tap 120ms later): renders in order `btn=Voted votes=1 credits=4` → `btn=Vote votes=0 credits=5` → `btn=Voted votes=1 credit
fix_sketch: Two changes. (1) In `load()`, do not apply server state for songs in `busy` — merge the response but keep the optimistic `mine`/`votes`/`remaining` for any id with a POST in flight. (2) Move the guard release after reconciliation: `await load(); busy.delete(id);` at 248. Additionally give `load()` a monotonically increasing sequence number and drop any response older than the newest already applied, so a slow poll cannot overwrite a fresh one.

title: Card payments are on for every new artist by default and all of it lands in the founding artist's Stripe account — INVARIANT 0r has no enforcement anywhere in the code
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: `paymentsEnabled` is `!!process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` — a single global. defaultShow() ships DEFAULT_PACKS (3 votes/$3, 9/$7, 18/$11) to every artist. So the moment an account exists, that artist's audience page renders "More votes — From $3" and "Tip" buttons, /api/pay creates a live Checkout Session, and the money settles in the one STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. There is no per-artist payments switch, no Connect account, no ledger of what is owed to whom, and no line anywhere telling the artist or the fan whose account it is. INVARIANT 0r states the rule ("Do not onboard a second paying artist before Connect") but nothing in the code keeps it — it is a promise a human has to remember at signup time.
failure_scenario: Bravo Band signs up on Tuesday to try MySet at Thursday's gig. They never open the Payments section. On Thursday twelve people in the room buy vote packs and one tips $20 — $56 total. All of it lands in Perry's Stripe balance. Bravo's Money tab shows "All payments, all time $56.00" and "Refunds are done in your Stripe dashboard" — a dashboard they have no login for. The plan card next to it reads "10% cut on money taken", implying $50.40 is theirs, when in fact $0 is reachable. If someone asks for a refund, Bravo cannot issue it and Perry is the merchant of record for a transaction he had nothing to do with.
evidence: Ran show.mjs for a brand-new artist created through the real createArtist(), with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set (/tmp/newartist.mjs): `paymentsEnabled: true`, `packs: {"small":{"votes":3,"cents":300},"big":{"votes":9,"cents":700},"max":{"votes":18,"cents":1100}}` — the artist had touched no payment setting.
fix_sketch: Before artist #2: add `show.acceptsMoney` defaulting to FALSE for any artist whose aid !== DEFAULT_ARTIST, and gate `paymentsEnabled` in show.mjs and the kind checks in pay.mjs on it. That makes 0r structural instead of remembered — same move as 0x (venue as a separate registry rather than a permission check). Longer term it is Stripe Connect: store `stripeAccountId` per artist and pass `stripe_account`/`application_fee_amount`. Until then, artist B's room simply must not see a buy button.

title: `playable()`'s fallback never fires when a setlist is played out, so the last songs of every set leave the audience with an empty voting page and the Studio with no warning
what_happens: `playable()` decides the fallback on `narrowed.length` — how many songs in the set are still `active`. Being PLAYED does not clear `active`, so a fully played-through setlist still reports `narrowed.length > 0` and `fellBack:false`. But `show.mjs:37` then filters the public pool with `!show.played.includes(s.id)`, so the room's 'Up next'/'Vote for these' list is empty while the library still holds unplayed songs. INVARIANT 0aq exists precisely to stop 'a silently empty setlist discovered on stage at 10pm'; it guards the way a set empties by editing, and not the way a set actually empties on a gig night — by being played.
failure_scenario: Perry runs a 12-song 'First set'. By the end of set one he has played all 12. The audience page now reads: 'Up next — Nothing yet', then 'Vote for these — 0 songs — Everything's in the queue above' (vote.html:341-346), then 'Already played · 5 votes to hear again'. Forty people in the bar can now only spend 5 credits each on a replay; a fan on 3 free credits can do nothing at all. Perry's Live tab shows 'Pool is empty.' and 'Start top voted — nothing left' greyed out (studio.html:1086-1094) — with 54 unplayed songs sitting in his library. The Setlist tab shows no warnstrip, because `listFellBack` is false, so nothing tells him the set is the reason. He has to work out on stage that he must open the Setlist tab and switch to All songs.
evidence: Probe p1.mjs against the real handlers: 8-song library, 3-song active set, played all three. Result — `stage listFellBack = false`, `public queue songs = []`, `public played = ['Bravo@5','Alpha@5']`, and a direct `playTop` call returns `409 nothing left in the pool`. Independent second check by hand
fix_sketch: Make the fallback test what the room can actually be offered, not what is nominally in the set: compute `narrowed` and then check whether any of it is still unplayed (`narrowed.filter(s => !show.played.includes(s.id))`). If that is empty, fall back to the whole library with `fellBack:true` so the existing warnstrip fires — and give the strip a second message for this case ('You've played everything in "First set" — the room is seeing your whole library now'). `votable()` sits on top of `inPlay()` so played songs stay replayable either way; the change only widens what is offered when the set is exhausted.

title: The page sells votes while voting is paused, then tells the buyer to "vote away"
what_happens: The dock is hidden only when `ended` (375). When the artist merely pauses voting — `windowOpen:false`, the header toggle Perry uses between sets per INVARIANT 0p — the dock still renders "More votes · From $3" at full prominence, `openBuy()` works, and pay.mjs creates a live Stripe Checkout Session with no `status`/`windowOpen` guard at all (it checks only the pack and the artist). On return, `redeem()` fires confetti and toasts "3 extra votes added — vote away!" (591) — and `row()`'s `!open` term (383) has every Vote button disabled. The credits are not lost (they persist as `extra`), but the fan has paid for something they cannot use and been congratulated for it. Note the same page is careful about this elsewhere: `askCard` disables the request buttons with the accurate label "Voting is paused" (409-411).
failure_scenario: Perry pauses voting at 10pm while he plays three requests he already took. A fan who has run out of free votes taps "More votes — From $3", pays $7 for the 9-vote pack, comes back to confetti and "9 extra votes added — vote away!", and finds all 67 Vote buttons greyed out. Nothing on the page explains it except the strip reading "Voting paused", and nothing tells her when it reopens. She comes to the stage mid-song to ask for her money back. At 1000 artists, every one who uses the pause toggle the way it is designed generates these.
evidence: Read of vote.html:375-379 (dock hidden only on `ended`), 591 (the success copy), 383 (`dis = !open || …`), against pay.mjs:4-45 in full — the handler validates method, Stripe key, fan, artist and pack, and never reads `show.status` or `show.windowOpen`. Contrast with the correctly-guarded sibling at
fix_sketch: Client: when `!open && !ended`, keep the dock but disable the More votes button with the sub-label "Voting is paused" — same treatment as `askCard`. Server: in pay.mjs, refuse `kind:'votes'` when `show.status === 'ended'` (a hard error) and, for `!show.windowOpen`, either refuse or add it to the Checkout description so the buyer is not misled. Tips should stay available in both states — a tip is not contingent on the vote window.

title: Votes cast before the show starts are never cleared, so the first "Start top voted" of the night can be won by stuffing done days earlier
lenses: Fan identity & anti-abuse — how a person
what_happens: defaultShow sets `status: 'pre'` but `windowOpen: true` (_lib.mjs:103-104), and vote.mjs:15 refuses only `status === 'ended'` — so voting is open from the moment an account exists, before the artist has ever tapped anything. `resetVotes` is set only by `play`, `playTop`, the explicit `resetVotes` action and `newShow` (admin.mjs:890, 911, 1005, 1026). `case 'status'` (admin.mjs:915) — which is what "Start the show" fires — does not set it. So whatever accumulated during 'pre' is the tally the night opens with.
failure_scenario: On Tuesday afternoon someone puts 40 votes on 'Charlie' at myset.vip/perry-idyll — no show is live, nobody is watching, nothing logs it. Friday at 9pm Perry taps 'Start the show', looks at his Studio and sees Charlie: 40, Alpha: 1 in a room where two people have voted. He taps 'Start top voted' and opens his night with a song chosen by someone who was not there on a day he was not playing. He has no way to tell, and the archive will record Charlie as the night's biggest winner.
evidence: scratchpad/abuse.mjs: /api/show reported `status: pre, windowOpen: true`; 40 votes from ids 'pre0'..'pre39' on 'charlie' all succeeded; one genuine vote on 'alpha'; then `A('status',{status:'live'})` and the returned stagePayload showed `Charlie:40 Alpha:1`; `A('playTop')` returned `nowPlaying: 'cha
fix_sketch: Set `resetVotes = true` in `case 'status'` when the new status is 'live' and the old one was not — it is a one-word change and it is the same shape as what 'newShow' already does. Be careful to keep it on the transition only, so an artist tapping the live pill twice does not wipe a live round. (Deliberately NOT suggesting that voting be blocked before 'live' — a queue that fills while people arrive is a feature, and INVARIANT 16 says nothing should make the page look broken. Clearing at the transition keeps both.)

title: The service worker returns Netlify's raw error page to the room instead of the good copy of the app it is holding
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: The navigate branch treats only a *thrown* fetch as failure. `fresh.ok` is consulted solely to decide whether to cache (sw.js:62); line 63 then does `return fresh` unconditionally, so any 5xx, 502 or 503 is handed to the user verbatim even when a working copy of that exact page sits in `myset-runtime-v3`. The 'No connection' fallback at sw.js:65-71 is unreachable for HTTP errors.
failure_scenario: Mid-gig, a Netlify CDN or origin blip (or the tail of a deploy) makes myset.vip answer 502 for ten seconds. A fan whose phone dropped the page reloads and gets Netlify's grey 'Application error' page. So does the next one. The cache has a perfectly good vote.html for that URL and never serves it. This is precisely INVARIANT 16's failure mode — the setlist stops being readable — for a transient blip the SW was added to smooth over.
evidence: swsim.mjs, dispatching a navigation while the mocked network returns `new Response('Netlify error',{status:502})` after a successful navigation had already populated the cache. Output: `502 during a gig -> body: Netlify error | status 502`, with the cache still holding `https://myset.vip/perryidyll/
fix_sketch: In the navigate branch, treat `!fresh.ok && fresh.status >= 500` the same as a thrown fetch: `const hit = await caches.match(req); if (hit) return hit;` before returning `fresh`. Leave 4xx alone — a real 404 should still show as a 404.

title: A pending request at "New show" is silently destroyed with no refund — and it takes PURCHASED votes with it
what_happens: newShow assigns a fresh showId and calls carryFans(). Both shapeRequests and myRequests filter on showId, so unresolved rows vanish from the artist's panel and the fan's page at the same instant; nothing refunds them, and nothing tells either party. For free credits the loss is invisible because clearAllFanVotes/carryFans reset `spent` anyway. For PAID credits it is not: unspentPaid() (_lib.mjs:398-402) computes the carry as min(extra, total - creditsUsed(fan, show)), and creditsUsed includes fan.spent — so credits consumed by a request the artist never answered permanently reduce what the fan carries into the next show. INVARIANT 0ac is careful that a decline cannot MINT votes; the reverse direction, a request that is neither honoured nor declined, quietly destroys them.
failure_scenario: A fan buys the $3 pack (3 votes) plus more, ending with 9 purchased votes on top of 3 free. She spends 3 on songs that get played and 3 asking for a song that is not on the list. Perry never gets to it — the set ends, and next week he taps "↺ New show". Her 3 purchased votes for the unanswered request are gone: she carries 6 instead of 9. Her request row has disappeared from her screen, so there is nothing for her to point at, and it has disappeared from Perry's panel, so there is nothing for him to refund. She paid cash and the app quietly kept it.
evidence: Scratchpad probe11.mjs, real handlers: fan granted extra = 9 with freeCredits = 3 (total 12). After 3 song votes, credits.paidLeft = 9. After a 3-credit request, paidLeft = 6. Artist taps newShow with the request still pending -> /api/show reports credits.extra = 6 and myAsks = []. Separately (probe
fix_sketch: Fold this into the newShow sweep from the previous finding: before carryFans() runs, walk the requests document for rows still `pending` on the outgoing showId and refund each one through the same resolveRequest('declined') path (which already clamps at zero and is replay-safe), marking them 'expired' so the fan's page can say "Not tonight — votes refunded" if they are still on it. Order matters the same way INVARIANT 17c states for archiveShow: refund before carryFans, or the spend has already been folded into the carry.

title: Switching requests off strands a fan's pending row: it disappears from their phone while their credits stay spent, and the later refund is silent
what_happens: show.mjs:59-61 gates the myAsks read on `asking = show.requests.on || show.birthdays.on` — an optimisation to keep a second blob read off the hot path. But the flag also controls whether a fan who ALREADY has a row in flight can see it. When the artist flips both switches off (askSet, admin.mjs:986), the payload returns asks:{song:null,birthday:null} and myAsks:[], and askCard (vote.html:394-395) bails out entirely on `if(!A.song && !A.birthday && !mine.length) return ''`. The whole card vanishes — including the row that says what the fan paid for and what its status is. Their credits.used still shows the spend, so their vote count is lower with nothing on screen to explain it. If the artist then declines, the refund lands but the fan never sees "Not tonight — votes refunded". The artist's own list still shows the row, so the two views now disagree.
failure_scenario: Half an hour into the set the requests are piling up faster than Perry can play them, so he goes to Settings and switches "Request a song" off — a completely reasonable thing to do on stage. Three fans are mid-wait with 3 credits each committed. Their "Waiting on Perry" rows disappear on the next poll. All three now see 0 of 3 votes left, no queue entry, and nothing on the page acknowledging the request they just paid for. One of them walks up to the stage to ask about it, which is the moment this app is supposed to prevent.
evidence: Scratchpad probe10.mjs, real handlers. With requests on: payload asks = {song:{cost:3}, birthday:null}, myAsks = ['pending'], credits.used = 3; artist's askList shows the row as pending. After A('askSet',{kind:'song',on:false}): payload asks = {song:null, birthday:null}, myAsks = [], credits.used st
fix_sketch: Keep the hot-path optimisation but widen the condition so an in-flight row is never hidden. The cheapest correct version is to have show.mjs read myAsks when `asking || fan has ever asked this show` — e.g. stamp a boolean on the fan record when createRequest succeeds and clear it when their last row resolves, so the extra blob read is still off the poll for the 95% of fans who never ask. vote.html:404-406 already has the copy for this case ("Requests are closed now, but here's what you asked for"), which is good evidence this was the intent and only the server-side gate is too narrow.

title: The whole audience page is torn down and rebuilt on every poll, whether anything changed or not
what_happens: `load()` calls `render()` unconditionally on any `d.ok` (232), and `render()` ends with `$('#app').innerHTML = h` (354) — a full DOM replacement of the header, queue, search box, sort bar, genre bar and all 67 song rows, plus re-binding every listener. Nothing compares the new payload to the old, even though `signature()` (627-632) already computes exactly the value that would gate it and is only used for the poll backoff. Two consequences. The cheap one: a phone in a quiet room rebuilds the entire page ~17 times in 2 minutes for byte-identical content. The expensive one: when the content genuinely changes, every row moves. On a song start the "Up next" card collapses from 3 rows to a one-line empty card and every row in "Vote for these" shifts up a slot, so a finger that went down on one song's Vote button lifts onto a different song's — including, potentially, a 5-credit replay button in the "Already played" section that did not exist a moment earlier.
failure_scenario: A fan's finger is on the Vote button for "Delta", fourth in the list. In that same 150ms, Perry taps "Start top voted" on stage and a poll response that was already on the wire lands. "Up next" empties, everything slides up three rows, and her finger lifts on the button now occupying those pixels — "Bravo". She has voted for a song she did not choose, and spent a credit doing it. She has no idea it happened; the button she was looking at is now somewhere else on screen. `wakeUp()` (645) reschedules the *next* poll on pointerdown, which helps, but does nothing about a response already in flight.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/startrace.mjs, real handlers, three fans building a queue of alpha/bravo/charlie: before `playTop`, the vote list is `[delta, echo, foxtrot]`; immediately after, it is `[bravo, charlie, delta, echo, foxtrot]` — slot 1 delta→bravo, slot 2 echo→charlie, slot 3 foxtrot→delta, all marked DI
fix_sketch: Cheapest correct fix: in `load()`, compute `signature()` on the incoming payload and skip `render()` when it matches the last rendered one — the function already exists and already captures every field the page displays that changes (add `songs.map(s=>s.id+':'+s.votes+(s.mine?'m':'')).join()` so per-song changes are covered). That kills the pointless rebuilds outright and shrinks the mis-target window to genuine changes only. Then, for the real-change case, either key the rows and patch in place, or suppress the render while a pointer is down (`pointerdown`/`pointerup` flag) and apply it on release. As a bonus this also fixes the search caret being forced to the end of the string at line 364.

title: Before the artist taps "Start the show" the room is told "● Live" and "Voting paused" with every button dead — while the Studio insists "Voting is open · Audience can vote right now"
lenses: Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: vote.html:279 computes `open = windowOpen && !ended && !pre`, but the header sub-line (296-298) only special-cases `ended` — for `pre` it renders a pulsing dot and the word "Live". The strip (312-314) then reports the *reason* as "Voting paused", which is not what is happening: `windowOpen` is true; the show simply has not started. The Studio's Settings row (studio.html:1415-1416) reads straight off `s.windowOpen` and says "Voting is open — Audience can vote right now". Both surfaces are confidently wrong in opposite directions. (The Live tab does say "Nothing says 'live' to the audience until you tap this", which is the only honest label in the loop.)
failure_scenario: 8pm, first fans scan the QR captioned "Choose the next song". They tap through the profile page and land on: "● Live · The Ugly Duckling", credits 3/3, and a full setlist where every Vote button is greyed out, explained only by "Voting paused". They wait, tap a few dead buttons, and put the phone away. Perry, glancing at Settings, sees "Voting is open" and has no idea. His head-count for the night is also zero, because markPresence only stamps while status==='live'.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/render.mjs case B, real payload with status 'pre' and windowOpen true: `HEADER SUB : ● Live · The Ugly Duckling` / `STRIP : Voting paused · 3 votes left` / `POOL : Alpha[Vote DISABLED] Bravo[Vote DISABLED] Charlie[Vote DISABLED]`.
fix_sketch: Give `pre` its own copy on both surfaces. Header: "Starting soon" with an outlined dot, not "Live". Strip: "Voting opens when the set starts" rather than "Voting paused". In the Studio, gate the Settings voting row on status — when status!=='live' it should read "Voting opens when you start the show".

title: Holding a vote at the moment the show ends silently destroys paid credits
what_happens: `unspentPaid(fan, show)` = `min(extra, total - creditsUsed)` (_lib.mjs:400-402). It charges the fan's current in-flight votes against their PAID balance rather than their free one. `carryFans` (_lib.mjs:409) then carries only that reduced figure into the next show and discards the rest. So the exact same act — holding a vote — is free during the show (clearAllFanVotes refunds it) but destructive at the moment the artist ends it, and only for the paid portion. This is the one and only way a fan can actually lose something by voting, and it fires on an event they cannot see coming.
failure_scenario: 11:48pm. A fan bought the 9-vote pack earlier, has 12 credits, and casts a 5-credit 'play it again' on Wonderwall right as the last song is winding down. Perry taps '↺ New show' (or sets status ended). `carryFans` runs: unspentPaid = min(9, 12-5) = 7. Her `extra` goes from 9 to 7. Two votes she paid cash for are gone, with no message, no refund, and no way for her to know it happened — and if she had simply not voted in that final minute she would have kept all nine. Measured exactly: extra 9 → 7 after 'New show' while holding one 5-cost vote.
evidence: Ran /tmp/msaudit/endshow.mjs against the real handlers: granted extra=9 (paidLeft=9), cast a 5-cost replay vote → paidLeft drops to 7 immediately, then `A('newShow')` → total=10, extra=7, remaining=10. Confirmed by reading _lib.mjs:398-417 — `unspentPaid` deducts the whole of creditsUsed from `extra
fix_sketch: In `unspentPaid`, charge in-flight votes against FREE credits first: `Math.max(0, Math.min(extra, extra - Math.max(0, creditsUsed(fan, show) - (show.freeCredits || 0))))`. That preserves the invariant that paid credits carry (5c's spirit) and makes end-of-show consistent with every other round boundary, where holding a vote costs nothing. Worth confirming against the intended model in the previous finding first — if `extra` becomes properly consumable, this maths changes shape.

title: An offline vote is silently dropped while the screen says it worked, and the toast promises a retry that does not exist
what_happens: Three things compound. (1) `vote()`'s catch at 247 toasts "Connection hiccup — retrying" — nothing retries; the function just falls through to `busy.delete(id); load()`. (2) `load()`'s catch at 233 is empty and `render()` is only called inside `if(d.ok)`, so a failed poll leaves the optimistic mutation on screen indefinitely: the button stays "Voted", the count stays incremented, the pill stays decremented, and the server has nothing. (3) `tick()` at 642 scores a failed fetch as "nothing changed" (the signature is computed from an unchanged `ST`), so `QUIET` climbs and the poll backs off to 12s exactly when connectivity is the problem. There is no `navigator.onLine` handling, no `online` listener, no staleness indicator anywhere — `updatedAt` is in the payload but is only fed to `signature()` (629), never shown.
failure_scenario: A fan steps out to the smoking area at the back of the bar where the wifi does not reach. She taps Vote on "Champagne Supernova". The button turns red and says "Voted", the count goes up, her pill goes 3→2, and a toast says "Connection hiccup — retrying". Nothing was sent and nothing will be. She comes back inside four minutes later; the page has been showing a frozen, live-looking room the whole time (red pulsing dot, "Playing now: Hallelujah" — the song ended three songs ago) with no indication anything is wrong, and the poll has parked itself at 12s. When it finally succeeds her vote silently evaporates and the pill goes back to 3.
evidence: /tmp/msaudit/offline.mjs runs the verbatim `vote()`/`load()` with a throwing fetch: `before tap : button="Vote" votes=0 pill=3/3` → toast → `after tap : button="Voted" votes=1 pill=2/3`, server got nothing, and reading the function confirms the only occurrence of "retry" is inside the toast string.
fix_sketch: Have `load()` return success/failure and let `tick()` distinguish them: on failure, do not increment `QUIET` — hold or shorten the interval and count consecutive failures. After 2 failures render a small "Reconnecting…" chip in the header (that also satisfies INVARIANT 16's spirit — the setlist stays readable, it just stops pretending to be live). In `vote()`, on a network error revert the optimistic mutation immediately and toast "Couldn't send that — tap again" (honest), or queue one real retry.

title: A lazily-loaded tab caches its own failure forever — the Gigs tab then states, falsely, that the artist has no gigs booked
lenses: public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: loadGigs/loadHist/loadPlan/loadTeam/loadRev/loadPitches all guard with `if(X && !force) return;` and then assign `X = await api(...)`. On failure api() returns the truthy object `{ok:false,error:'Connection hiccup — try again'}`, so the cache is now populated with a failure and the guard blocks every subsequent attempt. Nothing resets these on tab switch — grep shows EVENTS is only set back to null inside saveGig2 (950) and hideGig (984), i.e. only after a successful gig WRITE. The Gigs render at 1161 does `if(!EVENTS) …Loading… else { const occ = EVENTS.occurrences || []; … }`, so a failed EVENTS is treated as a successful empty calendar. loadProf is the one that gets this right — it uses raw fetch with `.catch(()=>null)`, so null lets it retry.
failure_scenario: Sound-check, 7:50pm. Perry opens the Studio and taps Gigs while the venue's wifi is still flaky. The eventList call fails once. The tab renders "Coming up — 0" and "Nothing booked yet. Tap 'Add a gig' — a weekly residency only needs entering once." His four-nights-a-week residency looks deleted. He switches to Live and back to Gigs: identical, because EVENTS is truthy. He does it five more times. The only ways out are a full page reload or adding a gig — and he is now half-convinced his calendar (which also feeds his public page and the city feed) has been wiped. The same shape hits the Money tab (a failed /history renders an empty `head` with no message at all) and Settings ("Your plan" and "Who can sign in" spin forever).
evidence: Code trace of the guard plus `grep -n "EVENTS=null"` → only lines 410 (declaration), 950 and 984. Confirmed against the render branch: `EVENTS.occurrences` is undefined on a failure object, `occ` becomes [], `up` becomes [], and the `.join('')||` fallback at 1202 emits the "Nothing booked yet" strin
fix_sketch: One line each: `const r = await api(...); if(r && r.ok) EVENTS = r;` — never cache a failure. Then render three distinct states rather than two: not-loaded (spinner), loaded-and-empty ("Nothing booked yet"), and failed ("Couldn't load your gigs — tap to retry"). "I have no data" and "you have no gigs" must never render as the same sentence.

title: The documented service-worker escape hatch has no caller anywhere in the app
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: sw.js:40-47 listens for a `myset-unregister` message and, on receiving it, unregisters and wipes every cache. INVARIANT 0ax and MYSET.md both describe this as the escape hatch. A repo-wide grep for the string `myset-unregister` across public/ and netlify/ returns exactly one hit — the listener itself. No page ever calls `navigator.serviceWorker.controller.postMessage('myset-unregister')`, and there is no URL parameter, no hidden Settings control and no console instruction that would trigger it.
failure_scenario: The failure this is documented to solve is 'the worker is serving something wrong to somebody standing in a bar'. In that moment Perry has no way to fire it. Deploying a new page that posts the message works only for the SWs that already carry this handler, and needs a production deploy (15 Netlify credits, INVARIANT 9d0) in the middle of a gig. Worse, the invariant reads as if the hatch is armed, so the next person to reason about a stale-app incident will believe there is a lever to pull and lose time discovering there isn't. Right now the only real recovery for a fan is 'clear your browser data' — the exact instruction 0ax was written to make unnecessary.
evidence: `grep -rn 'myset-unregister' public netlify *.md` returns three lines: public/sw.js:41 (the listener), INVARIANTS.md:521 and MYSET.md:499 (the two claims). No caller. Cross-checked by grepping all of public/*.html for `postMessage` in a service-worker context — nothing.
fix_sketch: Wire it: on every page, `if (new URLSearchParams(location.search).has('swreset') && navigator.serviceWorker.controller) navigator.serviceWorker.controller.postMessage('myset-unregister')`. Then myset.vip/perryidyll/vote?swreset is something Perry can say out loud into a microphone. Add a Settings > Advanced button in the Studio for his own device. If it stays unwired, soften 0ax to say the handler exists but is not reachable.

title: app.css is stale-while-revalidate with no version stamp, so the first load after any deploy pairs new HTML with the previous stylesheet
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: The STATIC branch (sw.js:78-87) returns the cached copy immediately and refreshes behind it. Every page that uses app.css links it bare — `href="/app.css"`, no `?v=` on any of the five (verified by script). The cache key is the URL, so a deploy that changes app.css cannot produce a new key: load N after the deploy gets the NEW HTML off the network (navigation is network-first) with the OLD CSS out of the cache. Only load N+1 is consistent. Note that without the SW this skew could not happen at all — Netlify serves these with `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so plain HTTP caching would revalidate both together.
failure_scenario: Perry ships a fix during the break — say a rename or a new class on the voting page's queue rows. A fan already in the bar pulls to refresh: they get the new vote.html markup styled by yesterday's app.css. Unstyled or half-styled queue rows on a phone in a dark bar read as 'the app is broken', and they will not reload a second time to find out it isn't. INVARIANT 0an is the record of how easily a class name changes underneath this file.
evidence: Read the STATIC branch: `const hit = await caches.match(req)` is returned before the network promise resolves whenever a cached entry exists, and the entry is keyed on the unversioned URL. Confirmed by script that no HTML file in public/ references app.css with any query string: `app.css referenced
fix_sketch: Cheapest correct fix: stamp the link — `/app.css?v=<build>` — in the five HTML files whenever the CSS changes, which makes it a new cache key and eliminates the skew. Alternative: make CSS network-first with a cache fallback like navigations, accepting one extra revalidation per load. Either is fine; the current pairing of unversioned URL with SWR is the thing that cannot be.

title: /api/show keeps naming the setlist after it has fallen back, so the room's header says "Set A" while the Studio's warnstrip says the opposite
lenses: Mid-show setlist changes — what the serv
what_happens: show.mjs:35 already destructures `fellBack` from `playable(show)`, but line 73 emits `setlist: show.listId ? { name: show.listName } : null` — testing only that a list is *selected*, not that it is actually narrowing anything. When the active set resolves to nothing, `playable()` falls back to the whole library and reports `fellBack:true`; `stage.mjs:42` passes that to the Studio, which renders "Nothing votable in that set. The room is seeing your whole library instead." But `/api/show` still ships the set's name, and vote.html:298 renders it into the audience header. The two surfaces state opposite things about the same moment. INVARIANT 0aq is explicit that the first version's sin was hiding the fallback from the place it needed to be visible; here it is visible in the Studio and actively contradicted on the audience's phone.
failure_scenario: Perry taps into his "Late set" and, still tidying, empties it (or hides its last remaining song). His Studio shows the amber warnstrip and he knows the room is on the whole library. Every phone in the bar reads **"Live · The Ugly Duckling · Late set"** while listing all 40 of his songs. Somebody asks him why the late set has forty songs in it. Measured: after `listSongs {id:L, songs:[]}`, `stage.listFellBack` was `true` and every song went `votable:true`, while `/api/show` returned `setlist={"name":"Set A"}` alongside the full six-song library. Harmless to the mechanics, but it is the app telling the room something untrue about the artist's own set, and it is the sort of thing he only discovers when a customer points at it.
evidence: Scenario 2, executed twice (emptied via `listSongs([])` and via three successive `listToggle`s). Both produced the same payload: `[after empty] stage listId=leddokkw name="Set A" fellBack=true` with `/api/show setlist={"name":"Set A"} songs=alpha:1 bravo:1 charlie:1 delta:0 echo:0 foxtrot:0` — six s
fix_sketch: One line, using a value already in scope: `setlist: show.listId && !fellBack ? { name: show.listName } : null` at show.mjs:73. The audience header then falls back to "Live · The Ugly Duckling", which is true. Worth an assertion in test/e2e.mjs beside the existing fallback cases, since this is the second time a fallback has been reported honestly in one place and not another.

title: After "End the show" the voting page still shows a live PLAYING NOW hero with animated equalizer bars — all week
lenses: Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: The hero at vote.html:303 branches only on `d.nowPlaying`; the `ended` check lives in the else-branch (line 310) and is therefore unreachable whenever a song is set. `status:'ended'` (admin.mjs:915-916) never clears `show.nowPlaying`, and nothing else does until `newShow`.

Anyone still on the page — and anyone who opens it at any point during the following week — sees the header say "That's a wrap — thanks for coming" directly above a full pink gradient card reading "● PLAYING NOW / Tennessee Whiskey" with four bars bouncing and a working Lyrics button. title: Fans who bought votes and never came back are counted as phones in the room on every subsequent night, and archived into the numbers venues see
what_happens: carryFans (_lib.mjs:404-418) rewrites a surviving fan record as `{v:[], ts:{}, extra:carry, gifted}` — deliberately dropping `seenShow` and `ipH` so the presence stamp is fresh for the new show. But roomCounts (_lib.mjs:522-535) treats `f.extra > 0` as proof of presence: `const here = !!f.seenShow || (f.v||[]).length > 0 || f.extra > 0 || f.spent > 0`. So a carried record satisfies the heuristic with no stamp. That number is `stage.mjs:21`'s on-stage head-count, `_history.mjs:91`'s archived `stats.room`, the `room` column of the history index, and — via _vstats.mjs:56 `s.room ?? s.peakVoters` — the people-count a venue sees for every night and every act.
failure_scenario: Friday: three people in the room, one of them buys the 9-vote pack and spends 4. Saturday, before the doors open, Perry taps 'New show'. The Studio's head-count reads 1 person in the room with nobody there. If Saturday is quiet — say six real phones — it archives as 7, and the Ugly Duckling's venue dashboard reports 7 people for that night forever. The inflation persists every night until that fan spends the credits, and compounds across regulars: ten people carrying unspent packs is a permanent +10 on every future night's head-count, in exactly the number INVARIANT 0aj calls 'the single biggest reason a bar signs up'.
evidence: Measured against the real handlers. Three fans polled /api/show?in=1 and voted; one was given extra:9. stage.mjs reported room = 3. Then POST /api/admin {action:'newShow'} and, with nobody polling, stage.mjs reported room = 1. Dumping the shards showed the single survivor: {"p1":{"v":[],"ts":{},"ext
fix_sketch: Presence should mean presence. Pass the current showId into roomCounts and count a record only when `f.seenShow === show.showId` or it has activity in THIS show (`v.length || spent`). `extra > 0` alone was a proxy for legacy records that predate the stamp; scope it to records with no `seenShow` field at all, or drop it now that markPresence has been shipping for a while.

title: An accidental End followed by Start silently reverts a setlist the artist switched by hand mid-gig
what_happens: `autoList` is resolved on every `status:'live'` (admin.mjs:834), not only on the first one, and applied unconditionally after the mutation. There is no memory of whether tonight's gig list was already applied, and no check for whether the artist has since chosen a different one. So the second and every subsequent 'Start the show' re-applies the calendar's `listId` over whatever is currently selected.
failure_scenario: Perry's Thursday residency in the calendar points at his 'Early set'. He taps Start at 8pm and gets the toast 'Playing your "Early set" tonight — 12 songs.' At 10pm the room has gone rowdy so he switches to his 'Late set' from the Setlist tab. At 10:20 he fat-fingers '■ End the show', confirms, then taps '● Start the show' to get back. The setlist snaps back to 'Early set' — the twelve loud songs vanish from every phone in the room mid-round, and the only warning is a toast on a phone he is not holding. Fans holding votes on Late-set songs keep them (they can still un-vote, per INVARIANT 15) but those songs are no longer in the payload.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle6.mjs with a real gig saved 90 minutes out pointing at list l1: `Start the show -> listId l6b1ka7b (Early set)` → `artist switches by hand -> listId lefo0lfn (Late set)` → after `status:'ended'` then `status:'live'`: `listId l6b1ka7b | note: Playing your "Early set" tonight — 2 s
fix_sketch: Stamp the show when a gig's list has been applied — e.g. `show.autoListFor = <occurrenceKey>` — and skip the `autoList` block at admin.mjs:834 when that key already matches. That also makes the auto-apply survive an accidental end without fighting the artist.

title: The audience page hard-codes "Perry" in every payment string and in the page title, so artist B's room is told to tip Perry
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: vote.html renders the artist's real name from the API in the header, but every payment-related string is a literal. The sheet heading is "Tip Perry", the lede is "100% goes to Perry. Add a note and he'll see it on stage.", failures say "grab Perry between songs" and "show Perry your receipt", the success toast says "your $X tip reached Perry", the disabled-payments label says "Ask Perry", and the document title/meta description are "Vote the setlist — Perry Idyll" / "Vote on what Perry Idyll plays next." pay.mjs by contrast does this correctly — it interpolates `show.artist` into the Stripe line item.

title: The starter setlist silently switches 12 of its 62 songs off on the free plan and tells the artist nothing
lenses: Multi-tenancy: the night MySet has more
what_happens: STARTER_SONGS has 62 entries; the free plan's `featured` cap is 50. The starterSetlist case adds all 62 but flips `active:false` on everything past the cap — and unlike the addSong case directly above it (which sets `note = 'Added, but switched off — your plan features N at a time.'`), starterSetlist never sets a note. The handler returns `{ok:true, stage, note:null}`, so the Studio shows nothing. This breaks the second half of INVARIANT 0s0: "a new song still saves — it just arrives switched off, AND SAYS SO."
failure_scenario: Bravo Band signs up on the afternoon of their first gig and taps the one button offered to a blank account: "Start with a covers setlist." 62 songs appear. Twelve of them — Blackbird, Imagine, Simple Man, Free Fallin' among them, the tail of the list — are greyed out with no explanation. At the gig someone asks for Blackbird, the artist looks at their phone, sees it there but off, and does not know whether that is a bug, a setting, or the plan. The first thing a new artist learns about MySet is that it does things to their setlist without saying so.
evidence: Ran the real admin handler for a fresh artist on the free plan (/tmp/two.mjs): `songs added: 62 active: 50 switched off: 12 | note returned to the artist: null`. Confirmed STARTER_SONGS.length === 62 with 62 unique slugs, and PLANS.free.featured === 50 at _plan.mjs:29. Compare admin.mjs:965 where ad

Worth also reconsidering whether a 62-song pack should be handed to a plan that features 50.

title: A purchase that completes after the artist taps New show is counted in neither night's history, and nothing tells the artist to re-reconcile
what_happens: admin.mjs:802-807 archives the finished show synchronously at the moment New show / status:ended is tapped, and archiveShow:92 computes moneyForShow right there. A Checkout Session created during that show but completed a minute or two later does not exist as a paid session yet, so it is absent from the archive. It can never appear later either: moneyForShow:36 does `if (md.show && md.show !== showId) continue`, so the next show excludes it by tag, and the unattributed bucket at line 37 only catches sessions with NO md.show — so nothing flags it. The fan does get their votes (redeemSession runs on its own path, and carryFans creates a fresh record), so this is a reporting loss, not a delivery loss.
failure_scenario: Perry's last song of set one ends at 00:58. A punter taps 'More votes' at 00:58, fumbles Apple Pay, and the charge completes at 01:01. Perry tapped 'New show' at 01:00 to start the second set. Set one's archived gross is $7 when it should be $18; set two's is $0 for that sale; the show detail page reports unattributed $0, so there is no warning. The Re-check the money in Stripe button (studio.html:1250) fixes it — I confirmed moneyForShow's +1h `lte` slack means a later reconcile does pick it up — but Perry has no reason to ever tap it, and 'what did Thursday make' is the number he will quote to the venue.

fix_sketch: Cheapest fix: have redeemSession, when md.show is present and that showId is already archived, call reconcileShow(aid, md.show) — the function already exists in _history.mjs:145 and is idempotent, and this makes late money self-heal with no artist action. Second, make it visible rather than silent: record `reconciledAt` (already on the money block, _history.mjs:18) in the history row and show a 'money last checked N hours ago' line under the gross. Optionally delay the archive's money pull by re-running it once ~10 minutes after the show ends.

title: When the webhook wins the race, the paying fan gets a flat 'Already added' instead of the confetti moment they paid for
what_happens: checkout.session.completed fires from Stripe essentially the instant payment succeeds, which is the same instant the browser starts its redirect to success_url. It is a genuine coin-flip which arrives first. When the webhook wins, redeemSession's line-14 early-out returns {already:true}, and vote.html:590 gates confetti and the '18 extra votes added' toast on `!d.already`, so the returning buyer gets the consolation branch at line 591: 'Already added — you're all set'.

Roughly half the time — with the webhook correctly configured, which is the state Perry wants — she gets a small grey toast reading 'Already added — you're all set' and no confetti, having just spent $11 at a bar. The paid moment is the product's whole conversion loop, and it is the path that works properly which degrades it.
evidence: Measured the ordering: two concurrent redeemSession calls for one session returned {granted:9} to the winner and {already:true, granted:9} to the loser (scratchpad t/pay1.mjs, section A). Traced the client gate at vote.html:590 — confetti/buzz/toast are inside `if(!d.already)`, and the `else if(loud
fix_sketch: The `already` flag exists to keep the silent background retry quiet, not to mute the return trip. In handleReturn's branch, celebrate whenever the session id came from the URL: pass a flag through redeem() so `?paid=` always fires confetti and the granted toast, and let only the pendingGet() retry path use the muted 'Already added' copy. Pair it with finding 5's fix so the celebration is driven by the balance the phone actually has.

title: Thirty throwaway fan ids permanently jam the request queue for the whole room
what_happens: `MAX_PENDING = 30` is a GLOBAL cap on open requests per show, while the per-fan guard (`mineOpen.some(r => r.kind === kind)`) is scoped to a fan id the caller invents. Since every fresh fan id arrives with `show.freeCredits` free credits (finding 3), and a request costs 3 by default, each throwaway id buys exactly one request for nothing. Thirty ids fill the queue; the cap only clears when the artist manually resolves rows.
failure_scenario: Requests are switched on. Someone in the bar posts 30 requests from 30 invented fan ids in about two seconds, each titled with whatever they want the artist to read on stage. Every genuine punter for the rest of the night gets `429 There are a lot of requests in already — try again in a bit` — a message that reads as a MySet failure, not an attack. Perry's Requests panel on stage is 30 rows of the troll's text, and clearing it means 30 taps of the ✕ button between songs.
evidence: scratchpad/probe7.mjs against the real request.mjs and admin.mjs handlers, with requests switched on at cost 3. Output: `requests planted from 40 throwaway fan ids: 30 | then: [429, 'There are a lot of requests in already — try again in a bit']`; then `a REAL fan now gets: 429`; and `artist's Reques
fix_sketch: Two changes. Cap open requests per hashed IP (2-3) as well as per fan id — `roomHash()` already exists and stores no address. And add a bulk "Decline all" to the Studio's request panel so the recovery on stage is one tap, not thirty, since INVARIANT 16 says nothing may break the gig and thirty taps between songs effectively does.

title: The featured-song cap is applied silently: the starter pack switches songs off without a word, and the add-a-song warning is overwritten by a generic toast two network calls later
lenses: public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: Two separate holes in INVARIANT 0s0 ("a new song still saves — it just arrives switched off, AND SAYS SO"). (a) The starter pack is 62 songs and the free cap is 50, so 12 arrive `active:false` — and `starterSetlist` returns `note: null`, so act()'s `if(d.note) toast(d.note)` at 749 fires nothing at all. (b) addSong DOES return the right note, and saveSongSheet toasts it at 1880 — but then awaits chartSet, awaits load(), and calls `toast('Added to your setlist')` at 1891. toast() overwrites textContent and resets its own timer, so the warning is replaced by a message that says the opposite.
failure_scenario: A new free-tier artist — one of the thousand this is supposed to serve — signs up an hour before their first gig, taps "+ Starter pack", confirms "Add around 60 well-known covers to your setlist? Nothing you already have is touched." and gets no message whatsoever. Twelve of their songs are hidden from the room. They then add one of their own originals through the song sheet; for about a second the toast reads "Added, but switched off — your plan features 50 at a time", then it is replaced by "Added to your setlist" while they are still typing the chart. The overwrite is a straight read of saveSo
fix_sketch: In admin.mjs's starterSetlist case, count how many landed switched off and set the note (`"Added 62 — 12 of them switched off, because your plan features 50 at a time."`). In saveSongSheet, make the final toast `toast(d.note || (id?'Saved':'Added to your setlist'))` and drop the early one, so the cap message is the message that survives. Longer term, a plan-limit message deserves the warnstrip treatment (like listFellBack), not a 3-second toast.

title: A buyer whose fan id changes between checkout and return is told '18 extra votes added' and receives none — the fallbackFan recovery hook exists but can never fire, and the artist has no tool to fix it
what_happens: _pay.mjs:17 is `const who = cleanFanId(md.fan) || cleanFanId(fallbackFan)`. md.fan is stamped by pay.mjs:38 at session-create time and is always present, so the fallbackFan branch is unreachable — the parameter confirm.mjs:14 goes to the trouble of reading from the query string is dead code. But confirm.mjs is the ONE place in the system that knows the buyer's identity RIGHT NOW (vote.html:585 sends &fan=FAN from the returning browser), and the session id in success_url is a bearer secret only the buyer's browser ever sees. Meanwhile vote.html:589-591 fires confetti and toasts `${d.granted} extra votes added` using the server's granted count, not the phone's actual balance, so the page cheerfully confirms a delivery to a device that got nothing. There is no artist-side recovery: admin.mjs has no 'grant N votes to fan X' action, and unlimitedFan (admin.mjs:927) is wired in studio.html:1428 to myFanId() only — the artist's own phone.
failure_scenario: A fan opens the table QR inside Instagram's in-app browser (fan id fanWEBVIEW in that webview's localStorage) and buys the $11 / 18-vote pack. Her bank's 3DS step bounces her out to Safari, which is a different storage jar with a fresh fan id. Safari lands on /vote.html?paid=cs_x, calls /api/confirm, gets {ok:true, granted:18}, throws confetti and says '18 extra votes added — vote away!'. She taps a song and is told she has no credits. Perry's Money tab shows the payment green-ticked and delivered. The same thing happens to anyone browsing in Private mode, or who scans the QR from a second app later in the night.
evidence: Ran the real confirm.mjs and show.mjs handlers. Session metadata.fan = 'fanWEBVIEW', request /api/confirm?session_id=cs_x&fan=fanSAFARI. confirm returned {ok:true,kind:'votes',granted:18,fan:'fanWEBVIEW'}. /api/show?fan=fanSAFARI then returned credits {remaining:3, total:3, extra:0, paidLeft:0}; /ap
fix_sketch: Two independent halves. (a) Make the recovery hook real: in redeemSession, when fallbackFan is present, non-empty and differs from md.fan, grant to fallbackFan and record both ids in meta.paid[sid] (`fan`, `claimedBy`). Restrict it to the confirm.mjs caller and to the first redemption only, so the webhook and the sweep still use md.fan — knowing the session id is proof enough of being the buyer, and it is the same bearer-token logic success_url already relies on. (b) Stop the client lying: in vote.html:589-591, celebrate off the balance that comes back from load(), not off d.granted, so a phone that did not actually gain credits says 'show Perry your receipt' instead of throwing confetti. Separately, an artist-side 'add N votes to this phone' action would give Perry a way out of every case in this whole family.

title: The Studio's Live tab shows a lifetime tip total in a row of tonight-only stats, and the unbounded array behind it is read on every single Studio tap
what_happens: stage.mjs:22 sums the entire meta.tips array with no show filter and stage.mjs:62 returns it as `tips.total`. studio.html:1067 renders it as the third of three headline stats on the Live tab, beside 'Votes now' and 'Voting · in room' — both of which are strictly about right now. Nothing resets meta.tips: newShow does not touch it, and _pay.mjs:26 pushes each tip without a showId, so it cannot be filtered by show even if someone wanted to. `recent` (stage.mjs:62, slice(-15)) mixes in tips from previous nights for the same reason. Separately, meta.paid and meta.tips are both unbounded while meta.gifts is capped at 500 (gift.mjs:36) — and INVARIANT 0l means stagePayload, which reads meta, is returned with EVERY /api/admin write.
failure_scenario: Perry is on stage at 10pm and glances at the Live tab between songs: 'Votes now 31 · Voting 12/40 · Tips $140.00'. Two of those three numbers are tonight; the third is every tip he has received since the app existed. He tells the bar owner he took $140 in tips tonight. Recent tips underneath shows a $20 with a note from a different venue three weeks ago, timestamped 'Aug 12'. At scale the same array is the per-write cost: after a year of gigs, meta_<aid> holds thousands of paid{} keys and tips[] entries, and every tap of Start / Pause / Add song / Toggle reads and re-serialises the whole document through a 40-try CAS.
evidence: Read the full chain: _pay.mjs:26 pushes {fan, amount, note, at} with no showId; grep for meta.tips shows no writer other than that push and no reset anywhere (`grep -rn '\.tips' netlify/functions/` returns only _lib.mjs defaults, _pay.mjs:26, stage.mjs:22,62 and _history.mjs's separate Stripe-derive
fix_sketch: Stamp the tip with its show: `m.tips.push({ fan, amount, note, at, showId: md.show || '' })` in _pay.mjs:26, then in stage.mjs sum only entries whose showId matches show.showId and label the stat 'Tips tonight' (studio.html:1067). Keep the lifetime figure in the Money tab where it belongs. Bound both arrays the way gifts already is — tips.slice(-500), and prune meta.paid entries older than ~120 days, keeping the marker long enough that no live Stripe session can be re-redeemed (sessions expire after 24h).

title: A failed /api/show leaves the voting page on the skeleton forever with no message, and an artist with no songs gets "Everything's in the queue above"
lenses: Scenario walk — one fan's night, 8pm to
what_happens: `load()` swallows every failure — a network error is caught and dropped (line 233), and a non-ok body is simply ignored (line 232 only acts `if(d.ok)`). `ST` stays null, `render()` is never called, and the grey skeleton written at line 221 stays on screen indefinitely; there is no error state and no retry control (artist.html has one, vote.html does not). They pull to refresh — the SW serves the page from cache, `load()` fails again, three grey rectangles. Nothing on screen says "no connection" or "try again"; the page just looks broken, which is precisely what INVARIANT 16 exists to prevent. The same permanent skeleton is what a 404 `unknown artist` produces. fix_sketch: Give `load()` a failure path: on a caught error or `!d.ok`, if `ST` is still null render a small "Can't reach the setlist — retrying" card with a Retry button (polling already retries, so the card only needs to say so); if `ST` exists, leave the last good render alone and show a quiet offline chip. title: The "New show" confirm claims it clears purchased votes; carryFans deliberately preserves them — the warning is wrong and steers the artist onto the broken path
what_happens: The dialog reads "Start a brand new show? Clears all votes, purchased votes and the played list." The code does the opposite for purchased votes: newShow calls `carryFans(aid, prevShow)`, which keeps `unspentPaid()` for every fan and only drops records with nothing owed. The comment above the call says so explicitly ("paid votes survive a reset"). The button is also the only real "new night" control and it is on the Settings tab, described as "reset everything", while the Live tab offers a friendly-looking "Start the show".
failure_scenario: Perry arrives for night two, wants a clean slate, opens Settings, reads "Clears all votes, PURCHASED votes", decides he does not want to rob the two people who bought packs last night, backs out, and taps "Start the show" on the Live tab instead — landing squarely in finding 2. He has been steered away from the correct control by a warning that is factually wrong.
evidence: Ran newShow with a fan holding extra=6 who had spent 1 free credit. Before: `f2 extra 6, votes ['bravo']`. After: `fan records surviving: ['f2'] {"f2":{"v":[],"ts":{},"extra":6,"gifted":0}}` — all 6 purchased votes intact, every other fan record deleted. Read carryFans/unspentPaid at _lib.mjs:398-41
fix_sketch: Change the copy to "Starts a fresh night. Clears tonight's votes, the played list and the queue. Votes people paid for carry over." Once finding 2 is fixed, demote this button further — the artist should not need it, because Start on a new night should do the right thing on its own.

title: A fan who paid cash for a song request that is declined after "New show" gets nothing back, and the Studio tells the artist it refunded them
lenses: Vote & credit accounting — every path th
what_happens: `createRequest` charges the request cost to `me.spent` (_requests.mjs:95). `unspentPaid` counts `spent` as consumed, so `carryFans()` on New show writes back `extra - spent` — and when that reaches 0 it deletes the fan record entirely (_lib.mjs:411). `resolveRequest` then refuses to refund a decline whose `row.showId` no longer matches the current show (_requests.mjs:153), which is correct as a mint guard but means nothing is returned. Meanwhile admin.mjs:562 reports `refunded: row.cost` unconditionally — it reads the row, not whether a refund actually happened — so the Studio confirms a refund that never occurred, and vote.html:401 shows the fan "Not tonight — votes refunded".
failure_scenario: Free credits are 0 (packs are the only way to vote). A fan buys the $3 pack and immediately spends all 3 on a song request. Perry is playing and doesn't get to the Requests tab. At the break he taps ↺ New show — `carryFans` sees `unspentPaid` = 0 and deletes the fan's record, destroying the 3 credits they paid $3 for. In the second set he finally opens the queue and taps Decline: the Studio says "3 refunded", the fan's page says "Not tonight — votes refunded", and the fan's balance is 0. They paid $3, got no song, and got no votes.
evidence: T15 (scratchpad/c5.mjs, real handlers): fanQ granted 3 with freeCredits=0, asks for a song → record `{extra:3, spent:3}`. `admin newShow` → record is `undefined` (deleted by carryFans). `admin askDecline` → response `refunded: 3`, fanQ's record still `undefined`. T9 is the same case with the record
fix_sketch: Two separate fixes. (a) Make the report honest: have `resolveRequest` return whether it actually refunded and use that at admin.mjs:562, so the Studio can say "declined — their credits had already refreshed" instead of claiming a refund. (b) Stop New show from silently eating an unanswered paid request: either treat pending requests as an outstanding liability in `unspentPaid` (don't count `spent` for rows still `pending`), or auto-decline-and-refund every pending request in the `newShow` handler before `carryFans` runs, which also stops last night's requests leaking into tonight's queue.

title: "Undo" on a played song hands the fan back credits they already spent while they keep the vote
lenses: Vote & credit accounting — every path th
what_happens: `costOf()` decides a vote's price purely from whether the song id is in `show.played` at read time. The `unplay` action (the "Undo" button beside each song in the Studio's played list) removes the id from `show.played` and touches nothing else. Every fan holding a replay vote on that song is instantly re-priced from `replayCost` down to 1 — they keep the vote and get the difference back as spendable credits. It is the mirror image of finding 2 and the same root cause: no price is stored with a vote.
failure_scenario: Perry starts "Hey Jude", then realises he mis-tapped and hits Undo on the played row to put it back in the pool. A fan who a minute earlier spent 5 credits (from a $7 pack) to hear it again keeps their vote on it AND gets 4 credits back — their pill jumps from 5/10 to 9/10 with no purchase. Across a room where a replay was popular, every replay voter is silently topped up. It is not fan-triggerable, so it is not an exploit, but it means the credit balance the room is looking at is not a ledger of anything.
evidence: T2 (scratchpad/c2.mjs, real handlers): fanA replay-votes 'alpha' at cost 5 with freeCredits=10 → `{"remaining":5,"used":5}`. `admin unplay song=alpha` → `{"remaining":9,"used":1}` and the fan record still reads `v:["alpha"]`. Four credits appeared from nothing while the vote was retained.
fix_sketch: The `me.c[song]` price stamp from finding 2 fixes this too: a vote keeps the price it was cast at, so `unplay` cannot re-price it. If you would rather `unplay` genuinely put the song back on equal terms, then have the `unplay` handler explicitly drop that song id from every fan shard's `v`/`ts` (a targeted `casDoc` sweep) so nobody keeps a vote at a price they didn't pay — but stamping the price is cheaper and matches how `play` already behaves.

lenses: Mid-show setlist changes — what the serv
what_happens: `votable()` requires `s.active !== false` before it considers `played`, so `toggleSong` on a played song removes it from the public `played` array (show.mjs:48-53) as well as from the pool. That is right per INVARIANT 0bd — but `costOf()` charged `replayCost` (default 5) for every vote sitting on it, and `creditsUsed()` keeps charging that after the song vanishes. The default `freeCredits` is 3, so a replay vote at cost 5 cannot be cast on free credits at all: every held replay vote is, by arithmetic, backed by a Stripe purchase or by an artist-raised free allowance. So this is the same strand as the documented setlist residual but at 5× the value and against money the fan actually paid. With `removeSong` instead of `toggleSong` it also becomes unrecoverable (finding 1).
failure_scenario: Perry played Wonderwall at 9:10. At 10:00 three people each spend 5 credits asking to hear it again — 15 credits of demand, and since 5 > 3 free, at least some of that was bought at $3 for 3 votes.
