Before hide: `/api/show` `played` = `[wonderwall cost=5 votes=3 mine=true]`, f1 `{remaining:1,total:6,used:5}`. After `toggleSong {song:'wond
fix_sketch: Fixed by finding 4's `stranded` array — a replay strand shows up in exactly the same place and is released by exactly the same tap, with no extra work. Separately worth considering: `toggleSong` on a song with `counts[id] > 0` could return a note ("3 people have votes on that — they'll get them back") so the artist knows what he just did, since he is the only person in the room who can see the tally.

title: The venue and artist token realms share one HMAC secret, so a pipe in an email address crosses the boundary
what_happens: Both realms sign with the same `authSecret()` and separate themselves only by a `v|` prefix inside the signed body, split on `|`. `validEmail` (`/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[a-z]{2,}$/`) permits `|` in the local part and `normEmail` does not strip it, so an artist account registered as `v|bar@duck.com` produces a token whose body is `v|bar@duck.com|<exp>|<rev>` — which `verifyVenueToken` parses as tag `v`, email `bar@duck.com`. Both registries start at `rev: 1`, so the rev check passes. Separately, `Number(exp) < Date.now()` is false when `exp` is NaN, so a misparsed body skips the expiry check entirely — that is what makes the shape work at all.
failure_scenario: An attacker signs up as an artist with the email `v|manager@theuglyduckling.com`. Their ordinary artist session token is then accepted by `verifyVenueToken()` as the OWNER of the Ugly Duckling's venue page: they can rewrite its address and opening hours, replace its photos, mark pitches, and read the room numbers of every act that plays there — the exact reach INVARIANT 0x says must be structurally impossible. Practical exploitation currently requires receiving the one-time code at that literal address, which Resend will probably refuse to deliver to, so this is a latent break rather than a live one — but the only thing standing between the two realms is a character class in a regex, which is not the structural separation the invariant claims.
evidence: scratchpad/probe5.mjs, real _auth/_venues modules. First confirmed the normal boundary holds: `venue token -> /api/stage (artist): 401` and `artist token -> /api/venueadmin: 401`. Then created a venue for `bar@duck.com` and an artist for `v|bar@duck.com`, signed an ordinary artist token with `signTo
fix_sketch: Three cheap, independent fixes, all worth doing: (1) reject `|` (and any non-RFC local-part character) in `normEmail` and `validEmail`; (2) derive a distinct key per realm — `createHmac('sha256', secret).update('realm:venue')` — so a token signed for one realm cannot verify in the other regardless of body shape; (3) fix the expiry check to `const t = Number(exp); if (!Number.isFinite(t) || t < Date.now()) return null;` in both `verifyToken` and `verifyVenueToken`, so a malformed body fails closed instead of being treated as never-expiring.

title: Venue statistics file every gig under a UTC calendar day, so every artist west of UTC has their Saturday night reported as Sunday
what_happens: _vstats.mjs:78-83 `dayOf(ms)` builds the date string from `getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate` on `s.endedAt || s.startedAt`. That value becomes `byNight[].date`, `busiest.date`, and `first`/`last`, which venue-studio.html:575 and :588 render as a weekday and day-month ('Busiest night: <artist> — Sunday 6 September'). The rest of the project is scrupulously timezone-aware — gigs are stored as wall clock plus IANA tz precisely so a residency does not shift at DST (INVARIANT 0f), and INVARIANT 0h says a set running past midnight belongs to the night it started — but this one derivation ignores all of it.
failure_scenario: A Nashville act plays The Ugly Duckling equivalent 8pm–11:30pm on Saturday 5 September. endedAt is 04:30Z on the 6th, so the venue's dashboard files the gig under Sunday 6 September and labels its busiest night 'Sunday'. A London act finishing at 1:15am BST gets the same treatment. The venue manager, who is the person Perry needs to convert, looks at a report saying his Saturday act played Sunday and concludes the numbers are made up. Invisible to Perry because Koh Phangan is UTC+7: the same gig there resolves to the correct date, so this bug cannot be seen from the only place it has ever been run.
evidence: Computed directly against the real dayOf implementation: Nashville Sat 2026-09-05 ending 23:30 CDT -> dayOf = '2026-09-06' (wrong); Koh Phangan same local times -> '2026-09-05' (right); London Sat ending 01:15 BST -> '2026-09-06' (wrong). Confirmed the value is rendered as a human date at public/ven
fix_sketch: Archive the show's own timezone. archiveShow already has the show record; carry the artist's gig tz (or the venue's) onto the history doc, and have dayOf format in that zone with an evening-rollover rule matching INVARIANT 0h — a night belongs to the day it started, so derive from `startedAt` in local time rather than `endedAt` in UTC.

title: play / playTop are not gated on status, and the Live tab keeps the play buttons after End — songs started after the archive can never reach history
what_happens: The archive for `status:'ended'` runs at admin.mjs:802-808 before the mutation, and nothing afterwards re-opens the document. Meanwhile `case 'play'` and `case 'playTop'` have no status check, and studio.html renders "Start top voted" and every queue row's "▶ Start" unconditionally — they are not hidden or disabled when the show is ended. Any play after the archive is appended to show.log and calls clearAllFanVotes, but the history doc is already frozen (finding 1), so it is invisible forever. The same window opens with two Studio devices even without an End-then-play sequence: the archive read and the show mutation are not serialised against each other.
failure_scenario: (a) Perry ends the show at 12:55am, the room thins out, someone shouts for one more and he plays it — tapping "Start top voted" out of muscle memory. It is accepted (200), logged with its 3 votes, and never appears in history; it also silently wipes every fan's votes. (b) Two devices: he ends the show on his phone while his laptop, already open on the Live tab, has "Start top voted" tapped in the same second. Charlie starts and plays; the archive records zero songs played and lists Charlie under "Wanted but never played".

(a) `status:'ended'`, then `A('playTop')` -> `200 ACCEPTED`; `show.log now: Alpha:2, Bravo:3 | status ended | nowPlaying bravo`; every fan record's `v` cleared; re-ending left `history detail STILL: Alpha` against `index songsPlayed 2`. (b) `Promise.all([A('status',{status:'ended'}), A('pl
fix_sketch: Refuse play/playTop with a 409 when `show.status === 'ended'`, and hide/disable those buttons on the Live tab in the ended state (the tab already branches on `s.status!=='live'` for the Start/End button). With finding 1's unsealed-overwrite in place, a legitimate resume would then re-snapshot correctly rather than losing the song.

title: Double-tapping the start controls: a second 'Start top voted' starts the alphabetically-first song with zero votes; a second '▶ Start' on the current song duplicates it in history
what_happens: `playTop` refuses only when the pool is EMPTY (admin.mjs:903) — it never checks that anything has votes. Since the previous start already ran `clearAllFanVotes` (admin.mjs:1053), the second call sees an all-zero tally, `rankSongs` falls through to the title tie-break, and the alphabetically-first eligible song is started and written into `show.log` as a played round with `votes: 0`. Separately, `play` on the song that is already `nowPlaying` is not rejected: admin.mjs:884 guards only the `push` of the previous nowPlaying, so the handler still calls `logPlay` (a duplicate row) and still sets `resetVotes = true`, destroying the round that has accumulated since. The client `WRITING` lock (studio.html:741) is per-tab and cannot stop either case across two devices or a stale render.
failure_scenario: 10:40pm, noisy bar, Perry taps 'Start top voted'. The Netlify cold start takes 1.2s, the busy overlay is up, he taps again through it on his iPad which is still showing the pre-tap render. MySet starts 'Alpha' — a song nobody voted for, alphabetically first — and the 14 votes the room cast in the last two minutes are wiped. The history row for that round reads 'Alpha · 0 votes'. Variant with '▶ Start': the iPad's stale queue still lists the song that is currently playing; one tap logs it twice and wipes the new round. MEASURED: with the room holding Zulu 3 / Yankee 2, tap 1 started Zulu, tap 2 started Alpha (0 votes) instead of Yankee.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle2.mjs: `tap 1 -> zulu | log ['zulu:3']`, `tap 2 -> alpha | log ['zulu:3','alpha:0']` — 'the room voted for YANKEE next; second tap started: alpha'. Same script, section C: `A('play',{song:'zulu'})` issued twice produced `log ['zulu:2v/4rv','zulu:0v/2rv']` and left every fan's `v:
fix_sketch: In `playTop`, refuse with 409 when the top of the pool has zero votes and a song was started in the last N seconds — or simply require `counts[pool[0].id] > 0` and return a friendly 'Nobody has voted yet — pick one from the queue'. In `play`, return early (no `logPlay`, no `resetVotes`) when `body.song === show.nowPlaying`. Both are two-line server-side guards that do not depend on the client lock.

title: `unplay` mints credits: a fan who spent replayCost on a 'play it again' gets the difference refunded while keeping the vote
what_happens: `creditsUsed` is not a stored balance — it is recomputed on every read by summing `costOf(songId, show)` over the fan's current votes, and `costOf` answers 5 or 1 purely from whether the id is in `show.played` at that instant. `unplay` (admin.mjs:998) removes the id from `played[]` without touching any fan record, so every standing replay vote on that song is retroactively repriced from `replayCost` down to 1 and the fan is handed the difference back.
failure_scenario: Perry starts 'Wonderwall' by mistake at 9:15, realises, and taps 'Undo' in the Played list to put it back in the queue — exactly the recovery the button exists for. In the eight minutes it sat in `played[]`, six fans each spent 5 credits asking to hear it again. All six instantly get 4 credits back and keep their vote. Two of them had bought a $3 pack precisely because they were out; they now have 4 free votes each to spend elsewhere. Nothing tells anyone this happened. At 1000 artists this is a repeatable way for a room to be handed credits the artist did not intend to give.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle4.mjs, section F2: fan `z1` with 20 credits casts a replay vote on 'zulu' (`cost: 5`) → `total 20 used 5 remaining 15`. Artist then runs `unplay {song:'zulu'}` → `total 20 used 1 remaining 19 -> vote still held: ['zulu']`. Four credits appeared from nowhere.
fix_sketch: Either (a) make `unplay` drop every fan vote on that song across the shards (it goes back in the queue as an unvoted song, which matches the artist's intent), or (b) record the cost actually charged on the fan record at cast time (`me.paidFor[songId] = cost`) and have `creditsUsed` prefer that over recomputing from `played[]`. Option (a) is a handful of lines and reuses the existing shard-mutation pattern.

title: The voting page says "Connection hiccup — retrying" and does not retry
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: When the vote POST throws, the catch at vote.html:247 shows `toast('Connection hiccup — retrying')`. Line 248 then does `busy.delete(id); load();` — a plain refetch of server state, which reverts the optimistic vote that was applied at lines 238-240. There is no queue, no backoff, no second attempt: the word 'retrying' describes behaviour that does not exist. There is no timeout on the request either, so on a stalled connection the fan sits with a voted-looking button until the browser gives up.
failure_scenario: A fan on the far side of a beach bar taps Zombie. The POST never leaves the phone. The toast says 'Connection hiccup — retrying', the credit count and the button briefly show the vote, then `load()` quietly puts everything back. Nothing retries. The fan believes the app is working on it, waits, and their vote is simply gone — the one thing they came to the page to do. At 1000 artists this is a steady trickle of 'I voted and it didn't count' with no server-side trace, because a request that never arrived leaves nothing to look at.
evidence: Read vote.html:236-249 line by line: the catch body is a single `toast(...)` call and the only subsequent statement is `busy.delete(id); load();`. Grepped the file for retry/attempt/backoff logic around the vote path — none. Confirmed by contrast that the payment path DOES have a real retry (`pendin
fix_sketch: Either make the words true or change them. Truthful is better: keep the failed (fan, song, intent) in memory, retry it once or twice with a short backoff, and only then revert and say 'Couldn't save that vote — tap again'. Add an AbortController with ~8s so a stalled request fails fast rather than hanging the button.

title: Returning from Stripe on flaky wifi lands on the offline page, because the cached page is keyed with the ?paid= query string
lenses: Bar wifi, locked phones, and the service
what_happens: `caches.put(req, …)` and `caches.match(req)` both key on the full URL including the query string (Cache API `ignoreSearch` defaults to false). Stripe returns the buyer to `…/vote?paid=cs_live_<id>`, which has never been cached and never matches the cached bare URL, so the offline branch skips straight past `caches.match(req)` to `caches.match('/')` and then to the hardcoded 'No connection' page — even though a perfectly good copy of that same page is in the cache one query string away. A side effect: every distinct return URL adds its own cache entry, so live Stripe session ids accumulate in Cache Storage indefinitely (the runtime cache is only ever cleared by bumping CACHE).
failure_scenario: A fan buys the $7 nine-vote pack. Stripe charges the card and redirects back to myset.vip/perryidyll/vote?paid=cs_live_a1b2. At that instant the bar's wifi is saturated by the same forty phones. They get a bare white page reading 'No connection — MySet needs the internet for the live bits.' immediately after being charged. The money is safe (the webhook and the pending-session retry in localStorage both cover it, INVARIANT 5c), but the buyer's experience is 'I paid and the app broke', which is when someone taps buy a second time or goes looking for Perry.
evidence: swsim.mjs with the network throwing: `offline, same URL -> FRESH:https://myset.vip/perryidyll/vote | status 200` (cache hit) versus `offline, ?paid=... -> <!doctype html><meta name=viewport conte | status 503` (cache miss, offline page) — same page, same cache, different key. Also traced the recover
fix_sketch: In the navigate branch's catch, fall back with `caches.match(req, { ignoreSearch: true })` before trying '/' — the query string is never what identifies the page here. Optionally strip the query before `caches.put` too, which also stops session ids accumulating in Cache Storage.

title: "Tonight / Tomorrow" is computed three times — once server-side in the gig's timezone and twice client-side in the viewer's — so the homepage and the venue page label the same gig differently
what_happens: events.mjs:126-131 `dayLabel(date, today)` computes Tonight/Tomorrow/weekday with `today = localDate(now, tz0)` — the GIG's IANA zone (events.mjs:90-91), which is the whole point of _time.mjs and INVARIANT 0f/0h. index.html renders that server label (index.html:372). But artist.html:205-211 and venue.html:206-211 each define their own `whenWord(date)` on top of `todayISO()` (artist.html:203, venue.html:204), which is `new Date()` in the VIEWER's device timezone. Three implementations of one rule, and the two client copies are the ones that ignore the zone the gig is actually in. artist.html:356 goes further and always prints `dowName(g.date)` in the gig list, so the same page's next-up card (artist.html:340, whenWord) and its list rows (dowName) can describe the same night two ways.
failure_scenario: A tourist on Koh Phangan has not changed their phone off Europe/London. It is 03:10 on 2 September in Thailand; Perry plays the Ugly Duckling at 20:00 on 2 September (Asia/Bangkok). They open myset.vip, pick Thailand → Koh Phangan: the server's tz0 is Asia/Bangkok, today is 2026-09-02, and the header reads "Tonight – 2 September". They tap through to the venue page for the same gig: venue.html's todayISO() returns 2026-09-01 (it is still 21:10 in London), so whenWord returns "Tomorrow" and the row reads "Tomorrow · 8:00pm". Same gig, two pages, one tap apart, opposite answers about which night to turn up. The other direction bites the artist: for a set that starts 22:00 and ends 01:00, at 00:30 local the server still says "Tonight" and marks it live (INVARIANT 0h), while artist.html's whenWord has rolled over to the next day and calls it something else — next to a row the server has flagged `g.live`, rendering "On now" beside the wrong day word.
evidence: Code trace across three files, plus the grep that establishes there are exactly three: `dayLabel` at events.mjs:126 is the only server implementation and index.html consumes `day.label` (index.html:372) without recomputing; `whenWord` is defined independently at artist.html:205 and venue.html:206 an
fix_sketch: The server already knows the answer and already sends `tz` on every occurrence. Add `label` to `shape()` in events.mjs:110-117 (it is one line: `label: dayLabel(o.date, localDate(Date.now(), o.tz))`), then delete whenWord/todayISO from artist.html and venue.html and render `g.label`. That collapses three implementations to one and puts it on the side that knows the zone — the same move INVARIANT 0e made for occurrence expansion. While there: artist.html:340 and :356 should use the same field so one page stops contradicting itself.

title: The network hash is only stamped from /api/show?in=1 while live — /api/vote never records one, so the `nets` signal is blank for exactly the traffic worth watching
what_happens: `markPresence(aid, fanId, show, req)` is the only writer of `f.ipH`, and it is called from exactly one place — `show.mjs:17`, gated on `in=1` AND `fanId` AND `show.status === 'live'`. `vote.mjs` performs a `mutateFan` write on every cast but never touches `ipH`. So a fan record created purely through the vote endpoint has no network hash at all, and `roomCounts()`'s `nets` set (`_lib.mjs:532`, `if (f.ipH) nets.add(f.ipH)`) simply skips it. The defence described in INVARIANT 0ae covers only the polling path, not the writing path.
failure_scenario: The flood in Finding 2 produced `room = 2040, nets = 0` — two thousand fabricated voters and the network counter did not move at all, because none of them ever called /api/show. Even after Finding 3 is fixed and Perry can see 'phones · networks', a scripted or curl-driven attack stays completely invisible in that display, and so does anyone who bookmarks the vote POST. The signal only sees the honest users it was not built for.
evidence: Read: markPresence has exactly one call site (grep for `markPresence` across netlify/functions returns _lib.mjs:540 definition and show.mjs:2,17 import+call). vote.mjs's mutateFan callback (vote.mjs:31-48) sets only `ts`, `v` — no `ipH`. Measured: after 2000 votes cast via /api/vote with no /api/sho
fix_sketch: Set `me.ipH ||= roomHash(aid, clientIp(req))` inside the existing mutateFan callback in vote.mjs — the write is already happening, so this costs no extra blob operation. Pass `req` through (it is already in scope). Use `||=` not `=` so a device that rotates networks mid-gig keeps its first stamp and cannot inflate `nets` in the other direction. INVARIANT 0af is unaffected: still no raw IP stored, still artist-scoped hash, and the once-per-device property is preserved by `||=`.

title: show.played is never reconciled against the library, so a re-added song comes back "already played" at 5 credits and vanishes from the up-next list
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: normShow repairs show.listSongs against the current library on every read (_lib.mjs:322) but does nothing to show.played. Song ids are deterministic slugs of the title (admin.mjs:959), so removing a song and re-adding it — or clearing and re-importing the starter setlist — regenerates the identical id, which is still sitting in show.played. costOf (_lib.mjs:487) therefore charges replayCost (5 by default) for a song the room has never heard, show.mjs:37 excludes it from the up-next pool, and playTop will not pick it unless it is already holding replay votes (admin.mjs:903).
failure_scenario: Mid-set Perry notices "Wagon Wheel" is credited to the wrong artist. He deletes it and re-adds it with the right one — two taps, exactly what the Studio is for. The song had been played at 21:00. It now reappears on every phone in the room in the "already played" section at 5 credits instead of 1, and never in "Up next". A fan with 3 free credits cannot vote for it at all. The same happens in one tap via Clear setlist → Starter setlist, which regenerates the whole covers pack with every previously-played title already flagged. Perry has no idea why the room stopped voting for it; the only cure is the `unplay` action, which he would have to know to look for.
evidence: Probe .../scratchpad/probe/p4_played.mjs and p5_showcas.mjs, real handlers. p4: after deleting and re-adding Wagon Wheel — `re-added with id: wagon-wheel` / `in the "up next" pool?: false` / `sitting in "already played": true at cost 5` / a fan voting is charged `{"voted":true,"cost":5,"remaining":1
fix_sketch: One line in normShow beside the listSongs repair: `show.played = show.played.filter((id) => ids.has(id))` — this also cleans up dangling ids from deleted songs, which currently sit in stagePayload's `played` array forever. That does not by itself fix the re-add case (the id is back in the library), so also clear the id from `played` in removeSong (`show.played = show.played.filter(p => p !== body.song)`) and from clearSetlist (`show.played = []`), which is what the artist means by those actions anyway.

title: learnDone is two unguarded writes and non-idempotent, so "Learned it" from two Studio surfaces duplicates the song — the exact failure its own comment claims to prevent
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: The comment at admin.mjs:509-510 says "one action, because doing it in two leaves a duplicate if the second fails" — but the implementation is two separate document writes: mutateShow appends the song (:520-534), then mutateLearn removes the row (:536). There is no compensation and the show write deliberately mints a suffixed id on a slug collision (:523), so re-running it does NOT converge — unlike askAccept, which returns the existing id (:581-588). Two concurrent requests, or a failure of the second write followed by the artist retrying, both produce two library rows with the same title.
failure_scenario: Perry has the Studio open on his phone on stage and on his laptop at the merch table. He taps "Learned it" on Stick Season from the phone; the laptop's list is a few seconds stale so he taps it there too. Both requests succeed. The library now holds `stick-season` and `stick-season-mi4`, both titled "Stick Season". Every phone in the room sees the song twice; the audience's votes split across the two rows, so a song five people wanted shows as 3 and 2 and loses to something with 4. Nothing in the Studio explains it.
evidence: Probe .../scratchpad/probe/p10_race.mjs, real admin.mjs, no storage failure at all — `await Promise.all([A('learnDone',{id}), A('learnDone',{id})])` gives `200 stick-season | 200 stick-season-mi4` and `library: ['stick-season','stick-season-mi4']`. p9_learn.mjs shows the failure-and-retry variant: w
fix_sketch: Make the show half idempotent the way askAccept already is: if a song with the slug id already exists, adopt it (return its id, flip active back on if needed) instead of minting a suffix — a to-learn row is a specific song, not a new one. Then remove the learn row inside the same handler and, if that write fails, return a note rather than a 500 so the artist knows to re-check rather than re-tap. Reserve the suffixing behaviour for addSong, where two different songs genuinely can share a slug.

title: 'New show' from the Settings tab silently puts the artist LIVE, and its confirm dialog states the opposite of what happens to purchased votes
what_happens: The `newShow` case sets `show.status = 'live'` unconditionally (admin.mjs:1022) regardless of what the status was. The button that triggers it lives on the Settings tab and is labelled '↺ New show (reset everything)' with the dialog 'Start a brand new show? Clears all votes, purchased votes and the played list.' Two things are wrong: it never says it will announce the artist as live, and it claims purchased votes are cleared when admin.mjs:1052 calls `carryFans` — which deliberately PRESERVES them (INVARIANT 5c). The artist is being told the opposite of the rule the code is built around.
failure_scenario: Perry gets to the bar at 4pm to set up, opens Settings, taps 'New show (reset everything)' to clear last night's played list. Nothing on that tab changes, so he assumes it worked and goes to soundcheck. From that moment `/api/show` returns `status:'live'`, his artist page at myset.vip/perryidyll renders the red 'Live now — vote the setlist' pill (artist.html:301), and anyone who follows the link four hours early lands on an active voting page for a gig that has not started. Separately, a fan who bought $7 of votes on Tuesday still has them on Wednesday — correct behaviour that the dialog promised would not happen, so Perry can never tell a fan what they actually have.
evidence: scratchpad/lifecycle4.mjs: `status before New show: pre` → `status after New show: live`, and `/api/show status seen by artist page + city feed: live`. Same script: a fan with `extra: 9` still had `extra: 9` after `newShow`, contradicting the dialog text at studio.html:1542.
fix_sketch: Have `newShow` preserve the existing status (or set `'pre'`) and let the Live tab's 'Start the show' be the only thing that goes live — that is what INVARIANT 0o says the button is for. Rewrite the dialog: 'Start a brand new show? Clears tonight's votes and played list. Votes people paid for are kept.'

title: If the first fetch hangs, the page never starts polling and never recovers
what_happens: Boot is a single serial await chain: `await load(); await handleReturn(); LASTSIG=signature(); schedule(); addEventListener('visibilitychange',…); addEventListener('pointerdown',wakeUp,…)`. Everything that makes the page live — the poll timer and both wake-up listeners — is downstream of two awaited fetches. No fetch in the file has an `AbortController` or any timeout (grep confirms: zero occurrences of AbortController/AbortSignal/timeout). A rejected fetch is fine, because the empty catches let the chain continue; a fetch that *hangs* is not, because the browser will not abandon a stalled connection for tens of seconds to minutes. During that time the page is the grey skeleton at 221-226 with no text, no timer, and no listeners, and it can only be fixed by a manual reload.
failure_scenario: A fan scans the table QR while their phone is still negotiating the venue wifi, or while a captive portal is accepting the TCP connection but not answering. The page loads from cache, paints the skeleton, and stops — no message, no spinner text, no retry. To them MySet is simply broken, and there is nothing on screen that suggests reloading. The money version is worse: they come back from Stripe to `/perryidyll/vote?paid=cs_…`, `handleReturn()` toasts "Confirming payment…" and awaits `/api/confirm` (585). If that request hangs, `schedule()` at 650 never runs — the page sits on "Confirming payment…" over a skeleton forever, having just taken their $7. (The payment itself is safe under INVARIANT 5c — the webhook grants it — but the buyer's experience is a frozen page immediately after paying, which is precisely the moment they are watching.)
evidence: Direct trace of 647-653: `schedule()` at 650 and both `addEventListener` calls at 651-652 are lexically after `await load()` at 648 and `await handleReturn()` on the same line, so nothing in the loop is armed until both settle. `grep -n "AbortController\|AbortSignal\|timeout" public/vote.html` retur
fix_sketch: Two lines of insurance. Arm the loop first: call `schedule()` and attach the listeners *before* awaiting anything, so the page is self-healing no matter what the first request does. And give every fetch a deadline — a small `withTimeout(fetch(...), 8000)` helper using `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` turns a hang into a rejection the existing catches already handle correctly. Optionally, if the first load has not produced a render within ~6s, replace the skeleton with "Trouble reaching the setlist — retrying", which is what INVARIANT 16 is asking for.

title: delGig checks the WRITING lock and never takes it
lenses: public/studio.html — the Studio as the a
what_happens: `async function delGig(id){ if(WRITING)return; if(!confirm(...))return; const d=await api(...) …}` — the guard is read but `WRITING=true` is never assigned, and there is no try/finally. Every other taker in the file (act 741-742, runAutoTag 666, saveGig2 937, skipGig 964, hideGig 977 after its confirm, askDo 1653, saveSongSheet 1864) sets it. This is precisely the class of omission INVARIANT 0k exists to prevent, in the very feature ("I tapped Add four times and got four gigs") that created the lock.
failure_scenario: Perry deletes a repeating residency from the gig sheet. The eventDelete call is slow. Because the lock was never taken, the app is not actually locked: a stray tap elsewhere in the sheet, or a second tap on "Delete this gig and its whole run" once the confirm re-appears, fires a second concurrent write against _events while the first is still in flight. Consequences here are mild (eventDelete on a missing id is a no-op and the confirm slows a human down), but the guard reads as protection that does not exist, and the next person to copy this function onto something non-idempotent inherits the hole.
evidence: `grep -n "if(WRITING)return" public/studio.html` → lines 666, 741, 937, 957, 964, 977, 1653, 1864. Line 957 (delGig) is the only one not followed by `WRITING=true` on the same line or immediately after a confirm().
fix_sketch: `if(WRITING)return; if(!confirm(...))return; WRITING=true; try{ … } finally { WRITING=false; }` — matching hideGig at 977-986, which already gets the ordering right (check, confirm, then take).

title: Declining a request reports "3 credits refunded" when the refund write failed, and the status marker blocks any retry
lenses: Storage, CAS and data integrity under re
what_happens: resolveRequest flips the row to 'declined' in the requests document, then calls `refund(...).catch(() => {})` (_requests.mjs:154). The swallowed failure is never surfaced: admin.mjs:562 returns `{ ok: true, refunded: row.cost }` computed from the row, not from anything that happened to the fan record. And because the row is now 'declined', a second attempt hits `if (!r || r.status === status) return false` (:146) and answers 409 "That one has already been dealt with" — the same idempotency-marker-blocks-recovery shape as the payment bug, one document over. INVARIANT 0ac's promise ("Declining a request refunds exactly once") holds for double-declines but not for a refund that never ran.
failure_scenario: A fan spends 3 of her 5 credits asking for a song. Perry can't play it and taps Decline. The Studio says "3 credits back", her page still shows 2 remaining, and she cannot vote for the two songs she wanted. Perry taps Decline again to fix it and gets "That one has already been dealt with". Her only recourse is for Perry to give the whole room fresh credits, which he will not know to do.
evidence: Probe .../scratchpad/probe/p8_refund.mjs, real admin.mjs + request.mjs + show.mjs with fan-shard writes forced to fail only during the decline. Output: `fan credits remaining : 2 (spent 3)` → `artist declines. API says {"ok":true,"refunded":3}` → `fan spent after "refund": 3 (was 3)` → `fan credits
fix_sketch: Refund before flipping the status (the mirror of createRequest's take-first rule, which is correct because the risk runs the other way), or carry a `refundedAt` field on the row: set the status, attempt the refund with a read-back verify, and only stamp `refundedAt` on success. resolveRequest's guard becomes `r.status === status && r.refundedAt` so a decline whose refund failed stays retryable, and admin.mjs reports `refunded` from the actual result rather than from row.cost.

title: Third accidental collision with app.css's .go, on the newest page that links it
what_happens: app.css:147-151 defines `.go` as the checkout slab: full-width gradient, `box-shadow: var(--sh-accent)`, a spring transition and a `:active` scale. venue.html:28 links app.css and then venue.html:166-168 redefines `.go` with a flat `background: var(--accent)` and its own padding — but never resets `box-shadow` or `transition`, so the venue page's buttons still carry the accent glow and the scale-on-press from the checkout button. INVARIANT 0an records that `.go` has been reached for by accident twice already and asks for a one-line audit before naming a class on any page that links app.css; that audit was evidently not run on venue.html.
failure_scenario: Cosmetic rather than functional: the venue page's primary buttons render with a coloured drop shadow the design did not ask for, and any future change to app.css's `.go` (a new border, a different radius on the shadow) silently changes venue.html too. It is the same latent coupling that produced the two documented incidents.
evidence: Mechanical intersection of class names defined inside each page's <style> block against class names in app.css. venue.html re-defines 13 shared names: bg, card, dot, empty, fine, go, grab, inp, lede, on, sheet, spin, toast. Cascade order confirmed: <link href='/app.css'> at venue.html:28 precedes <s
fix_sketch: Run the 0an audit as a committed script rather than a remembered habit — the intersection above is six lines of python and could sit in test/structure.mjs, failing the build on any new collision. Then either namespace venue.html's button (.vgo) or make its .go a complete override that also zeroes box-shadow and transition.
